description: ADR-0016 §1/§6 step 2. The tl sync command's always-runs local leg: read refs/tl/log, union this replica's own segment into it (CAS update-ref), and materialize the OTHER replicas' segments into .tl/log/ via atomic rename (never the own segment). No remote, no auth, no push-rejection/no-upstream — that is the remote leg (step 3) which this blocks. Delivers worktree-per-agent same-machine sharing over the shared common-.git ref.
title: Sync: the local-first worktree leg — tl sync reconciles against refs/tl/log (publish own segment + absorb siblings into .tl/log/)

description: ADR-0016 §3. Before a read folds .tl/log/, do an O(1) compare of refs/tl/log's OID against a last-materialized OID marker in .tl/local/; if it moved, incrementally materialize the changed foreign segments (reusing Tl/Sync/Local.writeForeignSegment) and record the new OID, then fold. Unchanged → skip (the common case, no git on the hot read path). Read-only FS → skip the refresh, fold what's there. Makes cross-worktree visibility live without remembering to sync.
title: Sync: read-time ref-OID refresh (ADR-0016 §3) — reads absorb a sibling's published changes without an explicit tl sync

description: Review-found boundary (ADR-0016 §3): the ref-mark keys off the ref OID, so if a gitignored foreign cache file under .tl/log/ is externally deleted/truncated while the ref stays put, the matching marker pins reads to the (now-incomplete) on-disk content until the ref next moves. tl sync re-materializes unconditionally; add a doctor check that compares the marker's ref tree against the on-disk segments and warns on a mismatch (a re-sync fixes it). Low priority — .tl/ is tl-managed and not meant to be hand-edited.
title: doctor: reconcile the read-refresh ref-mark against on-disk segments

description: Now that the local leg + read-refresh fold foreign segments routinely, a future-dated foreign HLC can win LWW and inflate the absent-clock reseed (toward 48-bit saturation). Pin a skew window W (~1h) in ADR-0007; at fold time, a FOREIGN op whose physical ms > now+W is deferred (excluded from the fold AND from maxHlc, disclosed) until wall-clock catches up — convergence-safe (eventual), never clamp (non-deterministic). Own segment exempt. doctor warns on deferred/near-bound clocks.
title: HLC skew-window: defer too-future foreign ops at fold time + doctor surfacing (ADR-0007)

description:
Lift the ADR-0007 skew-window safety argument from prose to a Lean theorem (CLAUDE.md principle 1: a provable property must be proved, not just tested). Factor the inlined fold-time check into a PURE predicate withinSkew (hlc now : Nat) : Bool := hlc/2^16 ≤ now + skewWindowMs, then prove:
  (1) withinSkew_mono — withinSkew hlc t → t ≤ t' → withinSkew hlc t' (once admitted, never re-deferred). ~3 lines: Nat.le_trans + Nat.add_le_add_right, no omega/decide.
  (2) eventual-full-admission — for now ≥ maxPhysical(ops), the filter is the identity (deferred set empty in the limit).
  (3) convergence corollary — compose with the existing kernel theorem fold_eq_of_mem_iff (replicas with the same op SET materialize identical state): two replicas past the threshold fold the identical admitted set ⇒ identical state. No re-proof of convergence; the filter just preserves the precondition.

Payoff/framing to capture: SAFETY (convergence) is independent of clock accuracy; only TIMELINESS depends on it — even a wildly-wrong clock cannot break convergence, monotonicity guarantees each replica converges as its clock advances. Add a one-line note to overview.md Trusted recording that the skew window's timeliness (not its convergence) rests on the system-clock carried assumption.

Location: put the pure predicate + lemmas in Tl/Clock (it is a pure HLC-time property, kernel-adjacent), and have Tl/Store/Materialize import it, so the shell file stays proof-free by convention. The boundary (exactly now+W, > vs ≥) stays a TEST concern — monotonicity holds for either boundary, so the theorem can't catch an off-by-one. #print axioms clean; no new axiom.
title: Prove skew-window convergence-safety: admission monotone in now ⇒ deferral is eventual (not permanent divergence)

description: Found by use: with W=24h and doctor's nearBound = 90% of W (21.6h), a 9h clock misconfiguration (e.g. a TZ-as-UTC machine) is FOLDED (within 24h, correctly not hidden) but NOT warned — silent. Deferral (hide) should be generous, but warning (flag, fix your clock) should be sensitive. Introduce skewWarnMs (~1h) distinct from skewWindowMs (24h): doctor warns if any op is deferred OR the max clock lead exceeds skewWarnMs. Three tiers: ≤1h normal (no warn, folded); 1h–24h folded BUT warned (notable misconfig); >24h deferred + warned.
title: doctor: warn on a notably-ahead clock even when its ops are folded (decouple warn threshold from the deferral window)

description: ADR-0001 §5 and ADR-0011 document claim flags that usage-error today: --verify re-checks ready against the freshest reachable state (fetch / local leg first; warn-and-degrade with no upstream) before writing, and --sync publishes the ref around the take (fetch, claim, push). The built claim already refuses non-ready items (not-claimable) against last-materialized local state; missing are the fetch-before-preflight and the atomic publish-around-claim. Also the designed remedy for directed claims by id against a stale view.
title: claim --verify / --sync: freshness preflight + publish-around-claim (ADR-0001 §5)

description: ADR-0011 §2: once sharing lands (the remote leg is built), doctor owns the authoritative sync posture — upstream, ahead, behind, lastSync, or a no-upstream marker. Current doctor has only local rows (replica / clock / log / graph / stale claims / clock skew), and nothing records lastSync anywhere yet. Needs a read-only ahead/behind computation against the configured remote, no push; the posture stays a pure diagnostic (ADR-0016: doctor does not refresh).
title: doctor: sync posture row — upstream / ahead / behind / lastSync (ADR-0011 §2)

description: ADR-0011 §2 pins a one-line advisory on ready when the local view is behind upstream (view may be stale — N behind; run tl sync), in human output and as a --json field. Shares the ahead/behind plumbing with the doctor posture row.
title: ready: behind-upstream staleness advisory (ADR-0011 §2)

description: refreshFromRef returns a RefreshOutcome whose degraded field carries the reason for callers that want to surface it — and loadView discards it, so a worktree whose refresh persistently fails (git missing from PATH, read-only FS) silently serves stale views: no note, no JSON field, no doctor row. Surface it like the other read notes (ADR-0008 loud-not-silent), taking care a racing-refresher degrade does not present as a false alarm.
title: reads: disclose a degraded read-refresh as a note and --json field

description: ADR-0016 §3 deliberately excludes the locked write path from read-time refresh, so a direct write by id from a stale worktree (claim/close/update/dep on a task that exists only on the shared ref) fails not-found until any read runs; auto-sync (ADR-0021) does not cover it — its hook fires after transact. Decide: a pre-transact absorb (the same O(1) ref-mark check reads use), claim --verify only, or pin the read-first contract in the docs.
title: Decide: write-path freshness — absorb the shared ref before write guards

description: readRefAt accepts any .jsonl tree entry name from refs/tl/log and absorbForeign materializes it into .tl/log/ unvalidated, while enumerateSegments refuses non-canonical names on every read — junk in the ref becomes a permanently flagged on-disk file with no cleanup path. Locally produced names are always canonical, so a Replica.valid filter in readRefAt drops only junk, stops it propagating through unions, and is defense-in-depth for crafted tree entry names (git mktree currently rejects slash-bearing names upstream of this).
title: sync absorb: validate ref-borne segment names with Replica.valid

description: After a remote leg that ran, cmdSync runs a second syncLocal to materialize what the fetch added and discards the result: local.absorbed in --json and the human absorbed-N-siblings line reflect only the first leg, so a sync that pulls a new replica from the remote reports absorbed: []. Fold the second-leg absorb into the report, and decide how an error there presents given the push already happened.
title: sync: report the post-remote second local leg (absorbed-from-remote)

description: ADR-0001 §6 says sync re-snapshots the own segment under the mutation lock immediately before each push attempt; the landed remote leg pushes the union of the local ref and the fetched remote without re-reading the own on-disk segment (nothing is lost — ops appended mid-sync ride the next sync). Implement the re-snapshot or amend the ADR to the landed form.
title: Decide: ADR-0001 §6 push-time own-segment re-snapshot — implement or amend

description: cmdClaim computes won/superseded for the --json data but the human line is unconditionally Claimed-as; cmdClose already discloses supersession. Reachable when a folded foreign op outstamps the fresh claim inside the skew window. Align the human path with close.
title: claim: disclose a superseded outcome in human output (parity with close)

description: label add refuses a trimAscii-empty label as a usage error; label remove accepts the same input and acks noop with exit 0. Align remove with add and cover the branch with a test — the empty-remove branch is currently untested (the shell coverage mandate).
title: label remove: reject an empty or whitespace label like label add

description: The stats stored-status row paints the open count with the ready display state (green), while the true ready count on the derived row renders bold — so green (workable, ADR-0017 §7) marks a count that includes blocked and deferred items, and the genuine ready count loses its color. Swap: neutral open, green ready.
title: stats: green marks the ready count, not the stored open count (ADR-0017 §7)

description: ADR-0003 §3 and ADR-0020 pin close --cascade (cancelling an epic cascades one close op per open child) with its JSON echo; vision lists the flag. The grammar does not accept it — usage-error today.
title: Implement close --cascade (ADR-0003 §3, ADR-0020 echo)

description: ADR-0011 presents list --stale, list --deferred and tl unblocks present-tense as part of the read surface; none exist in the grammar, so the agent-facing contract over-promises. These are pure read facets over already-materialized state (deferred display exists; the defer/undefer setters are tracked separately).
title: Implement read facets: list --stale, list --deferred, tl unblocks (ADR-0011)

description: Switch effectiveStatus from fuel-bounded descent (effStatusAux with present-issue-count fuel) to the memoized shape: visiting — the current recursion path — detects a parent cycle at the exact node (a global visited set would mistake shared DAG children for cycles), and memo caches completed statuses so each node is evaluated once per query; the fuel form can re-evaluate shared descendants combinatorially on diamond-shaped parent DAGs. Semantics unchanged: manual Cancelled precedence, cycle-trapped epics fall back conservatively (never Done), dangling children inert. Proof obligations: totality by well-founded recursion on the unvisited measure; re-prove acyclic exactness (effectiveStatus_epic) and the never-Done cycle guarantee over the new shape; bridge the efficient form to the spec (ADR-0003 §3 amendment).
title: Rollup: switch effectiveStatus to memoized visiting+memo recursion
Dep utilities: dep tree / dep path / dep critical commands
Dep utilities: dep tree / dep path / dep critical commands

description: In human list/ready/tree rows (and other one-line renders), shorten each id to its shortest unambiguous prefix over the present issue set — like git short hashes — with a sensible floor (e.g. tl- plus 4-5 chars), falling back to longer prefixes on collision. Input-side prefix resolution already exists (any unambiguous tl- prefix resolves, ambiguous-id lists candidates), so every rendered short id is directly usable as a command argument. Human display only: --json keeps full ids (the ADR-0020 forever-contract; agents and scripts must never depend on prefix length, which can grow as issues are added). Show/why detail views should keep the full id at least once. ADR-0017 governs the human output surface; the id scheme is ADR-0018.
title: Short display ids: render the shortest unambiguous prefix in human output

description: Render tl list as the hierarchy forest by default — the tree is the better browse experience — and replace --tree with --flat to opt back into one-line rows. Human output only: the --json data stays the flat items array (ADR-0017 §2 — a recursive JSON shape is not pinned), so the agent contract is untouched. Amend ADR-0017 §2 with the default flip and update the grammar summary, skill/docs mentions, and the list tests (default asserts the tree, --flat asserts rows).
title: list: tree view by default, --flat for one-line rows

description: The fold-per-invocation premise (vision §Scale target: comfortable at thousands of ops, cache deferred until real repos outgrow the fold) has fired its own trigger at a tenth of that scale. Measured on this tracker at 169 ops / ~30 open issues, idle machine: tl ready 87s, tl doctor 86s, tl stats 169s, tl list 5-7s, and writes grow x16 per x4 ops because transact folds the whole log under the lock. Root causes, verified per finding: the per-op sorted-list insert makes the fold quadratic in ops; effectiveStatus recomputes presentIssues (O(N^2)) on every call making list Theta(N^3); ready multiplies an O(R^2) insertion sort by uncached weight calls whose reachClosure never saturates early; cycle diagnostics run a closure per node, several times per command; the tree render re-walks shared subtrees exponentially on diamonds; sync union pays eraseDups O(L^2). Children are ordered by tier: shell-only fixes ship with tests; kernel fixes ship the efficient form as production with direct/characterization/agreement proofs per the efficiency principle (CLAUDE.md Code rules).
title: Performance: command paths at dogfooding scale

description: Vision §Scale-target already designs this cache (automatic, self-validating, gitignored .tl/local/, keyed to log content, rebuilt when stale — never user-managed) and its trigger condition has fired. Key the snapshot on per-segment byte lengths/hashes; on read, fold only the appended suffix — fold (l ++ ops) = ops.foldl apply (fold l) holds definitionally and order-insensitivity is already proved, so no new kernel theorem is needed. Kills both the per-command refold and the write-path quadratic (transact folds the whole log under the lock today). Tested-shell tier: snapshot codec round-trip, stale/absent/corrupt rebuild branches, and a property test that suffix-fold equals full fold.
title: Snapshot cache: persist materialized state, fold only appended suffixes

description: tl ready is 87s at ~30 open issues: rankSort is O(R^2) comparisons, each comparison recomputes weight, and each weight call recomputes presentIssues (O(N^2)) then burns all N reachClosure fuel iterations with no saturation exit — at least Theta(R^2 N^2) even on an edgeless graph (measured x17 per doubling). Fix in the kernel under the efficiency principle: compute presentIssues/presentEdges once per ready call, build a successor index, compute each candidate key (priority, weight, createdAt) once, sort by the cached keys; add a saturation early-exit to reachClosure (stop when reachStep acc = acc, justified by a fixpoint-stability lemma). Prove the efficient form correct directly or via one agreement theorem with the current definitions. The close path (its unblocked echo) shares the win.
title: ready: cache sort keys, precompute adjacency, saturate reachClosure early

description: tl stats is 169s and tl doctor 86s at 169 ops: sccWitnesses runs a full non-saturating closure per node with the successor function rescanning a freshly recomputed presentEdges per call, sameSCC runs more closures while grouping, and the commands recompute structural cycle results they already hold (cmdDepCycles re-calls cycles; stats recomputes per row). Shell quick win first: compute each cycle/diagnostic result once per command invocation and reuse it. Kernel: precompute the adjacency once per sccWitnesses call and reuse the reachClosure saturation exit; prove agreement with the current definitions per the efficiency principle.
title: cycles/stats/doctor: one adjacency index; stop recomputing closures per node

description: treeLines visits a node once per distinct root-to-node path — K chained multi-parent diamonds render 2^(K+2) lines (measured), and a single local command builds a diamond (--parent is repeatable on create, correctly unguarded per the CRDT no-write-guard rule). The tree is now the default list render, so this is reachable in normal use, not only after merges. Shell-only: thread a global emitted set through treeLines and render an already-shown marker on re-encounter (like the existing cycle marker), or expand only children whose canonicalParent is the current node and annotate extra parents; precompute one child index per render instead of filtering all present edges per node expansion. Ships with a diamond fixture test pinning linear output.
title: tree render: emit each shared node once (diamonds render exponentially)

description: Enforce the algorithmic-efficiency principle in CI: a Tests/ suite that builds synthetic logs at increasing scales (e.g. 200/800/3200 ops) and asserts growth stays near-linear for list/ready/stats/doctor/sync — by op-count or call-count instrumentation where feasible (timing-flake-proof), generous wall-clock ceilings otherwise. Catches the next accidental quadratic before it lands; complements, never replaces, the kernel proofs on efficient forms.
title: Perf regression tests: scaling assertions over synthetic logs

description: issueRow calls provenanceOf per rendered row, and provenanceOf walks every parsed op — list --limit 0 pays O(N x M) for provenance alone; doctor stale-claims does the same scoped to in-progress issues. Negligible today next to the cubic kernel walks, so sequenced after them — but the fix is cheap and local: one O(M) fold building provenanceMap (id -> provenance), threaded through View, reused by list/ready/show/doctor. Shell-only, zero proof obligations; property test pins map agreement with per-id provenanceOf.
title: provenance: one-pass map instead of a per-row log rescan

description: The union is superlinear in segment bytes, but not where first suspected: ByteArray append amortizes fine (capacity doubling, exclusively owned accumulator). The real costs: eraseDups is O(L^2) on the sorted line list, the mergeSort comparator calls toList per comparison, and segment equality in the local leg compares via toList. Fix: eraseReps adjacent dedup (sorted input makes duplicates adjacent), a direct byte-loop comparison in the sort, derived BEq ByteArray for equality. Shell tier; measured ~32s of union CPU at 12.8k lines, so it bites from the mid-thousands, scoped to tl sync only (reads use the O(1) ref-mark). Union output must stay byte-identical — round-trip tests pin the canonicalized bytes unchanged.
title: sync union: linear dedup and direct byte comparison

description: label list runs countOf twice per distinct label (JSON rows and the human string are both built strictly, even under --json) and each countOf rescans all issues through per-issue assoc lookups — Theta(L N^2). Count in a single pass over presentIssues and derive rows and human lines from the same counted list. Materialize accumulates lists by repeated append inside loops; switch to Array push (or cons + reverse). Both shell-only; tests assert unchanged counts, ordering, and JSON shape.
title: label list: count in one pass; materialize: linear accumulation

description: Switch effectiveStatus from fuel-bounded descent (effStatusAux with present-issue-count fuel) to the memoized shape: visiting — the current recursion path — detects a parent cycle at the exact node (a global visited set would mistake shared DAG children for cycles), and memo caches completed statuses so each node is evaluated once per query; the fuel form re-evaluates shared descendants combinatorially on diamond-shaped parent DAGs. Profile evidence makes this the dominant read fix: at N=400, effectiveStatus is 8165/8183 samples of tl list (via the effClosed filter), because every call recomputes presentIssues (O(N^2)) for the fuel and presentChildren per node — list is Theta(N^3) today. The switch must therefore also hoist presentIssues/presentEdges out of the per-node recursion, or ship as a batched effStatusAll : State -> AMap IssueId Status with one pointwise agreement lemma against effectiveStatus, so a list does one rollup pass total. Semantics unchanged: manual Cancelled precedence, cycle-trapped epics fall back conservatively (never Done), dangling children inert. Proof obligations (ADR-0003 §3 amendment): totality by well-founded recursion on the unvisited measure; re-prove acyclic exactness and the never-Done cycle guarantee over the new shape — directly, or via a characterization (recurrence) lemma quarantining the memo-coherence invariant; an equivalence bridge to a reference is admissible scaffolding, not required, and no unmemoized version ships. Recommended extra theorem: once-per-query — an id present in memo is never recomputed. Wall-clock stays tested, never proved.
title: Rollup: switch effectiveStatus to memoized visiting+memo recursion

description: Parent edges are settable only at create (--parent, repeatable); there is no verb to add or remove a parent edge afterwards, although ADR-0003 §4 explicitly treats issues as reparentable (multi-parent converges as two surviving edges, canonical parent derived by stamp). Surfaced concretely when a task needed moving under a later-created epic and the only route was recreate + close-as-duplicate. Options: extend dep add/remove with a --kind parent, or a dedicated tl parent set/remove pair; either way the courtesy guards stay local-only per the CRDT rule, and the multiParent diagnostic keeps reporting merge-created extras.
title: Reparent: a CLI surface for parent edges on existing issues

description: After the epic's algorithmic fixes, the dominant read cost at dogfooding scale is boxed string comparisons through the TotalOrd instances: TotalOrd String is comap String.toList (two char-list allocations + a boxed lex walk per comparison) and the blanket TotalOrd.instDecidableEq decides equality as le a b && le b a (two walks), shadowing native String.decEq inside all generic AMap/AssocList code. Profile: instDecidableListLe + comap + instDecidableEq = ~1.2k/1.4k samples of tl list --json at 172 ops (~1.4s). Fix direction: native-backed le/eq for String (UTF-8 byte order equals codepoint order, so the order is unchanged) with agreement lemmas, or DecidableEq routed to String.decEq inside the canonical-map code; kernel tier, so the efficient form ships with proofs per the efficiency principle (CLAUDE.md). Found while working the performance epic; out of its enumerated children, recorded per the deferral-as-task discipline.
title: TotalOrd comparison constants: native string equality/order fast paths

description: The performance epic fixed command paths with the fold cache and derived indexes; the kernel fold itself remains quadratic (each op's delta enters via AssocList.insertWith, O(position) per op), which still bites on the cache-miss surfaces: a cold cache rebuild (measured 26.8s at 2805 ops) and large sync absorptions. Two directions were weighed. (A) Replace the list-backed AMap/OrSet with balanced trees: rejected for now — the whole proof architecture rests on canonical sorted lists making the CRDT join laws genuine EQUALITIES (Tl/Crdt/Map.lean header; State.ext, fold_eq_of_mem_iff, the frame lemmas and CloseMono all rewrite through structural equality); trees are not canonical (one map, many shapes), so the laws degrade to setoid equivalences or need quotients/canonical-shape invariants — a proof-architecture rewrite ADR-0004/0009 deliberately avoided. If real logs outgrow batched folds, (A) becomes its own ADR-level decision. (B) THIS task: keep the structures, make the COLD fold near-linear by batched construction — collect all op deltas, sort entries once (O(N log N)), group per key, and merge into the canonical sorted list in one pass; ship as foldFast with a refinement bridge foldFast = fold per the epic's established fast+bridge pattern (RollupFast/ReadyFast/CyclesFast). Kernel tier: efficient form is production, proofs required, wall-clock stays tested.
title: Near-linear cold fold: batched canonical construction (not a structure swap)

description: Scoped follow-up to the done line-level sync fix, which linearized within-segment dedup/compare but not the per-segment axis. unionSegments (Tl/Sync/Merge.lean:69-74) builds its replica-id set via eraseDups then does xs.find?/ys.find? per id -- O(S^2) in the number of replica segments. segsEquiv (Tl/Sync/Local.lean:54-56) likewise eraseDups the ids and re-find?s per id. Small N today (one segment per replica), but unbounded in principle and on the merge/publish path. Fix (shell tier, no proofs): both segment lists sort by replicaId; sort once and merge-join on replicaId instead of eraseDups+find?, emitting the per-id union in one linear pass. Output bytes must stay byte-identical -- the round-trip canonicalization tests pin them. Filed per the principle: do not scale quadratically with segment count even when the count is small now.
title: sync: union/segsEquiv are quadratic in segment count (eraseDups + per-id find?)

description: The ceiling-only rows in Tests/PerfTests.lean (the fast ready queue and the fast diagnostics) are asserted by generous wall-clock ceilings, not the x4-ops ratio, because two algorithms stay superlinear after the epic's fast-path work. (1) readyFast sorts candidates with rankSortK, an O(R^2) insertion sort (Tl/Kernel/ReadyFast.lean:163-170); the ranking keys are already cached (RankKey), so a near-linear comparison sort over the keys is a drop-in. (2) Cycle diagnostics detect SCCs by running a saturating reachability closure per node, plus two more per candidate pair in sameSCC (Tl/Kernel/CyclesFast.lean:27-42) -- O(V*(V+E)), superlinear in present issues, the epic's own scale axis (vision targets thousands of ops). Replace with a single-pass SCC (Tarjan or Kosaraju) yielding the same witness components. The PerfTests ceilingRow comment currently attributes these to the TotalOrd-constants and cold-fold tasks, but neither addresses the sort or SCC algorithm -- this task is their real owner; update that comment when it lands. Kernel tier: ship the efficient form as production with a refinement bridge to the existing definitions (the established RollupFast/ReadyFast/CyclesFast fast+bridge pattern), per the efficiency principle. Wall-clock stays tested.
title: ready sort + cycle SCC: replace O(R^2) insertion sort and reachability-per-node SCC with near-linear forms

description: A few lower-frequency read paths still call non-hoisted spec helpers that re-derive presentEdges per call, instead of the View-hoisted edge views the epic introduced. issueObj uses canonicalParent s i (Tl/Cli/Project.lean:299) where the list row uses the hoisted canonicalParentE. doctor's multi-parent count calls s.parentsOf per present issue (Tl/Cli/Commands.lean:668) -- O(N*E) on the doctor path, the scaling axis. show uses s.blockersOf/s.dependentsOf for one issue (Tl/Cli/Render.lean:214-215). The single-issue ones are cheap; the doctor multi-parent scan is the one that matters at scale. Shell tier, no proofs: route these through the hoisted v.edges/v.pedges helpers (blockersOfE/dependentsOfE/kidsOfEdges/canonicalParentE). Tests assert unchanged output.
title: Hoist remaining per-call scan helpers in issueObj/doctor/show

description: Follow-on to the TotalOrd equality routing (String DecidableEq -> String.decEq, landed). That fixed the most frequent comparison (lookup's k = p.1) but the ORDER comparison still allocates: String's decLe is instDecidableListLe over String.toList a / .toList b — two List Char materializations (toList is @[extern lean_string_data]) per call, hit by insertWith positioning (lt k p.1) and the merge fold. Make it native with a proven agreement (the kernel efficiency principle: efficient form is production, proved). RECIPE (verified against lean4 v4.30.0 core): core defines String.lt s t := s.toList < t.toList with @[extern lean_string_dec_lt] decidableLT, and String.le a b := ¬ b < a with a native decLE; core List < is Lex (·<·) (Init/Data/List/Basic.lean:200,245). So override String.decLe a b := decidable_of_iff (a ≤ b) h, reusing core's native String.decLE, where h : (a ≤ b) ↔ TotalOrd.le a.toList b.toList. Prove h from a List-Char lemma listLe x y ↔ ¬ Lex (·<·) y x by induction on x,y (cases: nil/nil, nil/cons, cons/nil, cons/cons with a char trichotomy), bottoming out in charLt agreement: TotalOrd.lt c d ↔ c < d via Char.lt_iff_val_lt_val (rfl) + UInt32.lt_iff_toNat_lt, since our TotalOrd Char = comap (·.val.toNat). Keep String's le defeq to comap String.toList's (only decLe changes), so all order proofs are untouched; decLe is data (Subsingleton), so no theorem consumes it. Optionally add a ceiling/ratio assertion that an insert-heavy String-keyed build stays near-linear. Files: Tl/Crdt/Order.lean (the String instance + a Char/List agreement section).
title: Native-order decLe for String (route through core's extern String.decLE)

description:
Found while making the cycle-diagnostics perf row honest (the SCC work measured its machinery at ~0.7ms/call at 400 ops, yet the command path failed the x12 ratio): the dominant remaining superlinear on command paths is the OR-Set view materialization, not any algorithm downstream of it.

Where: Tl/Crdt/OrSet.lean — presentElements = elements.filter (decide (Present s e)), and Present e calls tagsOf e = (s.adds.find e), an AMap (sorted assoc list) find that is O(N) per element => Theta(N^2) per view; each tag additionally probes p.1 ∉ s.removed, another sorted-list find. Consumers: State.presentIssues / State.presentEdges (State.lean:245-248) and parentEdges (RollupFast.lean:46, which pays a presentEdges scan PLUS a per-edge hasIssue probe). Every command (list/show/ready/dep cycles/stats/doctor) pays these per invocation; cyclesFast x2 + precCyclesFast pays them three times.

Measured (compiled tltest probe, 400 synthetic ops, 25 reps): presentIssues ~1.2ms/call, presentEdges ~9.8ms/call, parentEdges ~11ms/call, growing ~x16 per x4 ops — vs the entire SCC certificate machinery at 0.7ms/call. The diagnostics command path is meanwhile pinned by an absolute-ceiling row in Tests/PerfTests.lean (named comment points here); the machinery has honest ratio rows.

Fix shape (kernel tier, efficiency principle): derive presence in ONE walk of adds.toList — for each (e, tags) entry decide ∃ tag ∉ removed directly (hash/sorted-merge view of the removed set to kill the per-tag find), giving presentElementsFast in ~O(total-tags log R). Prove presentElementsFast = presentElements (or mem_-iff plus order preservation — toList.map fst is already the sorted key order that elements/filter yields, so list equality should hold definitionally per entry) and swap the State views to the fast form behind the bridge, leaving every theorem stated over Present untouched. Watch the proofs that unfold State.presentIssues/presentElements directly. Also worth folding in: have cycleCount/doctor share one view computation across its three diagnostic calls instead of recomputing per call.
title: OR-Set presentElements is quadratic: derive presence in one entry walk

description:
Accepted-cost residual from the certificate-checked SCC work, recorded per the efficiency principle (CLAUDE.md: an accepted compromise is an ADR or tracked task, never silent).

Where: groupSCCH (Tl/Kernel/CyclesFast.lean) emits each witness as cyclic.filter (same-component-as v) — one full pass over the cyclic node list per emitted component, so witness grouping is Theta(cyclic-nodes x cycle-components). Zero on a healthy graph (cyclic = []), linear for one giant cycle (one component), quadratic only when the cyclic set shatters into many small components (e.g. N/2 disjoint 2-cycles => ~N^2/2 work). Detection (Tarjan + checker) is already near-linear; only the grouping has this shape. The covered-set scan is already hashed (groupSCCH); the residual is purely the per-component filter.

Fix shape (kernel tier): one pass over cyclic bucketing nodes by their component index (hash map index -> members in cyclic order, plus first-appearance order of indices), then emit buckets in first-appearance order. Output must stay EXACTLY the spec's sccWitnesses (deterministic witnesses contract): prove bucket contents = cyclic.filter (same-component) (bucket appends in walk order = filter order) and bucket emission order = groupSCCGo's first-uncovered-representative order (a node is covered iff its component was already emitted — invariant pairing the emitted-index set with the covered set). Bridge into sccFromCert behind the existing sccWitnessesT_eq statement; nothing outside CyclesFast.lean changes.

Optional fold-in while there: thread the cidxOf map from sccCertOk into sccFromCert instead of rebuilding it (the accept path currently builds the identical hash map twice — a constant-factor nit found in review).
title: SCC witness grouping: bucket by component index to kill the cyclic-by-components residual

description:
Confirmed by review + first-hand: cycleCount (Tl/Cli/Commands.lean:280-282) calls State.cyclesFast s .Blocks + cyclesFast s .Parent + precCyclesFast m s, and each fast form RE-DERIVES the OR-Set views internally from s (Tl/Kernel/CyclesFast.lean:479-482 reads s.presentIssues + s.presentEdges; :494-498 reads s.presentIssues + blocksAdj s.presentEdges + bucketBy s.parentEdges, so precCyclesFast materializes presentEdges TWICE). loadView already hoisted these once (Commands.lean:59-61). readyFast (ReadyFast.lean:183) re-derives them too. Net per tl stats: presentEdges materialized ~6-9x, each Theta(E^2) via presentElements (see sibling task). This is a 5-7x MULTIPLICATIVE constant on top of the presentElements quadratic, and is fixable INDEPENDENTLY of it.

Fix: give cyclesFast/precCyclesFast/cycleCount variants that accept the pre-hoisted present/edges/pedges lists (the kernel already has kindSuccE/precSuccH over explicit edge lists with rfl/proved bridges; cyclesFast just needs to take edges/present as params instead of reading s). Keep the cyclesFast_eq/precCyclesFast_eq bridges by instantiating edges := s.presentEdges at the call equality. Ripples to Commands.lean (cmdDepCycles, cycleCount, cmdDoctor) and the CrossTests/PerfTests mirrors. Measured impact: tl stats 10.8s and doctor 9.7s vs ready 6.8s at 4000 issues (warm) — the ~1.6x gap over ready is this redundancy.
title: Diagnostics rebuild hoisted views 3-7x: thread View.edges/pedges/rollup into cyclesFast/precCyclesFast/cycleCount

description:
Confirmed first-hand. reconcile (Tl/Sync/Local.lean:127-149): 'let merged := unionSegments refSegs localSegs' (line 133) and 'let refSegs := readRef d' (line 132) run UNCONDITIONALLY, then 'let publish := ownReplica.isSome && !segsEquiv merged refSegs' (line 136) decides publish from the already-built merged. So every write pays a full-log union + a per-replica git cat-file readRef even when nothing publishes. autoSyncLocal (Tl/Sync/AutoSync.lean:56) gates on tl.autosync; autoSyncInitDefault turns it ON by default for linked worktrees (the agent-per-worktree audience that is the project's whole point, ADR-0016/0021). unionLines (Merge.lean:59-63) does completeLines a ++ completeLines b then mergeSort over EVERY line. Not covered by the fold cache (read/transact-fold only).

Measured: writes 0.82s -> 2.1s -> 5.7s at 1000/2000/4000 issues (my throwaway repos had auto-sync OFF since non-linked-worktree, so that 5.7s is the base transact/materialize cost; the union adds on top for linked worktrees).

Fix: short-circuit BEFORE unioning — compare this replica's own-segment byte length/hash against the ref's own-segment entry (the write just appended to it and knows it); only union when the own segment genuinely diverged from the ref. Consider also a cheap ref-tip/marker check to skip readRef, and weigh debouncing auto-sync publish off the synchronous write path. NOTE: the fold cache is read/transact only; this path is the write-side analogue.
title: Auto-sync re-unions the whole log on every write; segsEquiv fast-out computed after the union

description:
readyFast computes keyOf per ready candidate (Tl/Kernel/ReadyFast.lean:188) -> weightFast edges s n i (:149-153) -> '(reachFix (blocksSuccE edges s) n [i]).erase i).length' (:101-102). blocksSuccE (:93-95) LINEAR-FILTERS the full hoisted edge list every call, and reachFix calls it per reached node per step. So weight is O(candidates x reachSteps x E). Bounded today only because the open candidate set is small, but it is superlinear in edges.

Fix: build a blocks-successor adjacency (Std.HashMap IssueId (List IssueId)) once per readyFast call, like CyclesFast.blocksAdj, and have weightFast/blocksSuccE read it. Keep the proved blocksSuccE_eq bridge by providing a blocksAdj_eq-style lemma (the reverse of the bucket = the filtered list, already proven for blocksAdj in CyclesFast). Pairs naturally with the diagnostics-hoisting task (shared adjacency).
title: readyFast weight: build a blocks-adjacency index once instead of filtering all edges per node per candidate

description: cmdList sorts present issues by createdAt (Tl/Cli/Commands.lean:151: 's.presentIssues.map (fun i => (s.createdAtOf i, i))'), and createdAtOf is an O(N) AMap.find per issue -> O(N^2) over the list. The provenance map already carries createdAt per id in one pass (provenanceMap). Fix: sort using (provOf v.prov i).createdAt (one lookup) or a precomputed createdAt index. CAUTION: createdAtOf uses the min add-tag HLC; Prov.createdAt uses the earliest-by-stamp create HLC — reconcile the two definitions (or keep createdAtOf but index it) so list order does not shift. Contributes to tl list 5.5s at 4000 issues.
title: cmdList sort recomputes createdAtOf O(N) per issue -> O(N^2); reuse the provenance map's createdAt

description: The human tree render (Tl/Cli/Render.lean / cmdShow tree) uses List.contains for the emitted set and path membership, and re-filters pedges per node to find children — O(N^2) / O(N*E) on wide/deep trees. The diamond-dedup correctness (one expansion per shared node, the restored cycle marker) must be preserved. Fix: Std.HashSet for emitted + path membership; build a parent->children Std.HashMap (bucketBy-style) once so each node's children is a lookup. Pin the diamond/cycle/shared-root fixtures still pass (Tests/CliTests.lean).
title: tree render: hash the emitted/path sets and bucket children once (currently O(N^2)/O(N*E))

description:
This is WHY the post-fold quadratic shipped invisibly. Tests/PerfTests.lean gaps, all confirmed:
(1) NO end-to-end spawned-binary latency test at any scale — the epic's headline symptom (multi-second tl ready/stats/doctor) is unguarded; every row is an in-process kernel-function bench. Add: seed a repo with a few thousand issues, IO.Process.run each read command on the built tl binary, assert a wall-clock ceiling or a two-scale ratio. This is the only test that exercises the real per-command view materialization.
(2) The memoized rollup row reads 0ms/0ms (effStatusAll) — vacuous, no scaling guard, despite being the dominant cost behind stats/doctor/list. Make it do measurable work (reps/N to clear 30ms) or assert an op count.
(3) ratioRow floor=max(tSmall,30) systematically masks any row under 30ms -> degrades to a ~360ms backstop a full x16 quadratic passes under (ready 2ms, rollup 0ms, others). Raise reps/N until each timed row clears 30ms honestly, OR switch to operation-count assertions (count AMap.find calls) so the floor cannot mask a quadratic.
(4) full-diagnostics ceiling is 2500ms vs a 4-42ms measurement (~60x slack) — tighten to a ratio or a ceiling sized to current+small multiple.
(5) bounded-32 open set makes ready/list rows measure a fixed candidate count, not a scaling workload; either let the open set scale with N or bench the view-scan cost explicitly with an honest floor.
(6) cache/sync-union/native-string-order benefits are pinned only for correctness — a revert to the slow form passes all tests. Add benefit assertions (warm materially cheaper than cold; honest >30ms floor on the union row; a structural check that String TotalOrd uses the native decEq/decLE path).
Measured baseline to anchor ceilings (warm, built binary): at 4000 issues list 5.5s, ready 6.8s, stats 10.8s, doctor 9.7s; at 1000 issues ~0.7-1.0s. Relates to tl-jfft8h1p16fc7nm6 (the original regression-suite child).
title: Perf suite is blind to the real per-command cost: add end-to-end binary latency + de-floor-mask the vacuous rows

description: Two definitions of the same parent-canonicalization logic exist with nothing tying them together at build time, so an edit to one silently diverges. Per CLAUDE.md (no silent spec/fast drift): either prove canonicalParentE v i = canonicalParent v.state i (a pure list-restriction argument mirroring kidsOfEdges_parentEdges) and make the spec the single source, or — if a kernel theorem is overkill for a display-only projection — collapse to one definition the shell and any proof both consume. Find both defs (grep canonicalParent in Tl/Cli + Tl/Kernel).
title: canonicalParentE (prod) and canonicalParent (spec) are hand-duplicated with no compile-time bridge

description: Tests/CrossTests.lean cyclesBranchOk/precBranchOk re-derive the successor functions by hand and today match cyclesFast/precCyclesFast verbatim (CyclesFast.lean:479-498), but the duplication spans files with nothing enforcing sync; PerfTests benches hand-roll it a third/fourth time. If a future change alters cyclesFast's internal succ hoisting (it changed twice during the epic), the cert-acceptance tests keep passing against stale wiring while production silently falls back to the proved-but-slow closure path. Fix: export a single production entry point (e.g. cyclesCertAccepted s k living next to cyclesFast) that both production and the acceptance tests consume, so a wiring refactor breaks the test. NOTE: pairs with the diagnostics-hoisting task tl-xgp45hqr (which WILL change that wiring) — do this first or together.
title: Test mirrors cyclesBranchOk/precBranchOk hand-copy production successor wiring; a refactor silently disables the near-linear SCC path

description: At the latencies measured pre-optimization (list 5.5s, stats 10.8s at 4000 issues) the terminal just freezes — the whole --json envelope buffers until the command completes, and read/write paths shell out to git (refresh, auto-sync-local) with no timeout, so a hung git hangs the command silently. Fix: (a) for interactive tty human output, a timer-gated stderr progress line/spinner once a command crosses ~1s (fast commands stay silent; --json stays a single atomic object, progress only to stderr); (b) bound the best-effort git invocations with a short wall-clock timeout, falling back to the same 'degraded' note path an error already uses. Lower urgency once the perf tasks land and commands drop back under ~1s, but the git-timeout robustness stands on its own.
title: No progress signal on multi-second commands; git calls have no timeout

description: Reproduced on the built binary: 'tl create "title"' with stdin a pipe/fd that is open but never EOFs blocks INDEFINITELY in IO.FS.Stream.readToEnd (fread), emitting nothing — the description-body-on-stdin read (Tl/Cli/Commands.lean, the create lam reading stdin) has no isatty guard. An agent that spawns tl with an inherited/forgotten stdin hangs with no diagnostic. Fix: only treat non-tty stdin as a body source when explicitly opted in (an explicit '-' / '--description -' sentinel), OR gate the read on stdin NOT being a tty AND being immediately ready / bounded. Ship with a test (a create invoked with an open, non-EOF stdin must not block; piped body with EOF still works; tty implies no body).
title: tl create blocks forever on a non-tty stdin that never reaches EOF, with zero output

description: Tl.Store.cacheVersion must be bumped on any change to decodeLine classification, WireOp.toOp, or kernel apply/merge semantics (else a stale cache silently deserializes wrong state). This is stated only in Cache.lean's header — the code sites that would trigger it (Apply.apply / State.merge, Codec.lean WireOp.toOp / decodeLine) have no pointer. Fix: one-line comment at each trigger site pointing to cacheVersion. Cheap, prevents a silent correctness bug.
title: cacheVersion bump discipline is load-bearing but documented only in Cache.lean's header

description: .claude/skills/tl/SKILL.md 'Not yet available' section still says there is no auto-sync, contradicting shipped behavior (best-effort local publish on write, default-on for linked worktrees, git config tl.autosync). Also: auto-sync/refresh degradation is disclosed only in the envelope's notes[] (e.g. 'auto-sync skipped (...) — run tl sync'), but the skill tells agents to branch on error.code and never mentions inspecting notes[] on success — so an agent never sees a degraded publish. Fix: update SKILL.md Sharing + 'Not yet available' to reflect auto-sync, and document notes[] as a field agents should surface on success (it carries refusals, skew-deferrals, stale-read and auto-sync-skip disclosures). Doc-only; verify against the actual emitted note strings in AutoSync.lean / Commands.lean.
title: Skill is stale on auto-sync and never tells agents to read notes[] on success

description:
After presentElements was made linear (tl-6hffv8hf), profiling at 4000 issues shows the dominant remaining cost is per-issue AMap.find — every find is a LINEAR assoc-list scan (Tl/Crdt/Map.lean AssocList.lookup), called once per issue across N issues => O(N²).

Measured (in-process, 4000 issues, /tmp/prof.lean): presentIssues build 0ms (fixed); but 'per-issue issueData find' (s.issueData i, = s.data.find i per row) = 2640ms/call, and 'per-issue rollup find' (effStatusWith/effClosedWith v.rollup, = rollup.find i per row) = 2941ms/call. These are paid by byStored (stats), the filter passes (blocked/deferred/effClosed), issueObj per rendered row (list/ready), readyFast's per-candidate reads, doctor's per-issue checks.

Fix shape (shell hoisting, no kernel-proof churn — the machinery already exists): build hash copies of the rollup and data maps ONCE per View (Std.HashMap, via SccFast's hashAssoc, which has the proved bridge getElem?_hashAssoc_amap : hashAssoc m.toList lookup = m.find), store them on the View (rollupH, dataH), and route per-row lookups through them (O(1) amortized). effStatusWith's spec fallback is preserved: the hash has the same keys as the AMap, so a miss = the same fallback. Add effStatusWithH/issueDataH-style helpers or look up in the shell. Provide a CrossTests agreement check (hash form == AMap form per issue).

This is THE remaining scale bottleneck: with it, list/ready/stats/doctor should drop from ~3-5s to sub-second at 4000 issues. Wall-clock at 4000 currently: list 2.75s, ready 4.3s, stats 5.2s, doctor 4.7s.
title: Per-issue AMap.find is O(N) ⇒ O(N²) commands: hash the rollup + issueData maps once per view

description:
Profiling (in-process /tmp/prof3.lean, 4000 issues) found TWO more O(N^2) view-layer costs, both rooted in AMap.find/insert being a linear assoc-list scan:

1. effStatusAll = 15886ms/call on a deep parent CHAIN. The 'memoized' rollup (RollupFast.rollupVisit) memoizes completed statuses in an AMap — but AMap insert/find is O(N), so memoization is O(N^2) on deep epic nesting (a 4000-long parent chain). Topology-dependent: a parent CYCLE happens to be fast, a deep DAG/chain is quadratic. The original 'memoized rollup' child (tl-vrqhx) fixed the recompute-per-call but the memo container is still linear. FIX: back rollupVisit's memo (and the visiting-path membership) with Std.HashMap/HashSet instead of AMap; the spec bridge effStatusAll_find stays (it's about the RESULT map, which can still be the AMap built once at the end, or a hash with a bridge). Watch: the proof effStatusWith_eq / rollupVisit_find_hit reference the memo.

2. parentEdges = 1183ms/call, TOPOLOGY-INDEPENDENT. parentEdges (RollupFast.lean:46) filterMaps presentEdges keeping Parent edges whose child is present — via decide (s.hasIssue t) PER EDGE, and hasIssue = OrSet.Present = an O(N) tagsOf find. So O(E*N) = O(N^2). This hits EVERY command (loadView builds parentEdges) — ~1.2s of the binary's 2.5-2.9s at 4000. FIX: build a present-issue Std.HashSet once (hashSetOf s.presentIssues, contains_hashSetOf_present bridge already exists in HashMapView) and presence-filter through it. Same pattern applies to kindSucc/blocksSuccE dangling-filters and anywhere hasIssue is called per-edge/per-row.

These are the same AMap-O(N) root cause as tl-z2nj35hk; distinct fixes (rollup memo container; edge presence-filter). Measured progress so far this session (committed): ready 6.8->2.5s, stats 10.8->3.2s, doctor 9.7->3.1s, list 5.5->2.9s @4000 via presentElements-linear + diagnostics/readyFast hashing.
title: effStatusAll memo + parentEdges are O(N^2): hash the rollup memo and presence-filter edges

description:
Native profiling (compiled exe, 4000 issues, 2.5MB cache) found the warm-read FLOOR is ~2.23s and splits into two comparable halves: effStatusAll (~1.5s, see tl-mkjvp4km) and the cache DECODE machinery (~1.0s) — measured here for the first time (was a suspicion in prior notes). Per-rendered-row work (tl-z2nj35hk) only adds ~0.4s on top, so decode now matters MORE than the render path.

Decode breakdown (Tl/Store/Cache.lean, warm read of a fresh cache):
- decodeCache(full) = 742ms = integrity-SHA(payload 2.5MB) 263ms + Json.parse 36ms + decState ~443ms.
- cacheValid = +240ms: shaHexOf (sd.bytes.extract 0 byteLen) re-hashes the WHOLE ~2.3MB log prefix every read to confirm the cached prefix still matches.
- So a warm read runs TWO pure-Lean SHA-256 passes (~503ms total) over ~2.4MB each, plus ~443ms rebuilding AMaps/OrSets from JSON sub-objects per issue.

Costs and the tension with the proof tier:
1) SHA-256 (503ms): Tl/Hash/Sha256.lean is a pure-Lean FIPS transcription; ADR-0018 says an optimized variant may only ship with a proved fast=spec bridge — so speeding the hash itself is a real proof undertaking, not a free shell change. Cheaper angles: (a) the cacheValid prefix-SHA — for the common append case byteLen grows and lineCount changes; can a cheaper rolling/incremental integrity suffice while keeping rewrite-detection? (b) hash only a bounded prefix+suffix+length sample? (weaker integrity — needs an ADR note). Both touch ADR-0014/0018 trust wording; record the decision.
2) decState ~443ms: JSON sub-object parse + AMap.ofAscList? per issue (the ofAscList? is O(N) — fine; the cost is the JSON shape). A more compact binary cache encoding (e.g. length-prefixed columnar) would cut this but is a format rewrite + new codec round-trip tests + cacheVersion bump.

This is tested-shell tier (Cache.lean): any fix ships with codec round-trip + every-validity-branch tests in Tests/CacheTests.lean, and a cacheVersion bump if the on-disk format/semantics change. Harness: Prof.lean (temporary lean_exe tlprof, reverted) + /tmp/tlscale4000. Filed under the perf epic; related to the fold-cache task tl-zwfewb3m.
title: Cache decode is ~1.0s of the warm-read floor: two SHA-256 passes over 2.4MB + JSON decState

description: Class fix + prevention for the dominant, recurring perf class: an O(N) associative access (AMap.find, OrSet.Present/tagsOf, List.contains, an edge filter) invoked once per element across N elements makes a command O(N^2)/O(N*E). The open instances (z2nj35, mkjvp4, whp0xy, p8kqkf) are this one bug restated. FIX: route every command/row/diagnostic path through the proved hash views in Tl/Kernel/HashMapView.lean (hashAssoc + getElem?_hashAssoc_amap, hashSetOf + contains_hashSetOf_present, bucketBy + getD_bucketBy), per the landed isReadyFastH pattern; build the hashed handles once per View (rollupH/dataH, present HashSet, blocks/parent buckets) and consume them everywhere. PREVENT (structural): make raw O(N) accessors unreachable from command paths — helpers take the indexed-view handles, never a raw State/AMap; consider an ADR promoting the hashed container as the standard memo/index substrate (the mkjvp4 trap: a 'memoized' rollup whose memo was still an AMap).
title: Indexed views — kill the O(N)-lookup-in-a-loop class

description: Class: collections built by repeated insert/append costing O(current size), and graph fixpoints recomputed without saturation or a single-pass structure. FIX: batched canonical construction (mergeSort + adjacent collapse, foldFast), adjacent dedup on sorted input, Array push, saturating reachClosure (fixpoint-stability lemma), single-pass SCC (Tarjan + checker) with bucket-by-component witness grouping. PREVENT: structural near-linearity / saturating-closure theorems (kernel) + near-linear perf ratio assertions. Mostly landed; open tail: rz9p7y (SCC witness grouping bucket).
title: Near-linear builds & graph walks

description: Class: recomputing the whole materialized state (or the whole sync union) per invocation instead of incrementally. FIX: content-keyed fold cache + suffix-fold on reads and transact (ADR-0022, landed); write-side analogue — short-circuit auto-sync's union by comparing the own segment's hash against the ref BEFORE building the union. PREVENT: cache validity tests + a write-path scaling assertion (append materially cheaper than a full refold/re-union). Open tail: fk9jydf.
title: Incremental materialization & write path

description: Class: per-comparison allocation / boxed equality in inner loops — TotalOrd String materializing char lists per compare, a blanket decidable-eq shadowing native String.decEq. FIX: native-backed eq/order routed through core's extern String.decEq/decLE with proved agreement lemmas keeping order semantics unchanged. PREVENT: a structural test that String TotalOrd uses the native path (a revert is caught). Landed (b26rmp9, e158zz).
title: Native comparison primitives

description: Class 0 / META: the perf regression suite is vacuous — a 30ms ratioRow floor masks a full x16 quadratic, no end-to-end spawned-binary latency test, the open set is fixed at 32 so ready/list rows don't scale, and cache/union/native-string wins are pinned only for correctness (revert-to-slow passes). This is WHY the post-fold quadratics shipped invisibly. FIX: op-count assertions (count AMap.find / per-edge presence) that grow linearly not N^2 (a wall-clock floor can't mask them; they pin the class structurally); end-to-end binary latency at thousands of issues; scaling open set; benefit assertions. COUPLING: test-honesty lands WITH each path fix (de-flooring a still-quadratic row is red); the independently-landable piece now is the end-to-end binary-latency harness.
title: Perf prevention net (keystone)

description: Split from tl-hkc3crt per proof-tier. A warm read runs TWO pure-Lean SHA-256 passes over ~2.4MB: decodeCache integrity (~263ms) + cacheValid prefix re-hash (~240ms). Tl/Hash/Sha256.lean is a FIPS transcription; per ADR-0018 a faster hash ships ONLY with a proved fast=spec bridge. Cheaper angles, each needing an ADR note on ADR-0014/0018 trust wording: incremental/rolling integrity for the common append case (byteLen grows, lineCount changes); or a bounded prefix+suffix+length sample (weaker integrity). Proof/kernel tier — the deliverable is the fast hash or the integrity-scheme change; prevention is a structural test it stays on the fast path. Full measured breakdown in tl-hkc3crt.
title: Cache decode: two SHA-256 passes (~0.5s/read) — fast hash behind a fast=spec bridge

description: ADR-0023 §3: the indexed-view rule is discipline backed by a lint, not a by-construction guarantee, until the type-level View-only-accessor form exists. Add a CI lint, in the spirit of the existing no-task-ID-leakage gate, that flags AMap.find / OrSet.Present / presentElements reached from a per-element loop on a command path (Tl/Cli and the fast-path kernel modules). Today the raw accessors are public and callable from a command path — the per-row render path still calls issueData/effStatusWith once per rendered row (the tracked open violation, tl-z2nj35hk). The eventual target is the stronger type-level form: command paths receive only a View exposing hashed accessors, with raw State accessors out of scope; the lint is the enforcement until then. Prevention class — pairs with the perf-suite reshape (tl-mbjw5qewytr18v4e) under this sub-epic.
title: Lint: flag O(N) accessors (AMap.find / OrSet.Present / presentElements) reached from a per-element loop on a command path

description:
The proved-fast-primitives epic (tl-2rc4t6mh) promises "a structural test that the primitive uses the fast path so a revert to the slow form is caught." That guard does not exist for the landed members: a grep of Tests/ finds nothing pinning the String native comparison path, and no perf row exercises a String-keyed insert-heavy build specifically.

Why it matters: a revert is BEHAVIOR-INVISIBLE. Dropping the String.decEq override lets TotalOrd.instDecidableEq fall back to the le-derived two-walk decEq; losing native String.decLE re-materializes List Char per order compare. Both decide the SAME Prop, so every correctness test stays green while per-comparison cost regresses (the ~1.4s symptom b26 originally measured at ~172 ops). This is a CONSTANT-FACTOR regression in the primitive (allocation + boxing per compare), not an operation-count change -- so an op-count assertion cannot see it; it needs an END-TO-END latency guard (ADR-0023 tested tier: "end-to-end latency pins the cost"; the constant-factor recorded-explicitly clause).

Deliverable: a perf-suite guard over a String-keyed insert-heavy build whose absolute/ratio bound trips if the native path is lost (e158 already suggested "a ceiling/ratio assertion that an insert-heavy String-keyed build stays near-linear"). The same guard generalizes to the SHA fast path once tl-ebk47tc lands -- a structural/latency check that the cache decode stays on the fast hash. Mechanism lives in the perf suite, hence related to tl-mbjw5qe. Tested-shell tier. The String half can be built now (b26/e158 are landed); the SHA half trails tl-ebk47tc.
title: PREVENT: guard the native String (and SHA) fast paths against silent revert

description:
Spun from tl-mkjvp4km (rollup near-linearization). After the HashMap memo + bucketed kids + O(N log N) materialization + fast parentEdges (5 commits on perf/per-issue-find), effStatusAll's COMMON case (cyclic/shallow nesting) is near-linear (1590->215ms @4000, no remaining O(N^2)/O(N*E)). ONE residual remains, on a PATHOLOGICAL input only:

rollupVisit/rollupKids check membership of the current descent chain via `path.contains c` (path : List IssueId) -- O(depth) per kid. On a DEEP parent chain (e.g. 4000 epics nested linearly) depth is O(N), so this is O(N^2) (effStatusAll deep-chain = 269ms @4000, vs cyclic 215ms). Real trackers nest epics shallowly (3-5), so this never bites in practice; it is correctness-safe (path.contains is correct, just slow on the pathological input) -- an ADR-0004/0023 tested-not-proved performance residual, not a correctness issue.

FIX (the ADR-0024 §4 + design-panel plan): carry a Std.HashSet pathSet ALONGSIDE the List path (List path STAYS the termination measure; pathSet is runtime-only) for O(1) contains. Descent pushes onto both (i :: path, pathSet.insert i). Soundness carries a PathMirror invariant (forall x, pathSet.contains x = path.contains x), established at the descent via Std.HashSet.contains_insert + List.contains_cons, and used in rollupKids_sound's path-hit arm (pathSet.contains c -> path.contains c -> List.contains_iff_mem -> effectiveStatus_open_of_reencounter). This is the genuinely-new invariant carried like ChainOk through the mutual recursion. ~30-40 lines across the two soundness theorems + the defs + effStatusAllH (pathSet := empty, PathMirror for (empty, []) is trivial). effStatusAll_find/effStatusWith_eq stay byte-identical.

Profiler: /tmp/Prof.lean (the deep-chain row is the worst case). Files: Tl/Kernel/RollupFast.lean.
title: Rollup deep-chain: path.contains is O(depth)/kid; add a HashSet path mirror

description:
Both `tl ready` and `tl list` defaulted --limit to 10 (Tl/Cli/Main.lean natFlag default), too small for dogfooding-scale backlogs. Raise the default to 50 for these two commands; `tl log` keeps its 10 default (op history, a different surface).

Mechanics: limitFlag (Tl/Cli/Grammar.lean) is shared by ready/list/log, so its help text can't carry one number for all three — split it: limitFlag -> 'default 50' for ready/list, a new logLimitFlag -> 'default 10' for log. Update Main.lean ready/list natFlag defaults 10->50.

Note on enforcement: the limit IS applied — cmdReady (ranked.take) and cmdList JSON/--flat (visible.take) cap correctly, and tree mode caps top-level ROOTS (roots.take), disclosed in the footer. So in the default tree view the cap rarely bites because there are few epic-roots, which makes it feel unenforced; raising to 50 does not change that root-scoped semantics. Whether the tree should cap total rendered nodes instead of roots is a separate design question, left as a possible follow-up.

Docs to fix in the same change: Grammar.lean help text, docs/design-backlog.md tl-list grammar bullet (says 'default 10'). ADR-0020's 'default 10' is the tl log section and stays. Ship with a CliTests regression pinning that ready/list show >10 rows by default (create 11 issues, assert default items length is 11).
title: Raise default --limit to 50 for ready and list

description: DONE (commit 0ffe4e9). tl list's tree view capped top-level ROOTS at --limit instead of total rendered rows, so a few epic-roots expanded their full subtrees and the limit barely bit — counterintuitive: a human asking to see N issues got far more. title: tree list --limit caps rendered rows, not roots

description: Split out of tl-9jtr (which is now just the git timeout). The original asked for a timer-gated stderr spinner once any command crosses ~1s. Largely moot at normal scale now that the perf epic dropped reads under ~1s — a generic ~1s-gated spinner would essentially never fire. The one command that is legitimately multi-second and NOT fixable by local perf work is Synced: published your changes; remote 'origin': pushed over a network remote. If progress UX is wanted, scope it narrowly: a plain 'syncing with <remote>...' line to stderr BEFORE the network call (no background timer, no spinner). --json stays a single atomic object; progress only to stderr. Low priority / optional.
title: Interactive progress signal for genuinely slow commands (sync)

description: Found in the sync code review (after the posture/--sync work). claim --sync does pre-fetch -> claim -> post-push. The won/superseded outcome (cmdClaim) is computed from local state BEFORE the post-push performSync, which can pull a competing claim from another clone. So claim --sync can report won for a take a sibling actually got; only the next read shows superseded. For multi-agent coordination that is a real correctness gap (an agent starts work on a task it lost). Fix: after the post-push reconcile materializes the pulled state, re-read the issue assignee and recompute won/superseded so the echo reflects it. The race cannot be fully closed (distributed), but the report is then as fresh as the post-push fetch. Note: the in-flight race is not deterministically unit-testable (a competing claim must land mid-command); the re-derive reuses tested read/claim paths, and an uncontested test pins the normal case. Also: the pre-claim performSync pushes the old segment before the claim is written — a wasteful full sync; a fetch-only preflight would be cleaner (separate optimization). See cmdClaim in Tl/Cli/Commands.lean.
title: claim --sync: re-derive won/superseded after the publish-around pull

description: Found in the sync review. reconcileRemote (Tl/Sync/Remote.lean) does writeRefMergeCas (advances the LOCAL refs/tl/log to the merge commit) FIRST, then pushRefLog. If the push throws (auth/hook-decline/timeout — anything not the retryable non-fast-forward), the local ref is at a merge commit the remote never received. This self-heals: the last-sync marker is gated on success (never falsely advanced), and a subsequent sync re-fetches, re-unions (idempotent), and re-pushes. The behavior is correct but has no regression test. Add one: a bare remote with a pre-receive hook that exits 1 (deterministic push reject; fetch still works) -> sync fails with the local ref advanced -> remove the hook -> sync recovers and the remote converges. Pure shell/test tier.
title: Regression test: a remote push that throws after the local CAS recovers on the next sync

description: Found in the sync review. On a bounded-git timeout, runBounded returns exit 124. writeRefCas / writeRefMergeCas (Tl/Sync/Ref.lean) treat any non-zero update-ref as a CAS check: they re-read the tip and, if a sibling moved it, return none (retry as a lost race). A 124 (hung local git) thus gets retried as if it were a concurrent move, spinning up to maxAttempts, then surfacing the generic 'kept moving' message instead of a timeout. Fix: detect exit 124 first and throw a timeout error (carrying the timeout stderr) rather than treating it as a race. Bounded by maxAttempts so low-severity. Note: the specific late-update-ref-timeout branch is not deterministically unit-testable (a global tiny timeout fails inGitRepo first); a remote-leg timeout test pins the broader 'timeout surfaces as a clear error, not a race/push-rejected' property.
title: writeRefCas/writeRefMergeCas: a timed-out update-ref (exit 124) is misclassified as a CAS race

description:
Add `tl log --since <cursor> [--json]`: a read-only projection over the append-only op log returning every op after `<cursor>`, for incremental/resumable tailing of task-state changes. Rides the pinned JSON contract (ADR-0020 shapes unchanged); no new Op, no kernel theorem — a derived read.

Why: external consumers — a supervisor/dashboard, a wake-on-change dispatch loop, an orchestrator control plane watching the refs/tl/log OID — need a resumable tail of the log. Without a first-class change-feed every consumer re-implements log diffing + dedup. Ship it once, correctly.

CRITICAL design: the cursor MUST be a per-replica version vector (the frontier ADR-0008 already reserves), NOT a scalar HLC high-water mark. A late-arriving foreign op (clock skew, delayed sync) can carry an HLC below a previously-returned max; a scalar cursor would silently drop it on the next --since. A version vector tracks the highest HLC seen per replica, so a late op that sits below another replica's max is still emitted exactly once. Output is { ops-since-cursor, advancedCursor } — pass advancedCursor on the next call.

Tier (ADR-0004): tested shell code, not kernel. Coverage must include the distinguishing regression — a foreign op whose HLC is below a previously-seen max from a DIFFERENT replica MUST still appear under a vector cursor (and would be dropped by a scalar cursor). Also cover: empty/zero cursor ⇒ full history; post-cursor delta; idempotent re-read (same cursor ⇒ same tail); malformed / unknown-replica cursor degrades cleanly.

Load-bearing + retrofit-hostile: if a change-feed ever ships with a scalar cursor it silently loses late ops, so the per-replica vector cursor must be there from the first version. Highest-value agent-consumption add for external-orchestrator integration.
title: tl log --since <cursor>: resumable incremental change-feed (--json)

description: whyFast (ReadyFast) recomputes s.presentEdges and calls blockersOfE edges x = edges.filter(...) per BFS node — an O(E) edge scan per cone node, so the why walk is O(K·E). The reach engine (reachBFS) is already O(V+E); the remaining quadratic is the successor function. FIX: add a bucket-backed liveSuccB (btgt blocks-by-target bucket + pset + rollup hash) mirroring the existing blocksSuccB (ReadyFast.lean), with a bridge lemma liveSuccB_eq modeled on blocksSuccB_eq / blockerDischargedH_eq, then a whyFastH that feeds it to reachBFS; cmdWhy passes v.idx.btgt/presentH/rollupH. Re-route whyFast_eq via the equivalence so the proved 'why' characterization (mem_why_iff, thm 10) transfers untouched — no theorem-statement change. Effort M (one def + one bridge lemma, structurally identical to blocksSuccB). Payoff high on dense blocker graphs. Found during the reach-cone reuse/O(N²) sweep (branch perf/reach-cone-ovpe). Related: the provenanceMap eager-build (~506ms, built every command but unused by stats/doctor/dep-*; make lazy/per-command — M, not reach-shaped) and decodeSegment re-parse (~500ms/read; new parse-cache layer — M/L) remain the biggest store-level read-floor levers.
title: perf: cmdWhy blocker-cone is O(K·E) — bucket-back liveSuccE

description: reachBFSgo (ReachBFS.lean:296) runs the full fuel = presentIssues.length rounds with NO empty-frontier short-circuit, so a saturated cone still runs ~V trivial O(1) rounds (an O(V) tail per query; O(V²) on the cycle-cache fallback which builds V single-source closures). The retired reachFix had 'if next == acc then acc' — a natural early-exit. FIX: add 'if frontier.isEmpty (or p.2 empty) then output else recurse' so fuel is a totality BACKSTOP and the worklist terminates at saturation; prove reachBFSgo_eq still holds (empty frontier ⇒ fixpoint ⇒ equals full-fuel, like reachFix_eq's iterateN_of_fixed argument). Robustness: fuel-full-iteration is fragile; empty-frontier termination is the proper worklist form. Found by code-review (xhigh) finding #14.
title: perf: reachBFS empty-frontier early-exit (fuel as backstop, not iteration count)

description:
Turn the O(V+E) claim from a tested-tier assertion into a PROVED structural theorem (ADR-0023's 'provable shape' tier), so a future parentOf-rescan / per-round-dedup regression fails the BUILD, not just a perf test (the defect that shipped under tl-b18x existed precisely because this was tested-only and the test was missing).

SCOPE — option 3 of the feasibility analysis (NOT a cost monad, NOT wall-clock):
Prove, for the shared frontier engine (reachBFS in ReachBFS.lean; reuse for parentSweep/parentSweepH in Path.lean), the structural invariants that pin the complexity class:
- the per-round frontiers PARTITION the reachable set: pairwise disjoint, union = reachClosure, each ⊆ presentIssues. (Layers are reachClosure k minus reachClosure (k-1); reuse the monotone-closure lemmas already in Reach.lean — reachClosure_mono, subset_reachClosure_succ, the saturation/cardinality argument.)
- each reachable node lands in EXACTLY ONE frontier, and the engine folds its out-edges ONLY in that round ⇒ each edge examined once (total edge-work ≤ E) and each node inserted once (node-work ≤ V).
This is a plain proposition (no cost semantics). It is UNPROVABLE about a Θ(V·E) engine (you cannot prove 'edges examined once' while parentOf rescans the frontier or bfsLayerH re-dedups a per-round list) — so it is a self-enforcing guard.

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE / carried assumption: wall-clock time and Std.HashSet/HashMap amortized-O(1) stay TESTED + a tier-3 carried assumption (hash distribution/resizing can't be proved; record it in docs/overview.md Trusted section, same status as the system clock). The per-op→wall-clock gap is assumed, not proved; this task proves only the operation-STRUCTURE (each node/edge processed once).

DEPENDENCY: do this AFTER tl-b18x lands a genuinely process-each-edge-once engine (the invariant is only provable about the corrected engine). Related: tl-5cvf (empty-frontier early-exit — bounds the round count). Effort: moderate (~100-250 lines, a focused module reusing the existing layer characterization), proved once for the shared frontier engine and reused. Filed from the option-3 feasibility discussion.
title: prove the frontier engine's 'processed-once' structural invariant (proved O(V+E) shape)
