description: Tl/Sync/Remote.lean:60 — .pushRejected is thrown from exactly one place (fuel-0 arm, maxRemoteAttempts:=2); both tests that mention it assert the NEGATIVE (SyncTests.lean:403, CliTests.lean:1951). A swapped message / mis-set code / off-by-one fuel passes CI, violating the DoD (every error code it can emit is tested). Also docs/overview.md:233 falsely claims SyncTests covers this branch. FIX: force two consecutive non-fast-forward/CAS-loss signals (background pusher or a stub returning the race signal twice), assert e.code==.pushRejected + the 'moved during the push … run tl sync again' message; correct overview.md:233. Review Major #3.
title: test: push-rejected error code is emitted but never asserted (only the negative is tested)

description: Tl/Clock/Hlc.lean:79-89 — observeRemote is defined + tested but has ZERO production callers, yet ADR-0007:127-129,144 presents it as the live 'on every sync fold' transport-merge clock rule. Compounds: the present-clock write seed (Store/Lock.lean:129) floors by own-segment max only, while the absent-clock branch (:140) floors by all within-window segments — the two disagree. Not a convergence/data-loss bug (the within-window-higher-HLC-foreign-op-wins-LWW outcome is the deliberately-tested skew tradeoff, CliTests:598-613); only a causal read-then-write across transport escapes it, and no causal tracking exists. Plus observeRemote's two overflow .error arms are untested (Hlc.lean:87,89; HlcTests:35-38 cover only the 4 .ok shapes) though the test docstring claims overflow coverage. DECISION: either WIRE observeRemote into the absorb path (advance+persistClock past each absorbed segment max HLC, floor the present branch by loaded.maxHlc to match the absent branch) so the ADR holds + add the overflow tests + a shell test; OR DELETE it and amend ADR-0007:144 + overview.md:228 to describe the actual own-segment-floor + absent-clock-reseed policy. Review #6/#7/#17.
title: correctness+doc: observeRemote is dead API; clock-seed floors by own-segment max only; ADR-0007 overstates

description: Tl/Sync/Ref.lean:54-60 — the synchronous stdinH.write stdin precedes the outTask/errTask spawns and sits BEFORE the timeout loop, so a child interleaving large stdout with reading stdin can deadlock with no wall-clock rescue. Current callers (hash-object, mktree) are safe by accident (both emit a fixed ~41-byte oid regardless of stdin size). Constrains any future gitBytes/run-with-stdin caller piping a large blob through a filter. FIX: move the IO.asTask reader spawns above the takeStdin/write block (ideally write on a task too); add a comment pinning the invariant. Review Minor #8.
title: correctness: runBounded writes all stdin synchronously before spawning drain tasks (latent pipe deadlock)

description: Tl/Cli/Commands.lean:663 — after the take is durably appended and the best-effort performSync (try-wrapped, :654-657) completes, loadView re-derives the outcome with NO try/catch. A transient FS error or clock-read failure (liftSys nowMs in loadView) makes a durable claim exit nonzero; an exit-code-branching agent concludes failure and may retry into a spurious second claim. FIX: wrap the reload in try, fall back to the already-built post-write view v with a disclosure note (the echo then reflects local-only state, so the note matters). Review Minor #9.
title: correctness: claim --sync post-write loadView reload is unguarded — a durable claim can report failure

description: Tl/Cli/Commands.lean:695-703 — the epic close-guard fires unconditionally for --as done; when all children are already closed (epic effectively Done via rollup) the message reads 'it becomes done when its children close (open: 0)' — instructing an unachievable fix, with empty reasons.openChildren beside a hard not-closeable. The refusal itself is correct/ADR-0003-mandated; only the wording is wrong in this sub-case. FIX: keep the refusal, reword to 'already done via rollup; no explicit close needed' — preserves the ADR-0003 invariant. Review Minor #10.
title: usability: close <epic> --as done on an already-rolled-up epic gives a self-contradictory message

description: Tl/Store/Lock.lean:78-80 -> Tl/Store/Local.lean:189-192 — the pure localEvent overflow is tested (HlcTests:33) but the store-layer bridge to the structured corrupt-clock(reason:saturated) is not; StoreTests covers corrupt-clock only via the UNREADABLE path (different message + reason:unreadable). A regression dropping the reason field or mis-mapping to .internal would pass. FIX: seed the clock at saturation (mintStamps replicaVal <physMax,logMax> physMax 1) and assert .corruptClock with (reason, .str saturated); note expectCode must be extended to assert context, not just code. Review Minor #12.
title: test: corrupt-clock(reason:saturated) store bridge in mintStamps is untested

description: Tl/Cli/Resolve.lean:70,76 — both spawns bypass runBounded, so a hung git-config (a config include firing a credential/exec helper, NFS-hung cwd) hangs every mutating verb indefinitely, inconsistent with the ADR-0014 effort to bound hung-git. They also run in the process cwd with no -C, so under --dir/TL_DIR a repo-LOCAL user.email is read from the cwd repo, not the resolved project (narrow: global gitconfig is cwd-independent). Writer-controlled => availability/robustness gap, not a boundary break. FIX: route both through a bounded runner (timeout -> next chain element / localhost) and pass -C <repoOf d>; cleanest is to lift the private runBounded into a shared shell helper. Review Minor #14.
title: correctness+security: resolveActor runs git/hostname with no timeout and in the process cwd

description: Tl/Sync/Ref.lean:283,285,312 — no --/--end-of-options before the resolved remote name; a name like --upload-pack=<cmd> (or --receive-pack= on push) yields arbitrary command execution (empirically reproduced). The name comes from local .git/config, which is BELOW the ADR-0014 trust boundary (config-write already grants code exec via core.fsmonitor/hooks) => zero new capability, not a boundary crossing. Defense-in-depth/wrapper-hygiene with a plausible social-engineering vector (copying a malicious tl.remote from a shared doc). FIX: add -- before remote in ls-remote/fetch and --end-of-options after flags in push, and/or reject a resolveRemote candidate starting with - at Remote.lean:48 (single point covering all three sites). Review Minor #15.
title: security(defense-in-depth): git remote name reaches ls-remote/fetch/push without a -- terminator

description: Tl/Store/Local.lean:71-77 — the .error arm (removeFile of the orphaned .tmp + mapSysError rethrow) prevents CSPRNG-suffixed temp files piling up under persistent rename failure; no StoreTests case forces it (the chmod-on-log-dir tests don't route through this rename). FIX: make rename over the clock/replica target fail (pre-create the target as a non-empty directory — works regardless of uid, unlike chmod which is bypassed under root) and assert a structured throw + no leftover .tmp. Review Minor #16.
title: test: writeLocalFile rename-failure temp-cleanup branch is untested

description: Tl/Store/Lock.lean:37-52 — the loop sleeps unconditionally after every failed attempt including the last; with attempts := timeoutMs/lockPollMs + 1, a 120ms timeout yields ~150ms (~25%) before throwing. Only inflates the contended-failure path (zero sleeps under no contention); the wait stays O(timeoutMs)-bounded so ADR-0015's guarantee holds — a budget-fidelity issue. FIX: skip the sleep transitioning into the terminal arm (if n==0 then throw else (sleep; loop n)). Review Minor #13.
title: correctness(minor): acquireLock overshoots the timeout by one poll interval

description: Tl/Store/Local.lean:71 — IO.FS.rename resolves intermediate path components with normal symlink following, unlike Sys.openNoFollow (validates every component); the module comment reasons only about the final component. Exploit window is tiny (the immediately-preceding temp open at :64 re-validates the identical parent prefix microseconds earlier, and the swapper needs mid-call write access to the validated .tl/local/ tree). FIX (proportionate): document in ADR-0015 §6 and the Local.lean:54-55/Paths.lean:83-84 comments that intermediate-component safety rests on the temp open having just validated the identical sibling prefix; stop implying the rename is fully guarded. A renameat-based no-follow shim parallel to mkdirNoFollow is the heavier alternative. Review Minor #11.
title: security+doc: atomic-replace rename bypasses the no-follow shim for intermediate path components

description: Tl/Store/Lock.lean:121-123 vs Tl/Store/Cache.lean:399 — materializeCached already decodes every segment (incl. the own one, which carries maxHlc) and discards the pairs; the next line re-runs decodeSegment sd true purely to re-extract the own segment's maxHlc on every mutation. The own segment is typically the largest local one; the two decodes differ only in skipBad, which cannot change maxHlc. Constant-factor 2x of one segment's parse. FIX: thread pairs (or just the own SegmentDecode) out of materializeCached and read its .maxHlc. Review Minor #4.
title: perf(minor): transact re-parses the entire own segment a second time for ownMax

description: A grab-bag of verified-but-minor nits; split out if any grows. (1) Tl/Store/Lock.lean:86 stamps := stamps ++ [...] O(n²) right-append (n small but uncapped via cmdCreate's 1+edgeCount) — cons-then-reverse. (2) Tl/Cli/Sanitize.lean:33-68 stripAnsi doesn't parse 8-bit C1 CSI/OSC introducers (0x9B/0x9D); isControl removes the introducer byte anyway so only inert literal residue remains (contract met) — optional belt-and-suspenders. (3) Tl/Crdt/Map.lean:233-234 AMap.merge generic O(|l2|·|result|); add a one-line doc-comment pointing batch callers to joinFast. (4) Tl/Kernel/CyclesFast.lean:61-64 sccWitnessesF fallback uses linear-scan assoc-list caches (super-quadratic) only when Tarjan's cert is rejected (tested not to occur) — add a one-line header note that the fallback cost is accepted as correctness-only. (5) Tl/Store/Local.lean:61-62 writeLocalFile doesn't verify Sys.entropy returned 8 bytes before the temp suffix (non-fatal; inconsistent with mintReplica/mintStamps) — optional consistency guard. Review nits.
title: nits: small comment/perf cleanups from the review (low impact, individually optional)

description: Tests/PerfTests.lean:193 benches readyFast at reps=1 so its small-scale time sits under the 30ms ratioRow floor — the ×12 growth assertion is effectively disabled for this row (floor-masked). The createdAt ranking-key read is now hoisted (State.createdAtH, O(1)-amortized via the createdAtH_eq bridge), so createdAtOf no longer contributes superlinearity to keyOf. The SOLE remaining masking driver is weightFast (Tl/Kernel/ReadyFast.lean:148-150 + comment 143-147): the per-cone blocks-reachability is O(V+E) but recomputed independently per ready candidate with NO cross-candidate shared-cone memo, so the rank phase is O(R·(V+E)) — still superlinear (~11x for x4 ops). ADR-0023 forbids honestly un-masking a still-superlinear row, so the row stays at reps=1 for now. DO: once weightFast shares/memoizes the blocks-cone across candidates (the cross-candidate residual left by tl-whp0's per-cone adjacency index), raise the rdy row's reps above the 30ms floor (like prov/row/canon at 800/1200/2500) so the x12 ratio actually bites; the x12 threshold and 30ms floor stay unchanged — only the rep count moves. Discovered while hoisting the createdAt half (code-review Major #2).
title: De-mask the readyFast 'fast ready queue' perf row once weightFast is near-linear

description: ADR-0025 (planned extension). The human `tl log` line shows timestamp, op, actor, and target id(s) but not the issue title, so a human cannot tell what each op touched without a lookup. Add each target's current materialized title to the human line: sanitized (attacker-controllable, ADR-0014, as the actor column already is), truncated to a sensible width (match `tl list`), and read through the indexed view (ADR-0024 / ViewIndex), not an O(N) issueData find per op (ADR-0023). Fall back to the bare id for a dangling or untitled target. The `--json` entry stays id-keyed with no title: the feed is an immutable op stream and the title is mutable state derivable from the id — a deliberate human/json divergence recorded in ADR-0025 (the allowed exception to the cli-human-json-parity rule). Tested shell, no kernel theorem: assert the human line carries the title and the json entry does not. Site: Tl/Cli/Commands.lean cmdLog `line` renderer.
title: tl log: show the target title in the human output

description: ADR-0025 (planned extension; the retrofit-hostile one — land it before any consumer depends on the current string `cursor`). Add `--until <cursor>`: ops before the cursor, newest-first, for backward history browsing. Change the `tl log` response `cursor` from a string to an object `{since: <resume-forward>, until: <resume-back>}` so each page is self-navigating — pass `cursor.since` to `--since` to continue forward, `cursor.until` to `--until` to page older; field names match the flags. `--since C1 --until C2` composes into a bounded window. Default `--limit`: `--since` drains (0 = all), `--until` pages (default like plain log, since it browses history). Semantics: `--since` (forward) is exactly-once; `--until` (backward) is best-effort, not exactly-once — a still-merging CRDT log can gain an op below where a backward page already passed; document it. Design subtlety: the before-edge cursor is the per-replica frontier just below the oldest delivered op; at a boundary HLC shared by two replicas the per-replica thresholds differ by the (hlc, replica, nonce) tie-break — specify and test it. Reuse the (HLC, nonce) version-vector cursor and its parse/render/validate from --since. Tested shell: a window, backward-paging resume, the {since,until} shape, the boundary tie-break. Wire via Grammar (a --until FlagSpec) + Main + cmdLog. Built on tl-nkdv.
title: tl log --until + dual {since,until} cursor (backward paging)

description: ADR-0025 (planned extension). Let `--since`/`--until` accept a duration (`1h`, `30m`, `7d`), a date (`2026-06-20`), or an ISO timestamp in addition to a version-vector cursor, so a human can browse recent activity without a saved token. Add `--last N` (count tail) and `--since all` (explicit from-start). Time values are best-effort over physical wall-clock (skew-sensitive); the cursor stays the exact, resumable form for machines. Reuse the single shared duration/date grammar — do not mint a second parser: the grammar is decided in tl-r9y7 (tz, bare-date base, duration units), shared with `defer --for/--until`; extend `Time.parseDurationMs?`. Dispatch by value shape (a `replica:hlc:nonce` cursor vs a `1h` duration vs an ISO date) with teaching usage errors. Tested shell. Blocked by tl-r9y7 (the grammar decision) and the --until task (the time selectors apply to both --since and --until).
title: tl log relative time selectors: --since/--until <duration|date>, --last N

description: Code implementation of the freeze-sensitive design decisions resolved 2026-06-21 (recorded in the ADR-0013/0008/0001/0006 amendments under the decisions epic). The decisions are pinned; this epic tracks the downstream CLI / kernel / codec / test work. Each child carries its plan and file refs. The tasks are largely independent (parallelizable); the one shared concern is the cacheVersion bump, owned by the reopen-clears-assignee task and reused if the update-drops-assignee task co-lands.
title: Implement the pinned freeze-sensitive decisions

description: Implement the ADR-0013 (2026-06-21 amendment) actor/assignee split: the provenance flag becomes `--actor` (matching the `TL_ACTOR` env form). Sites: `Tl/Cli/Grammar.lean:53` (actorFlag name "assignee" -> "actor", and its summary), `Tl/Cli/Resolve.lean:11` (doc) + `:68` (resolveActor), `Tl/Cli/Main.lean:94` (a.get? "assignee" -> "actor"). TL_ACTOR is unchanged. This frees `--assignee` for the assignee read filter (`--assignee me` on ready/list), whose grammar is tracked under the open list-facet-flags decision and is not built here. Breaking CLI change; pre-1.0, note it in the change. Shell-tier: update the `Tests/CliTests.lean` cases that pass `--assignee` as the actor passthrough to `--actor`. Refs ADR-0013/0008.
title: Rename the provenance flag to --actor; free --assignee for the read filter

description: Implement the claim-only-assignee rule (ADR-0008 2026-06-21 amendment / ADR-0013), update half: make `assignee` non-settable via `update`. Three-site Codec change in `Tl/Format/Codec.lean`: (1) `:328` remove "assignee" from the consumedKeys "update" arm; (2) `:291-292` gate the decodeScalars assignee reader so update does not read it (e.g. an allowAssignee flag: true from the create decode arm, false from update); (3) `:175-176` extend stripLifecycle to clear assignee on the update render path (render/decode symmetry). An update record still carrying assignee then preserves it in the unknown bag and is never applied (additive, no log v bump). No cacheVersion bump needed alone (no-op on existing folds: zero update-with-assignee ops in any log). Tests: re-pin `Tests/CodecTests.lean:50-51` (the update canonical line carries assignee:dana) and add a decode-into-unknown-bag test. Refs ADR-0008:119.
title: Drop assignee from the update op (assignee claim-only)

description: Implement reopen-clears-assignee (ADR-0008 reopen delta + ADR-0013). `Tl/Format/Codec.lean:190-191` (WireOp.toOp .reopen arm): add `assignee := some none` so the reopen delta clears assignee alongside closeResolution. Decide the cmdReopen guard (`Tl/Cli/Commands.lean:903`): reopen of an already-open issue is a no-op today, so an already-open assigned issue would not be cleared - either document "reopen clears assignee as part of closed->open" or widen the guard. This changes the WireOp.toOp fold, so bump `Tl.Store.cacheVersion` (`Cache.lean:68`) 2->3 and re-pin the guard digest at `Tests/CacheTests.lean:506-507` (the guard fails by construction: corpus has claim alice -> reopen idA). Fix `Tests/CliTests.lean:685-701` (the reopen-keeps-assignee fixture: eve no longer survives the higher-stamped reopen) and add a positive test. Verified safe against the live log: changes the materialized assignee only of reopened issues with no later claim (the one currently-open such issue becomes unassigned) - intended; no log v bump. This single cacheVersion bump also covers the update-drops-assignee change if co-landed. Refs ADR-0008:122.
title: reopen clears assignee (kernel fold + cacheVersion bump)

description: Implement claim --steal stale-claim takeover (ADR-0013 2026-06-21 amendment). Add `--steal` and `--stale <duration>` flags to the claim command in `Tl/Cli/Grammar.lean`; in cmdClaim (`Tl/Cli/Commands.lean` ~705) add a staleness courtesy guard: with --steal, succeed on an already-claimed item only when the existing claim is stale by now - claimedAt against an inline `--stale <dur>` or the `tl.staleAfter` git config (no default). It writes an ordinary claim (status in_progress, the stealer as assignee, a fresh claimedAt). The staleness test is a local courtesy guard, never merge-enforced (concurrent steals reconcile via LWW; the loser sees superseded). Error paths (teach via code + message): not-claimable when claimed-and-not-stale (report remaining time); usage when --steal is given but no threshold is set; --steal on an unclaimed or own item behaves as a plain claim. Reuse the ADR-0010 duration grammar (Time.parseDurationMs?). doctor may suggest claim --steal for its stale-claim rows. Shell-tier tests per branch. Refs ADR-0013.
title: Implement claim --steal stale-claim takeover

description: Implement init --stealth (ADR-0001 section 7): local-only task state with zero repo-visible trace. Add `--stealth` to the init command (`Tl/Cli/Grammar.lean` init spec + cmdInit in `Tl/Cli/Main.lean`). It creates `.tl/` + self-ignore + replica + clock + segment as normal, but does not configure the refs/tl/log refspec, does not push/fetch, does not offer auto-sync, and does not offer the committed discovery pointer (ADR-0011). `tl sync` in a stealth repo fails with the reserved `stealth-mode` error code (ADR-0008, currently no trigger) explaining how to un-stealth. Sole spelling: no `--local` alias, no env default (decided 2026-06-21). Un-stealthing needs no data migration (configure the refspec, snapshot the local segments into refs/tl/log, sync). Shell-tier tests. Refs ADR-0001 section 7.
title: Implement init --stealth (local-only; stealth-mode error trigger)

description: Implement the git >= 2.17 runtime-floor check (ADR-0006, Runtime prerequisite: git). In doctor and init, parse `git --version` (the stable `git version X.Y.Z` line) and emit a teaching warning below 2.17 rather than letting an older git fail cryptically. Add a CI job pinned to git 2.17 that runs the suite, so a future plumbing dependency above the floor cannot slip in unnoticed (the only feature tl uses above the ~1.8 era is rev-parse --git-common-dir at 2.5; no git worktree shell-out). Shell-tier tests for the version parse and the below-floor warning. Refs ADR-0006.
title: doctor/init git >= 2.17 version check + CI floor pin

description: Spun out of tl-dk1 (git >=2.17 floor, ADR-0006). The runtime doctor/init check shipped (Tl.Sync.parseGitVersion/gitMeetsFloor/gitVersion + cmdDoctor gitVersion row + cmdInit below-floor note, all tested). REMAINING (this task): a CI job pinned to git 2.17 that runs the suite, so a future plumbing dependency above the floor cannot slip in unnoticed. BLOCKED-IN-FACT: the repo currently has NO CI infrastructure at all (no .github/workflows, no CI runner). This task = stand up CI from scratch (runner choice, how the whole lake build + tltest suite runs in CI, then the 2.17-pinned matrix entry). Larger than a flag add; needs the CI platform decision first. Refs ADR-0006 'CI pins and tests the floor version'.
title: CI job pinned to the git 2.17 floor

description: Spun out of the bulk-import build (tl-kqbcw). cmdImport enforces the TOTAL-input-size bound (default 5MB, gated by --allow-large/--max), which is the load-bearing safety net (it transitively caps every field/label/edge). ADR-0005 §bounds also lists finer granular bounds not yet enforced: per-field byte size (title/description/notes), label/meta key+value size, parent-chain depth, and per-record edge count — each gated by the same --allow-large/--max, every truncation/skip disclosed (ADR-0014 T6). These give better error messages and finer control than the coarse total bound. Build in Tl/Import/Bulk.lean (the parse/build path) + tests. Refs ADR-0005, ADR-0014 T6.
title: Import: granular resource bounds (per-field / label / depth / edge-count)

description: Review suggestion (maintainability, not a bug): cmdList has grown several order-sensitive boolean/optional facets (--all, --label, --stale, --deferred), each a sequential filter + a comment-preserved effClosed-gate bypass + a summary-precedence branch. It's fine for now but close to wanting a small ListFacets/ListOptions struct (or a facet list with a uniform predicate + bypass flag) so future facets don't rely on comments to preserve semantics. No behavior change — pure refactor; pin it with the existing CliTests output staying byte-identical. Defer until the next list facet lands (e.g. tl-hwn6s9 --status/--assignee/--priority, gated on the tl-3qtz spelling decision) so they're designed together. Refs Tl/Cli/Commands.lean cmdList.
title: Refactor cmdList facets into a small helper (option-order resilience)

description: Deferred from the tl-3qtz facet-freeze decision (ADR-0020 amendment 2026-06-25). The structured list facets (--status/--assignee/--priority/--blocked) froze; free-text --text was cut from that freeze because it carries its own open design questions and is the one filter a consumer trivially reproduces client-side (tl list --json | jq/grep). It is a pure additive flag later — redefines nothing frozen. Open questions to settle when built: which fields (title only vs title+description+notes), substring vs word-boundary, case folding (recommend case-insensitive default), and whether repeats AND. Build over the already-materialized View in cmdList (Tl/Cli/Commands.lean), same sequential-filter pattern as --label; update the vision grammar block + tl help + CliTests. Refs ADR-0020 (list facet amendment), vision.md §list facets.
title: list --text free-text search facet

description: 10 shipped verb groups (13 subcommands) emit forever-contract --json payloads recorded nowhere: unblocks, dep path, dep critical, dep relate, dep unrelate, defer, undefer, reopen, meta set/get/clear/list, import. (sync IS pinned already -- ADR-0016:77-84; do not re-pin.) ADR-0020's own rule (:412-414, "pin their shapes when built") is unmet; the JSON surface freezes at first release, so this must precede 0.1.0. Front-load the genuine shape inventions: meta get/list, the import summary object (ADR-0005 names "the import summary" with no shape), unblocks, dep path/critical. defer/undefer/reopen likely follow the already-pinned mutating-verb echo convention (ADR-0020:144-145 "exactly as create") -- near-one-line pins, but verify against actual command output first. Deliverable: ADR-0020 body additions matching the shipped bytes (present tense, no dated amendment section) plus freeze/drift tests in the style of the existing shape pins. Found and verified by the 2026-07-01 gap sweep (binary surface + ADR header scan cross-checked).
title: Pin ADR-0020 JSON shapes for the shipped-but-unpinned verbs

Prune the resolved import section (:79-102) and the resolved discovery-pointer row (:72-77 -- decided AND implemented: ADR-0011:151-157, Commands.lean:2073-2077, closed task).

From the verified 2026-07-01 gap sweep.

description: ADR-0006 promises the release machinery; none of it is built and no task tracked it (tl-y02y covers only the three decisions; the CI task is the correctness gate, not the release matrix). Scope, to decompose into children when picked up: release.yml build matrix (darwin-arm64 + linux-x86_64 MVP per ADR-0006:85-92; the old-glibc build base applies to release binaries only), Sigstore/cosign signing + SLSA/GitHub attestation run DIRECTLY in release.yml (a reusable signing workflow changes the certificate SAN via job_workflow_ref and breaks the identity pin -- see the tl-y02y verifier decision), SHA256SUMS + per-asset Sigstore bundles, the curl|sh installer with the embedded verifier pin + VERIFYING.md identity-history table, the npm veneer under @taskloop/tl (ADR-0006:88 / ADR-0014:159 still say @tl/cli-* -- stale, fix in the ADR), the Homebrew formula (a fourth pin home; add a drift-guard test keeping all pin copies identical), and tl version --json build provenance (ADR-0006:112-115, deferred-not-dropped). Settle the final repo org/name BEFORE the first signed release -- a later rename rotates the signing identity immediately. description:
Rewrite README.md so it presents tl as a usable product rather than an implementation ledger.

Goals:
- Lead with the agent problem and a concise value proposition: a git-native task tracker for coding agents with a formally verified core.
- Show a real, currently working agent loop near the top, preferably with representative command output.
- Verify every command and flag mentioned against Tl/Cli/Grammar.lean and the machine-checked Shipped CLI surface in docs/vision.md.
- Replace the stale opening status dump with a short, accurate alpha/current-availability note. Do not describe shipped workflows such as import, defer, unblocks, dep path, dep critical, meta, or richer list filters as planned.
- Present the proved / tested / trusted boundary in a compact table and link to docs/overview.md for theorem-level detail.
- Preserve the important limitation that claims are not distributed locks: disconnected agents may briefly duplicate work, while synchronization resolves state without corruption.
- Explain refs/tl/log and the append-only CRDT architecture with a small diagram; keep detailed OR-Set, LWW, stamp, and fold mechanics in linked architecture documentation.
- Replace the speculative Install section with accurate build-from-source instructions, clearly labeling the project alpha and prebuilt/package-manager distribution as future work.
- Merge or tighten the Why and Why not just sections, while retaining the candid point that a TODO file is sufficient for a handful of independent tasks.
- Move detailed command, theorem, stage, and platform inventories into linked documentation. Reduce migration coverage to a concise statement now that import ships.

Acceptance criteria:
- The opening communicates the problem, audience, and differentiator before implementation status.
- The quick-start commands work with the current binary.
- All availability and shipped-feature claims match the current grammar and documentation.
- The verification language does not overclaim beyond docs/overview.md.
- The README remains concise, candid, and useful to someone encountering tl for the first time.
- No product behavior or scope is changed.
title: Rewrite README as the product front door

description: Prevent inherited Git routing variables from making tl read, publish, or refresh another repository. Route every shelled Git command through one environment-scrubbing baseline that removes GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_COMMON_DIR, GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY, GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES, GIT_INDEX_FILE, and GIT_NAMESPACE while retaining authentication/configuration variables and GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES. Refuse init in a bare repository with a teaching usage error, retain bare repositories as remotes, stop filesystem discovery at a bare-gitdir boundary, and add a doctor split-brain check comparing filesystem discovery with Git classification. Cover every Git spawn path, including timeout configuration reads, plus inherited-environment, bare-repository, boundary, doctor, and error-path tests. Record the policy in ADR-0012.
title: Isolate git subprocesses from inherited repository-routing environment

description: Ratify and document the fail-closed identity used to verify release artifacts before the first release. Pin the exact GitHub Actions OIDC issuer and an anchored certificate-identity expression that fixes the final repository slug, release workflow path, and version-tag ref pattern. Require Rekor inclusion and per-asset Sigstore bundles; define the explicit signature-skip escape so SHA-256 verification remains mandatory. Specify direct signing in release.yml, identity rotation, historical artifact verification, and the canonical pin locations in the installer, VERIFYING.md, Homebrew formula, and ADR-0006/ADR-0014. Settle the final repository organization/name and package scope first, then add a drift guard that keeps every operative pin copy identical. Do not add self-verification to tl doctor.
title: Pin signed-release verifier identity and rotation policy

description: Implement detect-and-warn network-filesystem policy without refusing operation or probing on every lock acquisition. Add a native fstatfs probe that opens its own no-follow descriptor and a pure, exhaustively tested classifier for local, definitely remote, and ambiguous filesystems on Darwin and Linux, including FUSE, 9p, WSL, and vboxsf cases. Surface the result as a doctor row and an init note; init probes the target parent because the state directory does not exist yet. Probe failures make no claim rather than blocking. Teaching warnings must direct users toward a local clone or explicit --dir/TL_DIR placement. Record the policy and platform assumptions in ADR-0015, update the native-shim license/ABI documentation if required, and test every classifier and shell error branch.
title: Detect network filesystems and teach safer placement

description: ADR-0001 §7 specifies un-stealthing (stealth → shared: configure the +refs/tl/log:refs/tl/log refspec, snapshot the local .tl/log/* segments into refs/tl/log, run tl sync; no data migration, same format and ids), but the only user-facing surface is the stealth-mode error message on tl sync. Verify the stealth-mode error message points at this guide. Consider whether a single tl command should automate the conversion — if deliberately excluded, record the exclusion in ADR-0001 rather than spinning out a deferred task.
title: Document the un-stealth conversion for users

description:
Verified findings from a 2026-07-14 concurrency audit of the kernel proof contract. Each finding was independently re-verified against commit a998c55 (8 adversarial verifiers, all confirmed; corrections folded into the child tasks). Scope: honest post-merge command-outcome reporting (claim/close), explicit OR-Set concurrency theorems (add-wins/re-add; corrected cycle-repair termination), element-scoped OR-Set tombstones (eliminates the unrelate stamp-uniqueness discharge — the single live tier-3 residual in docs/overview.md), an --append-notes concurrency-semantics decision, and the canonical-parent projection (tag-universe spec fix + kernel move).

File:line references in child tasks are against a998c55 — re-locate by symbol if drifted. Three tasks carry PROPOSED design decisions pending ratification (claim outcome wire contract; append-notes LWW-vs-grow-only; canonical-parent observed-vs-live tags); ratify before or when starting each.

Not filed (verified, no action needed): build hygiene — lake build green (1382 jobs), no sorry/admit/axiom declarations under Tl/, overview.md theorem inventory accurate.
title: Multi-replica conflict-reporting and CRDT hardening

description:
docs/design-backlog.md:29-34 ("Cycle-breaking progress / termination [low]") claims that removing one kind-k edge between members of any SCC witness strictly reduces the cyclic-SCC set, bounding the `dep cycles` -> `dep remove` loop by <= #SCCs steps. Both claims are false on arbitrary states, and such states are locally reachable because cycles are reported, never write-rejected (Tl/Cli/Commands.lean:1505-1507):

- Chord counterexample: A->B->C->A plus chord A->C. Removing the chord (an in-witness edge) leaves `cycles s k` literally unchanged — strict reduction fails under every measure (set of SCCs, flattened node set, count).
- Bound counterexample: the complete digraph on 3 nodes is 1 SCC but needs 3 removals (min feedback arc set), breaking the <= #SCCs bound independently.
- Non-monotone: one SCC can split into two cyclic SCCs (A<->B, C<->D, B->C, C->A; remove C->A), so the cyclic-SCC count can increase.

Rewrite the bullet to the provable form: (a) each removal of a present in-witness kind-k edge strictly decreases the present kind-k edge count and cannot create a cycle; (b) SCC refinement — every cyclic SCC after a removal is a subset of a prior one; (c) hence the repair loop terminates in <= (# present kind-k edges with both endpoints inside some reported witness) effective steps; while a witness is nonempty, a present in-witness edge exists. State the hypotheses explicitly: no concurrent kind-k edgeAdd at all (not merely "no re-add" — the OR-Set does not distinguish add from re-add; both are fresh-tag adds), and each remove tombstones every live tag of its edge (the CLI's well-formed shape, obs = s.edges.tagsOf e, Commands.lean:1386-1389). Optionally note the <= #SCCs bound does hold in the special case where every cyclic SCC is a single simple cycle.

Also correct the misleading repair hint while here: `dep cycles`' human line "break each with `tl dep remove`" (Tl/Cli/Commands.lean:605) is Blocks-specific advice also shown for Parent-kind witnesses (those are broken with `parent remove`/`parent set`).

No ADR change needed: ADR-0004 claims only report correctness, not repair-loop termination — the false claim lives solely in the backlog. Scope: the backlog bullet + one hint string. Proving the corrected statement is the follow-on task blocked on this one.
title: Correct the false cycle-breaking termination claim in the design backlog

description:
Graduate the backlog item at docs/design-backlog.md:35-39: ADR-0002 states add-wins and re-addability in prose; elevate them to stated theorems in Tl/Crdt/OrSet.lean so the `dep remove`/`unrelate` guarantee is a theorem rather than a consequence left implicit in the join laws.

Theorems: (1) add-wins — an add whose tag a concurrent remove did not observe survives the merge (Present holds after joining the remove's tombstone delta); (2) re-add — after a remove that observed all prior tags, a fresh-tag add makes the element Present again (not a 2P-set).

Current structure (a998c55): adds : AMap alpha (FinSet Stamp), removed : FinSet Stamp (one global set); Present s e := exists p in (s.tagsOf e).toList, p.1 not-in s.removed (Tl/Crdt/OrSet.lean:28-57); tombstone deltas built by OrSet.tombstones obs (OrSet.lean:49) from Op.edgeRemove / Op.labelRemove (Tl/Kernel/Op.lean:48,97,99).

Add-wins *distinctness* (two concurrent adds staying distinct) additionally leans on the carried nonce/stamp-uniqueness assumption (OrSet.lean:62-65; overview Trusted) — state the theorems so any such reliance is an explicit hypothesis, never silent.

Coordination: the element-scoped-tombstones task (related) restructures `removed` into a per-element map. Whichever lands first, the other restates over the new shape — cheap either way; do not block on it. When landing: cite the theorem names from the ADR-0002 prose and remove the backlog bullet (items leave the backlog by graduating). Completion report: theorem names + #print axioms check.
title: State and prove explicit OR-Set add-wins and re-add theorems

description:
Defect (verified @a998c55): cmdClaim decides its outcome from the assignee register alone — won := (vFinal.state.issueData i).assignee.value.getD none == some actor (Tl/Cli/Commands.lean:1117-1118; the same assignee-only comparison is duplicated in show's claimBlock, 487-489). claim lowers to ONE kernel op writing status+assignee at one stamp (WireOp.toOp -> Op.setFields {status := some .InProgress, assignee := some (some assignee)}, Tl/Format/Codec.lean:187-188), but close writes status+closeResolution and never assignee (Codec.lean:189-191). So a concurrent close that outstamps the claim flips status to Done/Cancelled while the claim keeps the assignee LWW — and claim reports outcome "won" / "Claimed ..." on a closed issue. ADR-0013:104-118 acknowledges the independent-register anomaly (its worked example is the inverse, open-but-assigned); docs/overview.md:249 documents the superseded signal as assignee-only.

Fix: derive the outcome from BOTH registers — full win = status holds (stamp, InProgress) from this claim's write AND assignee holds (stamp, some actor). Real symbols: State.issueData (Tl/Kernel/State.lean:227); IssueData.status : Reg Status / assignee : Reg (Option String) (State.lean:95-97); Reg V = Option (Stamp x V), Reg.write, merge = optCombine tmax (Tl/Crdt/Lww.lean:26-39); Stamp totally ordered lex on (hlc, replica, nonce) (Tl/Crdt/Order.lean:240-242). Kernel: add a claimWon predicate + decidable form and prove (a) applying the claim delta establishes it when its stamp dominates both registers; (b) merges preserve exactly won-vs-superseded; (c) a partial win (assignee won, status lost) is distinguishable and never satisfies the full-win predicate. CLI branches on the decidable form: kernel side proved, CLI branch tested (ADR-0004 tiering).

Decision to ratify in this change: claim.outcome in {won, superseded} is an agent-branching wire contract (ADR-0013). Options: (A) keep it binary — fold a partial win into "superseded" with a message that teaches (assignee kept, status lost, what to do next); no wire change. (B) add a third value (e.g. "partial") — a wire-surface change; document in ADR-0013 + the skill. PROPOSED: A (smallest honest contract).

Tests in the same change: a foreign close outstamping a fresh claim (via foreignLine; cf. the superseded-close block pattern, Tests/CliTests.lean:1247-1263 — existing coverage pins only assignee supersession per overview.md:249). Docs in the same change: ADR-0013 claim-only-assignee bullet; overview.md:249 signal row; human and --json surfaces must disclose the same outcome (parity). Exit contract unchanged: superseded stays exit 0; not-claimable stays 14. Completion report: theorem names + #print axioms check.
title: claim: derive the won outcome from both status and assignee registers

description:
Make cross-element tombstone interference unrepresentable, eliminating the last live tier-3 carried discharge.

Today OrSet keeps ONE global removed : FinSet Stamp with no element identity (Tl/Crdt/OrSet.lean:28-32; Present probes it globally, 56-57), and Op.delta discards the element the op already carries (edgeRemove _ obs / labelRemove id _ obs -> OrSet.tombstones obs, Tl/Kernel/Op.lean:48,97,99; OrSet.lean:49). Consequence: the proved boundary theorems ready/effectiveStatus_edgeRemove_of_undisturbed (Tl/Kernel/Frame.lean:456,464) have their undisturbed-views hypotheses discharged for a well-formed unrelate only via the tier-3 stamp-uniqueness assumption — the single live residual (docs/overview.md:175, 211-219, 266; Frame.lean:368-372).

Change removal storage to removed : AMap alpha (FinSet Stamp), mirroring adds (the project's List-backed AMap/FinSet — no Mathlib Finset, per CLAUDE.md). The unrelate frame lemma then becomes provable unconditionally — even against malformed/adversarial observed payloads, since the edge kind is part of the element key (Edge = IssueId x IssueId x EdgeKind, Tl/Kernel/State.lean:87; ADR-0002:33-35) — strictly stronger than what honest-stamp uniqueness gives.

No wire/log change: Op.edgeRemove already carries the Edge and labelRemove the Label; the record codec and change feed serialize ops, and the ADR-0008 snapshot is reserved/unbuilt. Work list: (1) Tl/Crdt/OrSet.lean — tombstonesAt (e : alpha) (obs), removedOf, Present, presentElements + lemmas, merge (removed leg becomes AMap.merge FinSet.union), re-discharge merge_comm/assoc/idem/empty via the existing AMap lemmas exactly as the adds leg does, ext, presentElements_mergeAdd_filter; add the removal workhorse (a tombstone delta keyed at e0 with not (P e0) leaves the P-filtered presentElements fixed — AMap.find_merge/find_singleton exist). (2) Tl/Kernel/Op.lean — delta uses the carried element; labelRemoveData gains the label parameter. (3) Tl/Kernel/FoldFast.lean — foldl_merge_removed + the joinFast removed leg become the FinSet.union form; re-prove joinFast_eq. (4) Tl/Kernel/Frame.lean — supersede the of_undisturbed pair with unconditional ready_unrelate / effectiveStatus_unrelate for EdgeKind.Related; update module comments (368-372, 434-437). (5) State.merge_comm/assoc/idem re-discharge through the new OrSet lemmas (statements unchanged).

Serialization: only the gitignored self-invalidating fold cache — encOrSet's "r" leg becomes an AMap-of-FinSet encoding like "a" (Tl/Store/Cache.lean:144-151); bump cacheVersion 3 -> 4 (Cache.lean:68) with the bump-guard test (Tests/CacheTests.lean) and codec-branch rows in the same change (Definition-of-Done #4).

Behavior: unchanged on well-formed logs (obs is always the element's own tags — Commands.lean:1389,1483,1532,1563); differs only under cross-element stamp collision or adversarial obs, which is the point.

Docs in the same change: docs/overview.md — frame-lemma paragraph (156-171), residual preamble (173-176), DELETE the unrelate-discharge bullet (211-219), trim the unrelate clause from the Trusted nonce-uniqueness entry (266 — the entry itself STAYS, for issue-id derivation and add-wins distinctness, OrSet.lean:62-65), and the perf row's per-tag tombstone-probe cost note (250); docs/adr/ADR-0002-minimal-crdt.md remove-semantics wording (line 43 — now element-scoped); docs/codebase-map.md OrSet annotation (24) + nonce-uniqueness row (397).

Coordination: the add-wins/re-add theorems task (related) states its theorems over whichever removed-shape lands first. Completion report: restated/new theorem names + #print axioms check.
title: Element-scoped OR-Set tombstones: retire the unrelate stamp-uniqueness discharge

description:
Decision task: the behavior is disclosed in code but recorded in no decision document.

Verified @a998c55: --append-notes is a CLI-side read-modify-write into the single whole-string notes LWW register — it reads the materialized notes, joins with "\n", writes the whole string back as one LWW value (Tl/Cli/Commands.lean:1209-1244; IssueData.notes : Reg (Option String), Tl/Kernel/State.lean:99). Two appends racing across replicas resolve by the LWW triple and the loser's contribution is dropped wholesale — on diverged bases, MORE than one line can vanish. The code already takes a position: the doc-comment calls serial accumulation "exactly the intended accumulate" and prescribes sync-between-writes; the help string discloses "read-modify-write; not atomic under concurrent writers" (Tl/Cli/Grammar.lean:133). But no ADR records it: ADR-0002:49-53 records notes as an LWW scalar and ADR-0008:120 routes notes through update/setFields; nothing anywhere documents append semantics or the lost-update race. Tl.Sync.preWriteRefresh narrows but does not close the race.

Decide and record (fold into the ADR-0002 or ADR-0008 body, present tense — no dated amendment sections):

(A) Ratify the status quo: notes stay one LWW register; concurrent appenders sync between writes; record the race and the rationale (single serial agent loop is the documented primary use) as an accepted limitation. No code change; cheapest; keeps the state model minimal.

(B) Redesign: a grow-only tagged note-entry collection (pattern: labels, State.lean:103) + merge laws wired into the IssueData.merge proofs + kernel theorems (both concurrent appends retained; merge/order/duplication independence; deterministic stamp-order rendering; every accepted append exactly once) + wire payload (ADR-0008 record schema, Tl/Format/Codec.lean) + CLI rendering + an explicit definition of the --notes full-replacement interaction — replacement is not expressible grow-only, so B must drop --notes, add a tombstone/clear design, or use LWW-of-collection. Multi-agent-correct but a state-model and wire-surface expansion.

PROPOSED: A now (primary use is serial; the disclosure already teaches the workaround), reopening B if multi-agent note accumulation becomes a real workflow. If B is chosen, spin its implementation out as its own task — this task's deliverable is the ratified decision in the ADR plus aligning the Commands.lean doc-comment and Grammar.lean help text with the recorded decision. Existing tests cover serial seed/join + mutual exclusion only (Tests/CliTests.lean:287-301); A adds no code so no new tests; B ships with its full proof+test suite.
title: Decide and document --append-notes concurrency semantics

description:
ADR-0003 section 4 (docs/adr/ADR-0003-relations-cycles-rollup.md:126-132) specifies the canonical display parent: concurrent reparenting converges to multiple surviving parent edges (reported, never rejected), and display derives the canonical one deterministically — the surviving edge greatest in (HLC, replica-id, nonce). The implementation lives entirely in the CLI shell (Tl/Cli/Project.lean): maxTagOf (396), canonicalParentCore (404), spec form canonicalParent (424), production form canonicalParentE (432) over ViewIndex buckets; consumers are show's render (Tl/Cli/Render.lean:238), the tree's isRoot (Tl/Cli/Commands.lean:443), and the JSON parent field (Project.lean:497). It is only test-pinned: canonicalParentTieTests (Tests/CliTests.lean:1935) and the rowAccessorAgreementTests conjunct (2041); no kernel symbol or theorem exists.

SPEC BUG, resolve first (found in verification; the audit missed it): maxTagOf maximizes over ALL OBSERVED add-tags (AMap.keys (s.edges.tagsOf e)) with NO filter against OrSet.removed — despite its own docstring and ADR-0003 both saying "surviving". An edge present only via a low surviving tag still ranks by a tombstoned higher tag (reachable: concurrent same-edge adds + a remove that observed only the greater tag). Decide observed-max (current behavior; correct the docstrings + ADR wording) vs live-max (what the ADR promises; a behavior change needing new test rows). PROPOSED: live-max.

Then move the projection kernel-side following the ADR-0024 section-3 bridge pattern (spec def + fast def + pointwise bridge, cf. effStatusWith_eq, Tl/Kernel/RollupFast.lean:651) and prove: (a) the selected parent is the `from` of a Present parent edge to i (edge presence only — the parent id itself may be dangling, Tl/Kernel/State.lean:241-244); (b) the winner's max tag >= every candidate's, over the ratified tag universe; (c) candidate-enumeration-order invariance — needs a pairwise-distinct-max-tags hypothesis (stamp uniqueness is the carried ADR-0007 assumption; equal stamps currently prefer the later-enumerated candidate, Project.lean:418) OR an id tie-break mirroring the LWW equal-stamp value tie-break (Tl/Crdt/Order.lean:250-251) to make it unconditional; (d) canonicalParentE = canonicalParent pointwise for present issues — needs a hasIssue hypothesis (production candidates come from child-present State.parentEdges, RollupFast.lean:47-50, while spec State.parentsOf, State.lean:268, does not filter) and a proved Edge-keyed hash-probe lemma edgeTags[e]?.getD empty = state.edges.tagsOf e (today asserted only in a comment, Project.lean:352-354; the HashMapView lemmas are IssueId-keyed, so this is new work).

Also retire the byte-identical shell twin Tl.Cli.parentEdgesFast (Project.lean:149) in favor of the proved kernel State.parentEdgesFast (RollupFast.lean:56-62) — the proven-fast form replaces the duplicate. New kernel defs go in a module imported by Tl.lean (root-module rule). Docs in the same change: ADR-0003 section 4 + ADR-0024 (ratified tag universe + tie-break), codebase-map annotation, overview theorem inventory. The existing CLI test pins stay as shell-composition regression. Completion report: theorem names + #print axioms check.
title: Canonical parent: fix the tag-universe spec, move the projection into the kernel, prove it

description:
Graduate the corrected cycle-repair backlog obligation (see the blocking doc-correction task for the counterexamples that killed the original SCC-measured form) into kernel theorems.

Statement shape, over State.cycles / State.sccWitnesses / State.onCycle / State.kindSucc / State.hasCycle (Tl/Kernel/Cycles.lean:35-90): under (i) no concurrent kind-k Op.edgeAdd and (ii) each Op.edgeRemove carrying every live tag of its edge (the CLI's well-formed obs = s.edges.tagsOf e, Tl/Cli/Commands.lean:1386-1389), each effective repair step strictly decreases the present kind-k edge count and creates no new cycle; every cyclic SCC after a removal is a subset of a prior cyclic SCC (refinement); hence the `dep cycles` -> `dep remove` loop reaches `hasCycle s k = false` in at most |present kind-k edges internal to reported witnesses| effective steps. Progress obligation: while a witness is nonempty, a present in-witness kind-k edge exists (a non-present pair is an explicit noop, Commands.lean:1386-1387 — not an effective step).

Existing supports: mem_flatten_cycles_iff / cycles_same_witness_iff (Tl/Kernel/SccProps.lean:201-211); the cyclesFast bridge (Tl/Kernel/CyclesFast.lean:482-491); Op.edgeRemove delta = OrSet.tombstones obs (Tl/Kernel/Op.lean:48,97); OrSet.Present / tagsOf (Tl/Crdt/OrSet.lean:52-57). Statements must hold on arbitrary states including dangling edges (Cycles.lean's "total on arbitrary graphs" contract — no acyclicity or endpoint-existence precondition).

The related add-wins/re-add theorem task supplies the vocabulary for hypothesis (i); landing it first is the natural order. If the element-scoped-tombstones restructure lands first, restate over the per-element removed map. Remove the backlog bullet when this lands (items leave the backlog by graduating). Completion report: new theorem names, one line each, + #print axioms check.
title: Prove cycle-repair termination in the corrected edge-count form

description:
Defect (verified @a998c55): cmdClose's success check is terminality-only — actuallyClosed := (v.state.issueData i).statusOf.closed (Tl/Cli/Commands.lean:1193). A concurrent foreign close with a DIFFERENT resolution that outstamps the local write (reachable: transact deliberately does not floor the HLC past within-window foreign stamps — pure LWW, Tl/Store/Lock.lean:127-129) leaves the state closed, so the human line prints "Closed {id} as {asStr}" with the LOSING requested resolution. Supersession is disclosed today only for the not-closed case (foreign reopen, Commands.lean:1203-1204; tested at Tests/CliTests.lean:1247-1263). Parity gap: close's JSON has no outcome field at all (only issueObj + unblocked, Commands.lean:1200), unlike claim's claim:{outcome, currentAssignee} — in the anomaly the JSON (truthful status/closeResolution via Tl/Cli/Project.lean:495-496) contradicts the human line.

Fix: value-based outcome mirroring the claim task's pattern — resWon := actuallyClosed && (v.state.issueData i).closeResolution.value.getD none == some res, plus the duplicate-target check for --as duplicate (cf. the idempotent guard at Commands.lean:1179); disclose supersession in the human line (teach: it IS closed, but as X by a concurrent write); add a close outcome field to the JSON for human/json parity. Register layout: IssueData.status : Reg Status, closeResolution : Reg (Option CloseResolution) (Tl/Kernel/State.lean:95,102); close lowers to one .setFields writing both at one stamp via statusOfResolution (Tl/Format/Codec.lean:79,189-191) — the divergence is between the requested resolution and the winning pair, never between the two registers.

Kernel closeWon predicate: optional, and semantically STRONGER than claim's value semantics — a stamp-equality predicate reports "superseded" even when a same-resolution foreign close won, which value semantics count as won. If added, mirror the claimWon machinery from the blocking task and move/restate statusOfResolution kernel-side (the kernel is verb-free, Tl/Kernel/Op.lean header). PROPOSED: ship the value-based CLI fix + tests; add the kernel predicate only if the claimWon machinery makes it near-free.

Tests in the same change: a later-stamped foreign close with a different resolution (extend the Tests/CliTests.lean:1247-1263 block via foreignLine), asserting the human line discloses supersession and the JSON outcome/closeResolution reflect the winner. Docs: wherever the close reporting contract is recorded (ADR-0008) plus the overview signal row if extended.
title: close: detect a superseded resolution and add a JSON outcome field

description:

Do not start before the ADR is pinned — fragment identity, losing-replacement tombstone semantics, rendering rule, observed-set minting, and the wire schema are decided there.

Kernel: replace IssueData.notes : Reg (Option String) (Tl/Kernel/State.lean:99) with the base register + fragment collection (project List-backed AMap/FinSet, no Mathlib Finset); new Op delta shapes for noteAppend and notesReplace(observed); wire the merge laws into the IssueData.merge comm/assoc/idem proofs; the notes rendering is a pure kernel projection (deterministic string).

Theorems (completion report, one line each, + #print axioms check): every concurrent append remains present; duplicate delivery renders an append once; replace removes exactly the fragments it observed; append-vs-replace is add-wins; rendering is deterministic under permutation, duplication, and replica merge.

Wire/shell, tests in the same change (Definition-of-Done #4): record schema + codec branches (ADR-0008, Tl/Format/Codec.lean); fold-cache encoding + cacheVersion bump + bump-guard test (Tl/Store/Cache.lean:68,144-151; Tests/CacheTests.lean); importer mapping — bulk-import notes lowers to notesReplace with empty observed (ADR-0005); CLI — --append-notes lowers to noteAppend, --notes lowers to notesReplace observing the live fragment stamps of the materialized pre-write view; rewrite the Commands.lean doc-comment (1209-1216) and the Grammar.lean help summary (133); show/JSON present the rendered string (human/json parity; structured-entry exposure per the ADR decision).

Test rows: concurrent append/append (both retained); append vs replace, observed (removed) and unobserved (survives); concurrent replace/replace (base by LWW; tombstone union per the pinned semantics); duplicate delivery renders once; identical-text concurrent appends both render; importer row; cache-version row; rendering determinism cross-check (fold-order/permutation). Existing serial coverage (Tests/CliTests.lean:287-301) must keep passing — serial semantics are unchanged (append accumulates; replace replaces what the writer sees).

Docs in the same change: overview.md theorem inventory + tested-shell rows; codebase-map annotations; the ADR gets its final theorem-name citations. Line refs @a998c55 — re-locate by symbol if drifted.
title: Implement the observed-reset notes CRDT (kernel proofs, wire, CLI)

description:
Migrate this repository's own tracker log (refs/tl/log + local .tl state) from scalar notes to the journal format, after the implementation lands. tl is pre-public, so a one-off rewrite of the shared ref is acceptable and preferred over carrying legacy-format compatibility into the first release.

Rule (pinned in the notes ADR): each issue's winning legacy scalar notes value becomes ONE synthetic immutable entry, stamped with the winning write's stamp so time/actor provenance is preserved; historically overwritten values do NOT each become entries.

Execution: take a backup of the current refs/tl/log; produce the migrated log (export -> transform -> re-import, or a direct record rewrite — decide by what the implementation makes cheapest); bump the log format v so old-format records fail closed (ADR-0008) and a stale clone cannot silently push the old ref shape back; flag-day coordination — every working copy and clone re-syncs from the rewritten ref.

Verification before deleting the backup: tl doctor healthy; note list shows the synthetic entries with their original stamps; a full re-fold matches the pre-migration materialized state in every field except the notes representation; sync round-trip against origin works (push + fresh-clone fetch).
title: Migrate this repo's tracker log to the notes-journal format

description: Two defects found by user adversarial testing after tl-pw8b merged (main@fd1e837). (1) With only XDG_CONFIG_HOME inherited, tl sync reported success but pushed refs/tl/log to a decoy repo, leaving origin untouched: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/config is a git global-config file, so it carries url.<decoy>.insteadOf rewrites — the same config-injection redirect that scrubbing GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL closes (ADR-0012 T7). The review's adversarial verify pass wrongly REFUTED this. Fix: scrub XDG_CONFIG_HOME (falls back to $HOME/.config, credentials in ~/.gitconfig/~/.ssh untouched); reclassify HOME as an explicit accepted residual (unset breaks ssh/credentials; HOME-control implies PATH-control, the already-lost tier). (2) isHeadContent (Tl/Store/Paths.lean) rejects uppercase hex, but git's hex parse is case-insensitive, so a valid bare repo with an uppercase detached HEAD is not recognized and discovery climbs out to bind an enclosing project — a wrong-repo binding. Fix: accept A-F. Tests: XDG insteadOf redirect canary (origin gets ref, decoy does not; mutation-verified), uppercase-HEAD discovery boundary + isHeadContent pins. Docs: ADR-0012 scrub list + preserved-list principle + Consequences residual, ADR-0014 T7 residual naming HOME, overview trusted entry.
title: Close XDG_CONFIG_HOME config-injection redirect and uppercase-HEAD bare bypass

description:
presentElements probes removedOf once per add-map entry; AMap.find is a linear list scan, so enumeration is Θ(#add-elements × #removed-elements). Tombstone-heavy states (many removed edges/labels) make presentEdges, ready, list, stats, doctor, and the cycle diagnostics quadratic. The performance fixtures contain essentially no removals, so nothing pins this — found by external review after the element-scoped tombstone restructure (the restructure recorded this cost honestly per ADR-0023 but did not remove it; the per-tag→per-entry hoist already landed).

Fix: both adds and removed are canonical sorted AMaps — traverse them together (sorted merge-join) or precompute the per-element tombstone view once per enumeration, giving O(#adds + #removed) per pass. The efficient form IS the production code (CLAUDE.md): rewrite OrSet.presentElements (and any other per-entry removedOf rescans — check Journal.visibleEntries when the notes journal lands, which reuses the same shape), then re-prove or bridge the pinned enumeration theorems (presentElements_eq_keys_filter, mem_presentElements, presentElements_pairwise_lt, the two filter workhorses) — statements must not change. Add a tombstone-heavy scaling row to PerfTests (e.g. N adds with N/2 removals: ×4 ops grows ≤ ×(bound)) so the class is pinned, per the ADR-0023 regression net.

Constraint: behavior identical (pure read-path change; no cacheVersion impact). Completion report: re-proved theorem names + #print axioms check + the perf row's measured ratios.
title: Retire the tombstone-probe quadratic in OR-Set enumeration

description: Constraint discovered in the tl-e4pg final confirmation (not reachable today; compaction is unshipped). The show claim-block contest scan (Tl/Cli/Commands.lean claimVerdict) detects a race-masking foreign claim only by that op's physical presence in v.loaded.ops. stampAuthoredByOwn already treats an ABSENT (compacted) origin conservatively (→ superseded), but that guard covers only the status/assignee authorship checks, NOT the contest scan. Unmasking sequence once compaction exists: own claim carol@t2 (surfaced), foreign dave claim@t3, own reopen carol@t4 — today dave@t3 is seen ⇒ superseded; if compaction later drops dave's dominated t3 claim while carol's reopen@t4 remains the own-authored winner, the contest scan no longer sees dave ⇒ ended, masking the transient lost race. When compaction (ADR-0008) is implemented, EITHER it must never drop a claim/steal op that a later burying own reopen/close supersedes, OR the contest scan must gain a materialized-contest fallback (e.g. a per-issue high-water 'last foreign claim stamp' preserved across compaction). Pick and record the choice on the compaction task; add a test row reproducing the sequence against a compacted log. No action until compaction is scheduled.
title: Contest scan needs a compaction-safe backstop for buried foreign claims

description: Discovered during the tl-5c0v gate (kind-aware dep-cycles hint). The cmdDepCycles 'no cycles' branch (rows.isEmpty -> human 'no cycles', JSON count 0) has no test pinning it — only the has-cycles hint branches are covered (blocks/parent/mixed/readiness). Add a row: an acyclic repo ->  count 0 + human 'no cycles', asserting no hint verbs appear. Trivial; grouped with the existing cliDepTests. Low priority, no correctness risk — a coverage completeness item per CLAUDE.md's shell-coverage mandate.
title: Pin the dep cycles 'no cycles' human/JSON branch with a test

description: Discovered during the tl-e4pg gate. Tl/Format/Codec.lean:199 spells the claim write-set literal '{ status := some .InProgress, assignee := some (some assignee) }' directly rather than referencing the kernel's Tl.Kernel.claimWrites (now merged in Claim.lean), which is definitionally the same set. Sharing would tie the codec's claim lowering syntactically to the kernel predicate the claim-outcome proofs are about. LOW PRIORITY / deliberately deferred: touching the codec raises a cacheVersion question (the change is behavior-neutral but the fold-cache guard is sensitive), so this is a hygiene item to do when the codec is next opened, not a standalone churn. No correctness risk (the two are definitionally equal today).
title: Share the claim write-set literal between Codec and kernel claimWrites

description: External review finding 2 (CONFIRMED against code). Op.noteRemove id obs (Tl/Kernel/Op.lean:121) tombstones EVERY stamp in obs at its own element; the decoder (Tl/Format/Codec.lean noteRemove) validates only the 'note' handle string, never that 'observed' is the singleton tag corresponding to that handle. So a syntactically valid record can carry note=<A> observed={tag of B} (remove B while naming A) or a multi-tag observed (mass-remove). This contradicts ADR-0027:207 'cross-entry interference unrepresentable' and its 'observed is a singleton by construction'. FIX (decoder-enforcement route, no kernel Op type change / no re-proof): in the noteRemove decode branch, require observed be a singleton {T} AND mintNoteId(preimage of T) == note (the handle is a hash of the tag, computable at decode) — else fail-closed (malformed, ADR-0008). This makes a cross-entry/mass/empty-observed record REJECTED, so the ADR claim holds through the fail-closed decoder + the existing remove-exactness theorem. Tests (same change): empty observed, multi-tag observed, observed tag not minting to the handle — each fails closed with a teaching message. Narrow ADR-0027 wording to state the decoder enforcement explicitly. Consider (optional, only if cheap) also tightening the kernel Op to a single Stamp for type-level unrepresentability — but the decoder route is sufficient and lower-risk.
title: noteRemove: fail-closed singleton observed matching the note handle

description: External review finding 3 (CONFIRMED against code). claimVerdict's contest scan (Tl/Cli/Commands.lean ~546) matches ONLY .claim ops: 'match p.op with | .claim ci _ => ... | _ => false'. Sequence t1 carol claim, t2 dave close, t3 carol reopen: after t3 both winning registers are carol-authored (reopen writes status=open + clears assignee), no foreign CLAIM exists above the own claim, so contested=false, statusOwn=true, assigneeHeld=true (clear arm) => .ended — masking dave's close that superseded the claim at t2. Contradicts the 'no lost race underneath' promise (docs/overview.md:330). FIX: extend the contest scan to match ANY foreign lifecycle/status write above the surfaced own claim — i.e. any op writing status or assignee (claim/steal AND close AND reopen) stamped above ownClaimStamp that the claimant did not author (!opAuthoredByOwn). Verify the legit .ended cells stay ended (own close/reopen are own-authored; cross-replica same-actor re-claim). Test (same change): the carol/dave/carol claim-close-reopen composition => superseded, built on deterministic crafted segments (no sleeps). This is a masking-class defect of the same family the 5-round arc fixed for foreign claims; it was missed because the composition (foreign CLOSE buried under own reopen) wasn't tested.
title: claim show: contest scan must catch foreign close/reopen, not only foreign claim

description: External review finding 4 (CONFIRMED against code). OrSet.entryLive (Tl/Crdt/OrSet.lean:100) tests 'q.1 ∉ p.2.2.getD empty' per tag — a FinSet membership (linear) per tag, so one element with n add-tags and n tombstones (one edge/label re-added+removed n times) is Θ(n²). va3p fixed the CROSS-element quadratic (adds-map vs removed-map merge-join) but not the within-element tag-vs-tombstone-set check. PerfTests fixture gives each edge ONE tag so it can't expose this. FIX: both the tag list and the tombstone set are sorted (canonical FinSet) — merge-join them within the element for O(n+m). Add a repeated-same-element PerfTests fixture (one element, n add tags, n tombstones) whose ratio row would fail on the current per-tag form. Keep the proved statements (entryLive feeds presentElements/allEntries — re-prove/bridge). Narrow the va3p complexity claim and fix the stale docs/overview.md:331 per-entry-lookup note. If the within-element merge is disproportionate, the fallback is an explicitly-accepted tracked residual + the fixture + narrowed docs — but prefer the fix (same sorted-merge discipline as zipLookup).
title: entryLive: within-element tag/tombstone merge-join (residual quadratic)

description: External review finding 5 (CONFIRMED against code). 'note add <id> -' calls (← IO.getStdin).readToEnd directly (Tl/Cli/Main.lean:350), unlike create which maps IO failures through liftSys — a stdin read failure escapes the stable Tl.Error/JSON-envelope discipline. FIX: route the readToEnd through liftSys (mirror create's body-from-stdin path). Coordinate the observed-set rows with the finding-2 task if done together.

description: External review finding 6 (CONFIRMED). docs/adr/ADR-0020-json-data-shapes.md:411 still shows logFormat: 1 but the binary now emits 2 (note records at v:2). .claude/skills/tl/SKILL.md:85 still advertises the retired 'tl update --notes'. Fix both to match the shipped surface (logFormat 2; SKILL.md points to tl note add). Trivial docs-only.
title: doc drift: ADR-0020 logFormat 2, SKILL.md retired --notes

description:
Verify/Report.lean:analyze and Verify/Policy.lean:importViolations are total pure functions that decide the entire tlverify verdict, and Verify/ currently carries zero theorems. Their branches are covered only by example-injection rows in Tests/VerifyTests.lean, which prove that ONE specific injected finding survives to the verdict. They cannot rule out a refactor making an arm unreachable — the failure mode that turns a green gate into false evidence.

Prove:

(1) analyze_clean_iff : (analyze cfg o).errors = #[] <-> GateClean cfg o, with GateClean a structure spelling out every condition: no first-party axiom declaration; every declaration axiom in cfg.allowedAxioms; evidence.importErrors empty; replayError? none; localModules and expectedModules equal as sets; landmarks map one-for-one onto expectedLandmarks, all theoremDecl, nodup; and the non-vacuity conjunct (decls, replayedConstants, importEdges all nonzero) when localModules is nonempty. The -> direction is load-bearing: the only route to a green verdict is that every stated condition holds. The <- direction rules out false positives, which matters because a gate that fires spuriously gets disabled.

(2) The same shape for GateEvidence.errors / AuditedReports.errors: errors = #[] <-> all five scope reports clean AND inventoryErrors empty AND unclaimedSources empty. This is the "no scope silently dropped" claim, currently one test asserting size = 7.

(3) importViolations_isEmpty_iff : importViolations p proj rows = #[] <-> for every (m, imps) in rows and every i in imps, directImportAllowed p m i (proj.contains i). Closes the "traversal silently stops reporting" class that the severalRows size-2 test only samples. Since the CI source greps were retired this is the only ADR-0009 enforcement left.

(4) directImportAllowed_cases : directImportAllowed p m i false = true -> (some q in p.ordinaryPrefixes is a prefix of i) OR (m in p.mathlibModules AND `Mathlib is a prefix of i). Proves "no third way past the policy" universally instead of by the Aesop/Qq examples.

(5) Two one-liners: completedSuccessfully_exitZero : completedSuccessfully c out = true -> c = 0 (a completion marker can never rescue a failing worker), and replayDependencies_superset : info.getUsedConstantsAsSet is a subset of replayDependencies info.

DECOMPOSITION: one lemma per analyze arm, plus a monotonicity lemma "each arm only pushes onto errors", which discharges all the retention claims (import findings, replay findings, per-scope findings reaching the final verdict) at once.

SETTLE FIRST, as part of this task rather than a separate one: docs/codebase-map.md currently states Verify/ "remains in the tested tier". Report.lean and Policy.lean are pure and total, so these are provable properties presently covered only by tests — the anti-pattern AGENTS.md principle 1 names as (a). Record the call in ADR-0004 or ADR-0026: either these become landmark theorems in Tl.Verify.landmarkTheorems (per the AGENTS.md rule that a documented proved claim gets a landmark in the same change), or the codebase-map tiering sentence is amended to say why a build-time gate outside the TCB is exempt. Do not leave it inherited by default.

Retires the corresponding example rows in reportTests / importTests / policyTests; keep only what the theorems do not cover (message wording, truncation disclosure, the summarize limit).

EXCLUDED, deliberately: propagatedAxioms correctness has its own task (it needs a reachability spec and a worklist invariant and can stall on the completeness half). The IO layer — modulesUnder, unclaimedSources, declarationsOf, projectModulesIn, and the supervisor's process handling — stays tested: it is filesystem and Lean-loader IO, correctly tier 2 under ADR-0004.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT BUY: a correct verdict GIVEN a correct Observation. It says nothing about whether observeEnvironment built an honest one. The residual risk stays in the IO observation layer; the value is removing ~180 lines of branching policy from the risk surface so review concentrates where the risk actually is.
title: Prove the trust gate's verdict logic: a clean report implies no violation

description:
Verify/Environment.lean:propagatedAxioms is where the real risk sits. It deliberately reimplements Lean's collectAxioms — it refuses to trust the serialized exportedAxiomsExt summaries in an imported .olean, which is the right call, since those summaries are data produced by the same compilation the gate is auditing. But that means the reverse-worklist propagation is now load-bearing on its own, and a bug in it is a SILENT FALSE NEGATIVE: gate green, axiom through. Tests cannot cover that space, because you can only test axioms you thought to construct.

Empirical check on the current implementation (2026-08-02): setting allowedAxioms := #[] made the production scope report 2362 declarations naming propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound individually. So the propagation is live and all three allowance entries are load-bearing, not inert. That is evidence it works on the cases exercised — not a proof that it never misses one.

Prove, over a Reaches predicate defined as the transitive closure of ConstantInfo.getUsedConstantsAsSet restricted to the constants map:

  propagatedAxioms_sound    : a in (propagatedAxioms cs)[n] -> IsAxiom cs a AND Reaches cs n a
  propagatedAxioms_complete : IsAxiom cs a -> Reaches cs n a -> a in (propagatedAxioms cs)[n]

DECOMPOSITION: prove soundness first — it is the "no false positives" half and is much cheaper. Completeness is the safety-critical half and needs the worklist invariant: every (dependency, axiom) pair either still sits in `pending` at or after `cursor`, or has already been propagated to every dependent of that dependency. The reverse-edge map built by the `alter` loop needs its own lemma (reverse[d] contains exactly the n whose stored body mentions d).

PRECEDENT: Tl/Kernel/Reach.lean already carries the machinery for this graph shape (finite reachability over a list-modelled graph, well-founded on a visited set). This is not greenfield. Note the ADR-0009 boundary — Reach.lean is inside the Mathlib escape hatch and Verify/ is not, so either the spec is modelled with batteries only, or the widening is recorded in ADR-0009 in the same change. Do not widen the hatch silently.

IF COMPLETENESS STALLS: AGENTS.md principle 1 requires decomposing and recording the residual as a carried assumption in docs/overview.md — not swapping the theorem for a test. A plausible residual shape: soundness proved, completeness proved for acyclic cones with the mutual-recursion case carried.

Blocked by the analyze/importViolations task: that one settles where Verify/ theorems live, whether they get landmarks in Tl.Verify.landmarkTheorems, and the ADR record for Verify/'s tier. Doing this one first would force those decisions under the harder proof.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE VERDICT-LOGIC TASK: analyze can only be wrong in ways that produce a visibly odd verdict. propagatedAxioms can be wrong in a way that produces a perfectly ordinary green run while an axiom sits in a kernel theorem's cone — which is precisely the claim docs/overview.md publishes.
title: Prove propagatedAxioms computes exactly the reachable axiom set

description:
The read-filter facets in Tl/Cli/Commands.lean (ListFacet, applyFacets, facetsBypassGate, labelFacet, assigneeFacet) were factored out so `ready` and `list` share one implementation. They are pure and total, and two of the claims made about them in comments and in ADR-0020 are currently asserted only by example rows in cliReadyFacetTests / cliListFacetComposeTests.

Prove:

  mem_applyFacets_iff : i in applyFacets fs xs <-> i in xs AND (for every f in fs, f.active -> f.pred i)
    — ADR-0020's "different facets compose with AND" rule, and the "an absent or empty flag is a no-op, not a false-matching filter" claim in the ListFacet docstring.

  applyFacets_sublist : applyFacets fs xs is a sublist of xs
    — order preservation. This is what makes cmdReady's inline comment true: "The ranking is preserved (filter keeps order) so count stays the post-filter total and items the ranked head of it." Currently backed by one test asserting a p0 issue comes first.

  readyFacets_cannot_widen : i in applyFacets fs (State.readyFast rollup s now) -> i in State.ready s now
    — the cross-layer claim, composing applyFacets_sublist with the existing kernel theorems State.readyFast_eq and mem_ready_iff. cmdReady's comment states it ("No facet here can bypass a closed gate: readyFast already excludes closed/rolled-up issues") and cliReadyFacetTests approximates it with four hand-built scenarios (blocked, deferred, epic, in-progress carriers). A theorem covers every facet and every state, including ones a merge could inject.

There is precedent for theorems in this layer: Tl/Cli/Project.lean already carries View.maxTag_eq, View.parents_eq, and canonicalParentE_eq as bridges. These are the same kind of thing.

EXCLUDED, recorded here rather than spun out as a speculative task: the filterSuffix byte bound. Proving (filterSuffix cs es).utf8ByteSize <= 1024 requires boundBytes_le : (boundBytes b s).utf8ByteSize <= b in Tl/Cli/Sanitize.lean first, and that lemma has value well beyond this footer — the 1 KiB single-line and 64 KiB multi-line render bounds are an ADR-0014 contract applying to every rendered field and error message, and they are currently asserted by construction with no theorem. If that lemma gets proved on its own, the filterSuffix bound is a corollary and can be added here. Do not fold Sanitize.lean into this task; it is a separate completable unit.

Independent of the two Verify/ proof tasks — different module, different risk, no shared prerequisite. Cheapest of the three.
title: Prove the CLI read-facet algebra and the ready non-widening bridge

description:
Verify/Main.lean:96-103 maps evidence.errors to (status, stdout summary, completion marker). Nothing proves or tests it: analyzedGateEvidence_clean_iff stops at the finding array, and completedSuccessfully_exitZero/_markerFinal constrain the SUPERVISOR's acceptance rule, not the worker's emission. They compose only under the assumption that the worker emits the marker exactly when it exits zero — which is the untested step. Its failure mode is the project's worst: a silently green trust gate.

Reproduced by an adversarial verification pass: no test in Tests/ reaches runChecked, and the live-gate canary exercises the initializer/supervision path, not this branch.
