Do it as a PROVED seam rather than a tested one, and put it in Verify/Report.lean, not Verify/Supervise.lean:

  structure WorkerVerdict where
    diagnostics : Array String
    report : Array String
    status : UInt32
    deriving DecidableEq

  def workerVerdict (summary marker : String) (evidence : GateEvidence) : WorkerVerdict

with theorems pinning both arms: nonempty findings give status 1 with no marker on stdout, and empty findings give status 0 with the marker last. Then runChecked is reduced to executing that decision (print diagnostics, print report, return status), which is the IO residual and stays tested.

Verify/Main.lean is protected-review bootstrap (AGENTS.md), so the change to it must be minimal and reviewed as such: the point is to move the DECISION out of it, leaving only emission.

Add the theorems to pinnedVerdictLogicTheorems. No landmark and no docs/overview.md proved-claims row — gate-internal theorems get none, per the recorded rule.
title: Prove the worker's verdict-to-exit decision

description:
Tl/Import/Bulk.lean:optInstantField is the lenient provenance reader for createdAt/closedAt/claimedAt. Its own docstring one line above promises that a present-but-unparseable value yields none WITH a disclosure, but the catch-all arm returns (none, []) — so a present, non-string value (number, bool, array, object) is silently discarded and replaced by the fallback timestamp.

Narrowed deliberately, and both review passes agree on the narrowing:
 - present non-string  => the defect. Silently swallowed; contradicts the docstring; it is the one place in parseRecord where an ill-typed value is neither refused nor reported (assignee/description/notes/duplicateOf/parent go through optStrField and DO throw).
 - unparseable string  => already correct, already discloses.
 - absent / null       => NOT a defect. Silence is intended; disclosing would flood ordinary imports, since most records carry no provenance at all. If the ADR-0005 wording reads otherwise, the wording is what changes.

Fix shape (verified to elaborate):
  match j.getObjVal? k with
  | .error _ | .ok Json.null => (none, [])
  | .ok (Json.str s) => ...unchanged...
  | .ok _ => (none, [disclosure naming the field and that the fallback was used])

Ship with one test row per input class per field — absent, null, ill-typed, unparseable-string — asserting which disclose and which do not, so the intended silence is pinned as deliberate rather than incidental.

Pre-existing; surfaced by the malformed-line coverage audit, outside what that task committed to.
title: Import: disclose a present, ill-typed provenance timestamp

description:
CI has been red since 2026-07-13, and this is one of two independent causes. The first red run (29263571691) is titled 'feat(cli): tl licenses and a generated THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES notice' — the run that added the test. It has never passed in this job.

Tests/CliTests.lean:150 reads .lake/packages/<pkg>/LICENSE. The git-floor job downloads only the binaries artifact (.github/workflows/ci.yml, 'download the tl binaries' -> path .lake/build/bin) and never fetches .lake/packages, so every package reads as missing-LICENSE and the row fails with the whole manifest listed.

The test is right; the job is under-provisioned. Two options, and the choice is the deliverable:
 (a) restore the lake-packages-src cache in git-floor so the LICENSE files are present;
 (b) scope the row to environments that have the packages.

If (b): it must NOT silently skip. An arm that is silent when its input is absent reads as success, which is the failure mode AGENTS.md names for the trust verifier and which this project has now fixed twice (tlverify's vacuity arms; the task-id lint's fail-closed scan). Gate it on an explicit marker and fail loudly when the marker says the packages should be there and they are not.

Note (a) also costs cache restore time on a job whose point is a fast floor check.
title: git-floor: the license test cannot run in that job

description:
The second cause of the red CI. This one is the gate working: git-floor caught a real ADR-0006 floor violation.

Tests/CliTests.lean:980 calls: git a ["worktree", "add", "-q", w.toString]

git 2.17.1 has no -q on 'git worktree add'. The CI log shows:
  git-env hostile-environment matrix: fixture setup failed: fixture `git worktree add -q /tmp/.../w` in /tmp/.../a exited 129: error: unknown switch `q'

tl's own code is fine — this is the test harness not being floor-compatible, which landed with the git-env isolation work around 2026-07-14.

Fix: drop -q (redirect if the output is unwanted). Then check the rest of the suite's git invocations against the 2.17 floor rather than only this one — the same class may exist elsewhere, and the floor job is the only thing that would surface it.
title: git-floor: a test fixture uses a git flag below the 2.17 floor
Implement tl edit ($EDITOR for a long description)

description:
`lake exe tlverify` takes ~2:51 on an 8-core machine (130s user, 19.6s system, 87% cpu — effectively single-threaded). Measured with an interpreted probe calling the verifier's own functions per scope (probe total 2:30, so it tracks the compiled binary): environment loads 31.8s, replayClosure 1.5s, propagatedAxioms ~0ms, Environment.replay 100.1s. Kernel replay is two thirds of the run.

Most of that replay is redundant. observeEnvironment calls replayConstantsError? with a fresh `mkEmptyEnvironment` per scope (Verify/Environment.lean:499), so every shared constant is kernel-checked once per scope. Cone sizes: production 15,048 (17.9s) / tests 18,904 (24.8s) / verifier 10,277 (19.4s) / supervisor 5,017 (13.7s) / test-supervisor 5,017 (10.9s) / tooling 5,196 (13.4s) = 59,459 constant replays over 19,108 unique constants, a 3.1x factor. The production cone is a subset of the tests cone; the two supervisor scopes inspect 41 declarations each and re-check near-identical ~5,000-constant Lean-core cones; three scopes inspecting 111 declarations between them spend 38s. Measured alternative: replaying the deduplicated union once from an empty environment takes 30.4s (whole probe 1:20 instead of 2:30), which puts the gate around 1:15-1:30.

Fix: thread a cumulative already-replayed name set and the returned environment across the six scopes, filtering each cone before submitting it. Lean.Replay.replay (v4.32.2, Lean/Replay.lean:176) only processes names in `remaining`, so a name already in the base is skipped; do not pass an unfiltered overlapping cone, since addDecl rejects a duplicate defn/inductive outright (only theorems have a duplicate-tolerant path). Soundness is preserved: a dependency-closed cone replays identically inside the union as alone, because replay is dependencies-first in both cases, so the claim "every safe total inspected declaration and its complete stored dependency cone independently replays from an empty environment through Lean's kernel" still holds.

Two things the change makes load-bearing that are free today, both of which need handling rather than silence:

(a) It introduces the assumption that a name recurring in two scopes carries the same stored ConstantInfo. That is true now — all six environments load the same .olean files — but nothing currently depends on it. Either compare on collision (a hash, not full structural equality on proof terms) or record it as a carried assumption in the Trusted section of docs/overview.md. CLAUDE.md principle 1 tier 3: never silently relied on.

(b) Per-scope attribution of a replay failure is lost. Observation.evidence.replayError? is per scope today, and the six analyses feed gateEvidenceOf separately. Lean's error text names the failing declaration ("while replaying declaration 'X'"), so either map it back to its owning scope or change the reporting deliberately.

Also in scope: update the gate description in ADR-0026 and the docstrings on replayConstantsError? / replayedConstantCount, and cover the new sharing path in Tests/VerifyLoadedTests.lean with a discrete test per branch (outside-TCB rule — the replay seam is already injectable via the ReplayAudit abbrev, so a scope-ordering and a skip-already-checked case are both reachable).

Excluded rather than deferred: running the six scopes as concurrent tasks. They are independent and the gate uses about one core of eight, but deduplication implies sequencing them, and six live environments plus the Mathlib slice is a memory risk on a 16 GB machine. If dedup lands and the resulting time is acceptable, this stays unbuilt.

Small adjacent observation, worth folding in while here: replayedConstantCount is computed per scope (Verify/Environment.lean:514) but never surfaced. The success line reports inspected counts (production=4227, tests=507, verifier=782, ...) and then says "safe total dependency cones independently replay-validated" with no number, so the ~19k constants that account for the runtime are invisible in the output.
title: tlverify: deduplicate the six per-scope kernel replays (~100s -> ~30s)

description: Implement tl version and tl version --json before the public contract freezes. Report the CLI version, source commit, pinned Lean toolchain and manifest provenance, with explicit development or dirty-build semantics per ADR-0006 and ADR-0020. Keep this in the tested CLI shell and cover every output and error branch; the release workflow must smoke-test the compiled value.
title: Expose release build provenance through tl version

description: Create the direct .github/workflows/release.yml workflow pinned by release/identity.json. On a SemVer tag, run the full build, test, verifier and policy gates, then build and smoke-test linux-x64, linux-arm64, darwin-x64 and darwin-arm64 artifacts with stable names. Linux artifacts must honor the documented old-glibc floor. Preserve one source commit and toolchain/manifest identity across the matrix and upload immutable candidate artifacts for signing.
title: Build four native release artifacts on SemVer tags

description: Extend the direct release workflow to generate SHA256SUMS, a Sigstore bundle for the sums file and every native asset, and GitHub OIDC provenance or artifact attestations. Use the exact issuer and certificate identity from release/identity.json, require bundled Rekor inclusion, verify every candidate using the published user procedure before creating the GitHub Release, and grant only the minimum workflow permissions. Tests must exercise missing, mismatched and malformed identity, digest, bundle and proof paths.
title: Sign and attest release artifacts fail closed

description: Add the curl-compatible POSIX shell installer for GitHub Releases. Detect linux or darwin and x64 or arm64, select the exact asset, verify the signed SHA256SUMS and per-asset Sigstore bundle against release/identity.json, require SHA-256 even when TL_INSTALL_SKIP_SIGNATURE=1 is explicitly set, install atomically, and emit teaching errors for every unsupported platform or missing verifier path. Cover every branch and failure code in the same change.
title: Ship a verified POSIX shell installer

description: Add packaging and trusted publication for the public @taskloop/tl package plus @taskloop/tl-darwin-arm64, @taskloop/tl-darwin-x64, @taskloop/tl-linux-arm64 and @taskloop/tl-linux-x64. The public package uses a small POSIX #!/bin/sh launcher that resolves its npm symlink, detects OS and architecture, and execs the exact optional platform dependency. Use os/cpu constraints, exact versions, public access, npm trusted publishing and provenance, with no JavaScript launcher, lifecycle scripts or install-time downloads. Pack/install tests must cover global-style and local-style links, signals and exit status, missing package, unsupported native Windows, and all four selections; published binaries must match the signed GitHub assets.
title: Publish @taskloop/tl and four native npm packages

description: Create the Homebrew distribution from the signed GitHub Release artifacts, defaulting the tap name to DmitryKorolev/homebrew-tap unless ownership is intentionally moved before the first release. Keep the maintained formula source or generator in this repository, select Intel and Apple Silicon macOS assets, pin SHA-256 and the signing identity, verify fail closed with no signature bypass, and extend the release-identity drift guard to the operative formula copy. Add formula audit and install/version smoke tests and an explicit update step in the release workflow.
title: Publish a verified Homebrew formula

description: Follow-up to the release-pipeline epic: a max-effort adversarial review returned 54 confirmed + 9 plausible findings. Fix them by root cause, not instance. Architecture adopted: a release is defined by one signed release-manifest.json; every channel is a resumable projection of it; a channel operation must be idempotent, must verify existing state before accepting it, and must never treat missing external configuration as successful publication. Compliance payload ships as companion signed assets listed in SHA256SUMS (decided against per-platform archives; record the deviation in ADR-0006).
title: Release pipeline hardening: manifest, one policy gate, idempotent channels

description: sha256_of, the SHA256SUMS awk lookup, uname->target detection, the Supported/Best-effort tier lists, the stub cosign and the selftest harness are each copy-pasted 3-5 times across install.sh, verify-release-artifacts.sh, gen-build-provenance.sh, gen-homebrew-formula.sh and npm-pack.sh, and have already diverged. Add scripts/lib/release-common.sh plus a machine-readable target/tier source, convert every script that can source it, and drift-guard install.sh's necessarily-embedded copies (it is piped from curl and has no checkout). Also retires the note-$? class: five selftest rows are unreachable under set -e.
title: Shared release shell library and one target/tier source

description: Nothing compares the tag, productVersion in Tl/Cli/Commands.lean, the lakefile package version, the five npm manifests, and the 0.1.0 literal in Tests/ReleaseTests.lean, even though two error messages instruct the operator to keep them in lockstep. Add a single validator over every copy and call it from the one release-policy entry point. Also harden the greedy sed scrape of productVersion in release.yml, and pin npmPackage from release/identity.json against npm/tl/package.json.
title: One version source, one version validator

description: ci.yml runs nine release gates; release.yml's gates job runs four, while its comment claims it re-runs the correctness gates on the tagged commit. Move the whole policy into scripts/check-release-policy.sh and call it identically from both workflows so the two definitions of ready cannot drift apart.
title: One executable release-policy entry point

description: Uppercase-hex digests are accepted by the sanity check and then compared case-sensitively against lowercase output, so a valid sums file reads as tampering; install.sh never checks the 64-character length; the $-anchor check present in Tests/ReleaseTests.lean is missing from the shell verifier; TL_INSTALL_SKIP_SIGNATURE is honoured from the ambient environment inside the release workflow's own pre-publish gate; an interrupted install leaves .tl.install.<pid> behind; resolve_version is wholly untested and its curl carries no --proto restriction.
title: Verifier and installer refusal-path fixes

description: The <version> argument is validated only by a leading-digit test and is then interpolated into a Python replacement string and into Ruby source, so it can crash the generator or inject arbitrary Ruby into the published formula. Dropping an absent Best-effort block leaves asset_name mapping that platform to a url the formula no longer has. The selftest overwrites the tracked Formula/tl.rb with its only backup inside the tempdir its EXIT trap deletes. mv from mktemp silently makes the formula 0600. if: always() uploads the unfilled placeholder under the same artifact name a good formula uses. Nothing executes the formula's install or test bodies.
title: Homebrew generator and formula correctness

description: Trusted publishing must be configured per package and npm only allows that for packages that already exist, so the first release cannot authenticate; document and check the bootstrap. The publish loop is not resumable and npm versions are immutable, so a partial failure strands the version permanently; pre-pack, query, skip-if-identical, fail on conflict. Plus: the musl guard is unreachable behind the missing-binary exit, delegate resolution gates on -x so a lost executable bit reads as not-installed, the skip warning describes the opposite of what npm-pack publishes, nothing proves three of the four platform tarballs ship bin/tl, and staging into an existing directory nests the trees.
title: npm channel: bootstrap, idempotent publish, launcher fixes

description: Publish one signed release-manifest.json that every downstream job validates against instead of reconstructing asset lists. Ship LICENSE, THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES, SBOM and the per-target link audit as companion signed assets in SHA256SUMS, and have the installer and formula place the notice beside the binary (ADR-0006 requires it in every distribution artifact). Carry each leg's smoke-tested binary digest out of the build job so sign does not sign whatever download-artifact returned, and have each leg emit signed build metadata (runner image, container digest, toolchain, manifest digest) rather than granting four more jobs id-token: write. Fix the unquoted command substitution that trips the new actionlint gate.
title: Release workflow: signed manifest, compliance assets, build-boundary evidence

description: environment: release is only meaningful once required reviewers, a deployment tag rule and a tag ruleset are configured, and that exists solely as a workflow comment; npm trusted publishing and the tap credential are the same shape of unenforced external state. Add a prerequisites document and a checker that queries what it can, and record the residue in the Trusted section of docs/overview.md as explicit carried assumptions, together with the new user-facing trust claims this branch introduces.
title: Release prerequisites: document, check, and carry the assumptions

description: docs/vision.md still advertises native Windows as best-effort after the branch retired it everywhere else; ADR-0014 T3 is marked mitigate-DONE while three of its bullets are unimplemented and its launcher integrity-pin mitigation was deleted without recording a carried assumption; ADR-0006 and VERIFYING.md describe the installer and formula as future work in the change that lands them; VERIFYING.md promises old artifacts verify against the identity that signed them while every verifier reads only the current pin; docs/codebase-map.md claims the installer shares the verifier implementation, which the same change says it does not.
title: Documentation drift across the release change

description: Three review rounds produced 63 + 8 + 15 findings, and the recurring defect is one shape: POSIX shell discarding a non-zero status so a check that cannot run reports success (swallowed command substitution, failing substitution in an assignment prefix, set -e inside $( ), status lost to a nested substitution). Fixed twice and reintroduced four times while fixing other things, which makes it a language problem rather than an author problem. Move the decision layer — typed models, parsing, validation, generation, planning, result classification — into a separately built tlrelease executable following the tlverify precedent. HARD CONSTRAINTS: Release/ imports nothing from Tl/ (keeps release administration out of the shipped product AND keeps the toolchain-free CI gate fast — batteries only, no Mathlib); tlrelease is not part of the product TCB, with small theorems only for high-risk verdict functions as Verify/Proofs.lean does; install.sh, Formula/tl.rb and verify-release-artifacts.sh stay at their native boundaries, because a precompiled verifier must not become the only way to authenticate the release containing it. Scope v0.1.0 to signed GitHub Release + installer; npm and Homebrew follow once the repository is public and the npm bootstrap is done.
title: Port the release decision layer to a tlrelease Lean executable

description: install.sh (the TL_INSTALL_SOURCE_ONLY hatch that makes a real install and the gating selftest exit 0 under dash; the notice fetch that exits 1 after a successful install; the notice digest lookup missing the hex and length checks the binary path carries), Formula/tl.rb (Formula#system raises rather than returning false, so the opoo fallback is dead code and a missing notice aborts the install; the deleted version line loses the SemVer prerelease suffix so every interpolated url points at a tag that does not exist), and verify-release-artifacts.sh (the nested substitution that hides rc_sha256_of's failure and reports a missing digest tool as tampering; the scratch file written into the asset directory, which leaves an empty refusal message on read-only media). These survive the port because their files stay shell and Ruby.
title: Fix the seven findings in code that is not moving

description: tlverify refuses a top-level Lean source that no scope claims, so Release/ needs a scope entry before the first file or every build fails. Verify/Main.lean and its scope table are protected-review bootstrap. Decide the inspection depth deliberately: production is axiom-audited and kernel-replayed, tooling is lighter, and release administration should not become a sprawling proof obligation. Do not put it under Tl/ to satisfy the root-import rule — that would import release administration into the shipped product.
title: Claim a Release/ scope in the trust verifier, before any Lean lands

description: Release/Model.lean and Release/Json.lean. Make the problematic states unrepresentable rather than validated after the fact: a malformed digest cannot inhabit Sha256, a published target requires its build metadata by construction rather than carrying Option, and an audit result is an inductive with verified/missing/unchecked/operationalError arms so an API outage cannot become an empty string that reads as absence. Batteries only, no Mathlib, no imports from Tl/.
title: Typed models: version, target, digest, commit, metadata

description: Release/Manifest.lean + Release/Metadata.lean. Absorbs two confirmed findings: the rc_targets substitution failure that empties the target list and skips every build-metadata check, and runId compared only leg-to-leg rather than against the ambient run. Keep the shell implementation alongside and compare outputs byte-for-byte in CI until it is deleted.
title: Port manifest generation and verification, with golden fixtures

description: Release/Prerequisites.lean. Absorbs two findings: an API failure collapsing into an empty policy and being reported as a MISSING prerequisite that aborts a legitimate release, and the tag-ruleset check accepting any refs/tags/v prefix rather than a pattern that covers v*. Lean decides and classifies; gh is still invoked through IO.Process with explicit exit classification.
title: Port prerequisite classification

description: Release/Sbom.lean + Release/Homebrew.lean. Absorbs the unvalidated fallback digest that can emit sha256 "" and exit 0. The formula stays Ruby and is still validated by brew style/audit in CI; only the rendering moves.
title: Port SBOM and Homebrew formula rendering

description: Release/Npm.lean. Absorbs two findings: the bracket-class typo that makes the never-publish-to-latest guard unfireable, and package-content comparison that ignores symlinks and file modes. Compare type, mode and symlink target, not just regular-file digests. Lean decides absent/matches/conflict; npm still performs the publication.
title: Port npm bootstrap and publish planning

description: verify-release-artifacts.sh needs python3 solely to read the certificate pin out of identity.json without mangling its regex escapes, and it must stay shell — a precompiled verifier cannot be the only way to authenticate the release containing it. Have tlrelease emit a two-line sourceable pin file, drift-guarded against the JSON the way Tl/Build/Stamp.lean is, so the user-facing verification path needs no parser.
title: Emit a sourceable release/identity.sh and drop python3 from the shell verifier

description: Release/Policy.lean + Main.lean, and the remaining shell wrappers become one exec line each. The release-policy CI job is deliberately toolchain-free so a lint failure surfaces in seconds rather than after the build matrix (ADR-0026); porting the runner makes it depend on a Lean build, which is only acceptable because Release/ imports nothing from Tl/ and no Mathlib — verify that lake build tlrelease is minutes, not the full matrix, and record the measured cost in ADR-0026.
title: Replace the shell policy runner, and keep the fast CI gate fast

description: npm needs a manual bootstrap that has not happened, Homebrew needs a tap that does not exist, and neither works while the repository is private. Cut the first release to the one channel that can ship, record the deferral in ADR-0006 rather than leaving the ADR promising channels the release does not deliver, and run a workflow_dispatch rehearsal first — not one of the four build legs has ever executed.
title: Scope v0.1.0 to Release + installer; defer npm and Homebrew

description:
Release-blocking, and its own task rather than a line inside the scope task. Not one of the four build legs has ever executed.
MUST OBSERVE: all four legs run; Supported vs Best-effort behaviour on a deliberately failed leg; the glibc floor assertion; the link audit and build metadata produced per leg; manifest assembly and verification over artifacts that actually crossed the artifact store, not a local fixture; and that the run has NO signing or publication capability — a dispatch run must be incapable of it, not merely not asked.
FAULT INJECTION, because every gate here is supposed to fail closed: a missing command, a command exiting non-zero, malformed JSON, a timeout, and an unreadable file. Each must produce a refusal that names the cause, not a pass and not a bare non-zero exit.
The cross-job artifact handoff is the part local selftests cannot reach, and it is where the build-to-sign evidence check lives.
PROOF BOUNDARY: none. This is the end-to-end I/O tier.
title: Full workflow_dispatch rehearsal and fault injection

description:
Release-blocking for v0.1.0. No path reachable from the GitHub-only release workflow, install.sh, verify-release-artifacts.sh, or the strict v0.1 release policy may invoke python, python3, ruby, brew, node, or npm. Lean owns JSON parsing, typed decisions, manifest and metadata generation, prerequisite classification, SBOM generation, and identity-pin generation; POSIX shell remains only as thin orchestration and the user bootstrap boundary.

Enforce this twice. First, maintain an explicit inventory of v0.1 entry points and reject forbidden command invocations in their reachable first-party scripts; deferred channel files are excluded by name, not by an open-ended directory exception. Second, exercise the v0.1 policy, installer selftests, verifier selftests, and rehearsal with PATH-precedence shims for python, python3, ruby, brew, node, and npm that fail loudly if called. The test must prove each shim can fire before trusting a silent run.

This is a dependency-boundary claim, not a ban on channel-native runtimes. When Homebrew is enabled later, Formula/tl.rb is necessarily Ruby and real brew validation uses Homebrew-managed Ruby; formula rendering and shared decisions remain Lean. When npm is enabled later, npm operations use node/npm; planning, classification and comparison remain Lean. Neither boundary may leak into the v0.1 GitHub release.

DELETES or rewrites every Python and Ruby invocation remaining on a v0.1-reachable path, including inline workflow snippets and strict-policy gates. The completion report names the retained deferred invocations and why none is reachable.
title: Enforce the v0.1 release dependency boundary

description:
DEFERRED CHANNEL WORK for v0.2.0. It does not block the v0.1 GitHub release, its dependency-boundary gate, or its rehearsal.

Release/Homebrew.lean renders Formula/tl.rb from the typed release model and signed GitHub-release evidence. The formula itself remains Ruby because Homebrew formulas are a Ruby DSL, and validation uses real brew with Homebrew-managed Ruby. Users do not acquire a separate project Ruby dependency. Shared parsing, validation and rendering decisions remain Lean; no Python is introduced at this boundary.

The tap, credential and publication job are enabled only when Homebrew is part of the declared release plan. Until then, no Ruby or brew command is reachable from the strict v0.1 policy or release workflow.

PROOF BOUNDARY: none. Test deterministic rendering, stable and prerelease version resolution, missing Best-effort assets, digest validation, formula load, install and test bodies, style and audit.

DELETES on completion: scripts/gen-homebrew-formula.sh entirely. Formula/tl.rb remains by necessity. The existing shell implementation is a differential oracle only until golden comparison is green, then it and the comparison are removed.
title: Port Homebrew formula rendering at the Ruby boundary

description:
The branch stays local, so the CI matrix cannot run — but most of a build leg is not GitHub-specific. Eight of its fourteen steps are ordinary commands and can be executed directly on this machine, which de-risks the largest untested surface without pushing anything.
RUNNABLE NATIVELY on the macOS host (darwin-arm64, the Supported tier): stamp the checkout with gen-build-provenance.sh --stamp; lake build tl; stage the artifact; ad-hoc codesign and verify; record the macOS minimum version; the full smoke test including the git task round-trip; the link audit via otool -L and nm; and the build-metadata record. Then feed the result to the manifest generator and to verify-release-artifacts.sh so the local half of the artifact contract is exercised end to end.
RUNNABLE WITH DOCKER for the two Linux legs, whose daemon is installed but not running: the pinned glibc-floor image, elan from the hash-pinned tarball, lake exe cache get, lake build tl, and — the point of that leg — the readelf glibc floor assertion against a real binary. On an arm64 host the linux-arm64 leg runs natively; linux-x64 runs emulated, which is slow but still exercises the build.
NOT RUNNABLE LOCALLY, and must be stated as untested: actions/checkout, upload/download-artifact and therefore the cross-job handoff where the build-to-sign evidence check lives, the cache actions, OIDC, cosign signing, and gh release create.
Prefer driving the real steps over reimplementing them — a rehearsal script that drifts from the workflow rehearses the script. Extracting each step's shell from the workflow and running it is better than paraphrasing it.
title: Rehearse each build leg locally, without GitHub

description:
sign, publish-release, publish-homebrew and publish-npm currently gate on `github.ref_type == 'tag'` alone. Require both a real push event and a tag ref — `github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref_type == 'tag'` — so no dispatch, schedule or future trigger can reach a job holding id-token, contents: write, or the tap credential.
The stamp job already refuses a dispatch against a tag ref, but that is one guard in one place; the privileged jobs should each be unable to run rather than relying on an upstream refusal. Worth doing whatever is decided about pushing: it makes any future rehearsal incapable of signing rather than merely not asked to sign, which is the property a rehearsal needs.
title: Harden every privileged job against a non-tag trigger

description:
scripts/check-release-version.sh is a strict-policy gate on a v0.1-reachable path and invokes python3 (measured: it fails under refusing interpreter shims), so ADR-0006's dependency budget cannot hold while it stands. No other task covers it — tl-avzfpen names strict-policy gates in its scope but lists only the three generator ports as blockers.

The python does two things, neither of which needs an interpreter: json.load over the five npm package.json manifests, and line-anchored literal extraction of productVersion from Tl/Cli/Commands.lean and version := v!"..." from lakefile.lean. release/Json.lean already parses and renders JSON with typed access; the extraction is plain string scanning. No regex engine required.

Move it to a tlrelease subcommand over the typed model, keep the --tag/--print/--selftest surface, retire the shell gate, and re-point the policy's gate entry. Every refusal path it documents keeps a discrete selftest row (ADR-0004 tiering: this is shell/IO, tested not proved).
title: Port the version-consistency gate off python3

description:
scripts/check-embedded-copies.sh is a strict-policy gate on a v0.1-reachable path and invokes python3, so ADR-0006's dependency budget cannot hold while it stands. No other task covers it.

It guards the copies of scripts/lib/release-common.sh that cannot source it — install.sh, piped from curl, and the npm launcher, which ships inside a published package — comparing them textually where the code can be identical and by classification for the uname mapping, where the wording differs legitimately but a disagreement about which system is which would ship the wrong binary.

The python is block extraction and comparison, not semantic matching: it locates named shell function blocks and diffs them. Plain string scanning in Lean. Move it to a tlrelease subcommand, keep both comparison modes and the --selftest arm, retire the shell gate, and re-point the policy entry. Each documented refusal keeps a discrete selftest row.
title: Port the embedded-copy drift gate off python3

description:
scripts/check-release-identity.sh is a strict-policy gate on a v0.1-reachable path and invokes python3, so ADR-0006's dependency budget cannot hold while it stands. It is the hardest of the unported gates and the only one that needs a regular-expression *engine* rather than string extraction.

WHAT IT DOES, and why a text check cannot replace it: Tests/ReleaseTests.lean guards that every operative copy of the pin carries the same text, which is drift. It cannot guard what the text MEANS. An expression that is anchored and well-formed but matches the wrong repository would sail through a text-equality check while hollowing out the fail-closed verifier (ADR-0014 T3). So this gate compiles the pinned certificateIdentityRegexp and evaluates it against adversarial candidates: a repository whose name contains ours, a different workflow in this repository, an unescaped-dot match, a non-SemVer tag.

WHY THIS IS TRACTABLE. The committed expression uses only ^ $ escaped-dot, character classes, groups, alternation, +, * and ? — no lookaround, no backreferences, no brace repeats. That is exactly the RE2-safe subset. A matcher over {literal, class, concat, alternate, star, plus, optional, anchors} is bounded work, not a general engine.

WHY IT IS AN IMPROVEMENT, not merely budget compliance. The script's own header records that Python's re is NOT cosign's engine: cosign is Go, Go's regexp is RE2, a strict subset with no lookaround and no backreferences. Today the script hand-refuses the constructs RE2 rejects and states that this is narrower than compiling with the real engine. A Lean matcher implementing the subset directly is CLOSER to cosign's semantics than Python is, and cannot accept a construct RE2 would reject, because it cannot represent one.

PROOF BOUNDARY: the matcher is a pure total function and is the natural place for a theorem — match agrees with a denotational semantics of the parsed pattern. Do not phrase it as a claim about cosign; the carried assumption is that Go's RE2 agrees with the modelled subset, and that belongs in docs/overview.md's Trusted section. The gate's I/O and the adversarial candidate table stay tested (ADR-0004).

Keep the matcher and the gate in one task: the matcher is the bulk, but it is infrastructure with exactly one consumer, and split apart neither half can be validated on its own.
title: Port the identity-discrimination gate: an RE2-subset matcher in Lean

description:
ADR-0006's dependency budget binds paths reachable from the GitHub-release workflow, and tl-avzfpen's scope names inline workflow snippets explicitly. .github/workflows/release.yml still runs python3 in three places, none of them ticketed:

  line 194  the stamp job's tag check — matches the tag's synthetic SAN against
            the pinned certificateIdentityRegexp before the matrix runs
  line 626  the build legs' build-metadata record — digests the artifact and
            lake-manifest.json and renders the JSON document
  line 772  the sign job's second SAN check, before anything is signed

The 626 one is absorbed by the manifest/metadata port. The two SAN checks need the same regex evaluation as the identity-discrimination gate, so they are its natural second consumer — do them after that matcher exists rather than duplicating the decision in YAML.

Each becomes a tlrelease subcommand invocation. The workflow keeps only thin orchestration, which is what the budget leaves shell (and YAML) for. Verify by running the release policy and the workflow-reachable selftests under failing PATH-precedence shims for python, python3, ruby, brew, node and npm, proving each shim can fire first.
title: Remove the inline python3 from the release workflow

description:
The Homebrew generator's selftest checked the mode of the formula it had just
written with

    $(stat -f '%Lp' "$out" 2>/dev/null || stat -c '%a' "$out")

which is the BSD spelling with the coreutils one behind it. coreutils reads -f
as file-system status and takes no format there, so on Linux '%Lp' is a second
path operand: the run fails on it and prints a filesystem report for the real
one. Redirecting stderr hides the complaint but not the report, and a command
substitution keeps the stdout of both sides of a ||, so the fallback's 644
arrives concatenated onto that report.

The row reported FAIL on every Linux run and could report nothing else, which
took the release-policy job down with it. The formula it was checking was
correct throughout: the generator chmods 0644 explicitly.

Outcome: one rc_file_mode in scripts/lib/release-common.sh that tries each
dialect on its own and accepts an answer only if it is octal digits, covered
the way the digest tools are — the check shown to discriminate against a real
0600 file, and both dialects driven through the helper by stubs that answer
with a mode the file does not have.
title: Read a file mode in whichever stat dialect the host speaks

description:
Move lean-toolchain to leanprover/lean4:v4.33.0, repin mathlib at its v4.33.0 tag (db584cd6) and batteries at 4488d40d, and byte-match every transitive rev in lake-manifest.json against mathlib's own v4.33.0 manifest so the prebuilt olean cache still hits.

Known 4.33.0 breaking surface to audit against this tree:
- backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency.types defaults to true (simp/grind lemma application at implicit transparency).
- Float.lt/Float.le change Prop -> Bool; Float no longer opaque.
- Kernel recursion depth bounded by maxRecDepth rather than the physical stack.
- Lean.initializing / enableInitializersExecution / isInitializerExecutionEnabled move IO -> BaseIO; lean_enable_initializer_execution returns a scalar (FFI).
- Namespace moves: Int.Linear -> Int.Internal.Linear, IO.AsyncList -> Lean.AsyncList, LLVM -> Lean.LLVM; Nat.ne_of_gt is protected.
- Lake: the setup facet is no longer buildable from the CLI.
- Code generation stops inspecting the private constructor of a public type (FFI representation).

Bump checklist beyond the pins: regenerate THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES and the embedded Tl/Cli/Licenses.lean, re-run the bundled-LICENSES and dead-strip determinations, move stampToolchain, and update every pinned version string in fixtures, ADR worked examples and the release workflow. Gates: lake build --wfail, lake build tlverify --wfail, lake exe tlverify, lake exe tltest, scripts/check-task-ids.sh, scripts/check-release-policy.sh --strict.
title: Upgrade the Lean toolchain to v4.33.0

description:
Replace the opaque TL_VERIFY_COMPLETED_V1 and TL_TESTS_COMPLETED_V1 terminal markers with plain, self-explanatory, versioned success verdict lines for tlverify and tltest.

Preserve the supervision contract: status zero is accepted only when the exact protocol-specific verdict is the last nonempty stdout line. The change must continue to reject a missing verdict, a verdict followed by later output, the wrong worker verdict, and a nonzero worker exit even if it printed the verdict. Do not weaken this to exit status alone or imply that the public in-band verdict authenticates a deliberately malicious worker.

Prefer deriving the displayed verdict from structured CompletionProtocol fields instead of maintaining another pair of arbitrary duplicated constants. Use product-consistent names such as tlverify and tltest and retain an explicit protocol version so stale worker/launcher combinations remain distinguishable.

Update Verify/Supervise.lean, worker emission in Verify/Main.lean and Tests/Main.lean, the verdict proofs in Verify/Proofs.lean, real-process and pure tests in Tests/VerifyTests.lean, and documentation that quotes or describes the current marker terminology. Keep the proved properties intact: emission iff clean evidence, the clean report shape, final-line acceptance, distinct worker protocols, and failure-path rejection.

Done when lake build --wfail, lake build tlverify --wfail, lake exe tltest, and lake exe tlverify pass, with the new readable final lines visible in command output and no opaque TL_*_COMPLETED_V1 strings remaining.
title: Make tlverify and tltest completion verdicts human-readable

description: Verify/Report.lean documents a residual call-site hole: gateEvidenceOf receives seven values of the same Observation type, so an accidental duplicate or swap compiles and can leave one environment unaudited. Introduce a seven-case gate-scope type and make each observation carry its scope at the type boundary, either as an indexed Observation or an equivalent proof-carrying wrapper. Derive the human scope label from that type, assemble the seven inputs through a named structure whose field types differ, and remove reliance on named arguments as the only mitigation. Definition of done: a production/tests or supervisor/test-supervisor swap cannot elaborate; analyzedGateEvidence_clean_iff and the worker-verdict composition remain proved without sorry, admit, decide, or bare simp; compiled verifier tests still pin every finding arm and inventory argument; docs/overview.md narrows the verifier-bootstrap assumption accurately; and the stale six-scopes comment on the seven-field AuditedReports structure is corrected. Run the full verifier gates required by AGENTS.md.
title: Make trust-verifier observations scope-typed

description:
Define 'reproducible' before implementing it. A second build from a different absolute path, same target/toolchain/build capsule, must produce byte-identical PAYLOAD; evidence about a particular run is not reproducible by construction and must not be claimed to be.

REPRODUCIBLE (payload): the unsigned executables, the deterministic packaging payload, AND the SBOM — release/Sbom.lean already fixes creationInfo.created to the epoch and derives everything from lean-toolchain + lake-manifest.json precisely so two generations of one release agree byte-for-byte. Excluding it would give away a property that is already built and tested.

NOT REPRODUCIBLE (evidence about a run): build-metadata-*.json (records the leg that ran); the manifest's run-identity fields (workflowRef/runId, and the embedded per-leg build records); Sigstore bundles, transparency-log material, GitHub attestations.

Note the manifest is NOT wholly excluded: everything except the run-identity fields and the embedded records is a function of the payload. State the boundary as payload-vs-run-evidence rather than as a file list, which goes stale.

An independent rebuilder reproduces the binary digest and compares it against the digest in the signed release evidence; it does not reproduce the evidence. Pin this in ADR-0006 (or a reproducibility ADR) BEFORE implementation.
title: Pin the reproducibility boundary: payload reproduces, run-evidence does not

description:
Once manifest-verify passes, downstream jobs read targets, npm.distTag and homebrew.pinnedTargets from the typed manifest instead of re-deriving the release. SHA256SUMS stays the published user-facing digest surface but stops being a second release planner.

CONDITION, and it is not optional. release/Manifest.lean's ManifestDescription deliberately parses ONLY 'tag' and 'assets' today, because manifest-verify asks one question and re-parsing a section no verdict consumes would be surface without a decision behind it. The moment a downstream job reads targets / npm.distTag / homebrew.pinnedTargets, that narrow parse becomes a hole: a manifest with a garbage or absent targets section verifies clean and is then consumed. So this task must widen ManifestDescription to a full typed parse — target rows, the embedded build records, the npm and homebrew blocks — in the SAME change that adds the first downstream reader. Not afterwards.

Also decide there: whether the derived npm/homebrew blocks are re-derived on read (they are derived, not stored, in Manifest.of) or trusted from the document. Trusting them is the point of the manifest; re-deriving them would reintroduce the four-derivations problem this replaced.
title: Make the verified manifest authoritative downstream

description:
Tests/CrossTests.lean samples the compiled kernel against its proved spec. The mechanism exists; the residual is making it contractual rather than incidental.

PIN THE CONTRACT, NOT THE CONSTANTS. Do not write the seed formula, the seed count, or the operations-per-seed into the ADR: those live in Tests/CrossTests.lean and a second copy in prose will drift — which is exactly the staleness this repo just deleted from the discovery backlog entry. The project already has the better pattern: Tl.Verify.landmarkTheorems pins NAMES in code, docs/overview.md pins CLAIMS in prose, and tlverify fails when they diverge.

So ADR-0004 should record: the cross-check is deterministic and never fuzz-dependent; the list of sampled properties (fold order/duplication insensitivity, CRDT join laws, ready soundness+order, unblocks = ready-diff, rollup totality, fast/spec bridges, cycle implementations, certificate-path acceptance); crafted SCC and wire-order fixtures are retained alongside the random corpus; strengthening is additive; and REDUCING the corpus or the property list requires an ADR edit. The numeric corpus parameters stay in the test, referenced by name.

State plainly that sampling the compiled binary is a regression net over compilation, never a substitute for the Tl/Kernel + Tl/Crdt theorems.
title: Pin the compiled-kernel cross-check contract in ADR-0004

description:
PATH shims are a negative control, not isolation: they cannot shadow an absolute
path (/usr/bin/python3), and the lexical arm only closed that by comparing a
command's last path segment. A runtime where the forbidden interpreters do not
exist at all closes it by construction.

BUILD: a CI job that runs the first-party release path — check-release-policy.sh
--profile release, the installer selftest, the artifact verifier selftest — in a
minimal container with no python, python3, ruby, brew, node or npm installed.
Absolute paths then fail because the file is absent, not because a shim decided
to fail.

CONSTRAINTS. GitHub Actions' own Node runtime is outside this boundary and stays
outside it: only first-party `run:` steps enter the container, never the actions
themselves. The container image is pinned by digest, like every other pinned
tool in this pipeline. scripts/check-release-runtimes.sh stays: it runs
everywhere, including a developer's machine, and static scanning still covers
branches this run does not take. State in ADR-0026 which arm covers what, so
three arms do not read as three copies of one.

RISK TO MANAGE: this job has never run. Land it with tl-10ny (the full CI
rehearsal) or immediately before, so an unexercised workflow change is not
sitting on main.
title: Run the v0.1 release path hermetically, not only under PATH shims

description:
ADR-0004 now lists what Tests/CrossTests.lean samples and separates three kinds
of claim in prose: a re-check of a proved statement, a delegation the kernel
makes to the shell (wire-order preservation), and an observation about which
branch ran (certificate fast-path acceptance). A review found the first version
of that list called all of them proved, which is the drift a prose table invites.

BUILD: a registry in the test file pairing each sampled property with its
evidence — `proved (theoremName)` or `tested (reason)` — where a `proved` entry
resolves its theorem name at compile time, the way Tl.Verify.landmarkTheorems
and pinnedVerdictLogicTheorems already do. Retiring or renaming a theorem then
breaks the build rather than leaving the ADR claiming a proof that is gone.

Then either generate the ADR's list from the registry or check it against it.
Do not write the theorem names into the ADR as a second copy — that is the
staleness this replaces. The numeric corpus parameters stay in the test and are
referenced by name, as recorded.
title: Give the compiled-kernel cross-check's claims an evidence type

description:
The recurring defect this layer was built to remove is POSIX shell discarding a
status. tlrelease now owns the manifest, SBOM, identity, prerequisites, version
consistency, embedded copies and the dependency boundary; what is left in shell
is orchestration that still makes decisions of its own.

MEASURE FIRST, then port what the measurement justifies. The candidates, in the
order their decisions matter:
- policy dispatch and profile selection (scripts/check-release-policy.sh,
  scripts/check-channel-policy.sh) — argument parsing, which gates a profile
  has, and the skip-versus-fail rule. Note tl-x9n1 already asks whether the
  policy runner should move at all, and its criterion is cold-runner CI time;
  do not pre-empt that answer here.
- runtime classification in scripts/check-release-runtimes.sh: which commands
  are forbidden is a list in shell and a list in Lean today, deliberately
  duplicated so one edit cannot lose both. If tlrelease emits the list, the
  duplication becomes generation and the reason for it has to be restated.

WHAT STAYS SHELL, and why: install.sh is piped from curl and has no checkout to
read; scripts/verify-release-artifacts.sh must not require a precompiled
verifier to authenticate the release that contains it (ADR-0006). Those two get
a dedicated external harness rather than a port.

The target shape for everything else is `exec tlrelease <command> "$@"`. A
script that only execs cannot discard a status.
title: Shrink the release shell to adapters over tlrelease

description:
Add tlrelease stamp and tlrelease task-id-lint as complete replacements for the two remaining repository gates that make decisions in shell.

The stamp command runs from ReleaseCore, which imports nothing from Tl, so CI builds tlrelease first, writes Tl/Build/Stamp.lean, and then builds the product without a dependency cycle. Preserve development versus clean stamped builds, commit and dirty-state checks, toolchain and lake-manifest digest validation, atomic output, and every refusal currently covered by the shell selftest.

The task-ID command reads the tracked-file inventory, applies the canonical Crockford rule and placeholder registry, refuses vacuous or unreadable scope, and keeps stable teaching errors. Both commands receive public-command black-box fixtures in Tests/ReleaseToolTests.lean.

DELETE on completion: scripts/gen-build-provenance.sh and scripts/check-task-ids.sh, their embedded selftest branches, and workflow calls to them.
title: Port build stamping and task-ID lint to tlrelease

description:
Add a typed policy registry to ReleaseCore and expose tlrelease policy --profile ci|release [--strict]. Gate membership, enabled-channel selection, external-tool requirements, strict missing-tool behavior, invocation, completion, and reporting are data and code in Lean rather than shell branches.

Both ci.yml and release.yml build tlrelease and invoke the same policy command. The CI profile includes channel validation even while a channel is deferred; the release profile is derived from release/plan.json and contains only enabled channels. npm and Homebrew commands are invoked directly after their ports land. Build, verifier, test, bootstrap-script black-box, formula, package, and workflow gates remain discrete named outcomes.

Move complex inline workflow decisions into tlrelease subcommands, including Homebrew tap update and npm publication. Leave only pinned actions, environment wiring, and short command-launch steps in YAML. Do not add a second generated shell runner.

Public real-process tests cross tool present or absent, strict or non-strict, pass or fail, multiple requirements, malformed invocation, profile membership, enabled and deferred channels, timeout, and non-zero completion.
title: Add the typed tlrelease policy runner and cut over both workflows

description:
After every consumer runs through tlrelease, remove the infrastructure that existed only to make shell decisions survivable.

DELETE: scripts/check-release-policy.sh, scripts/check-channel-policy.sh, scripts/check-release-runtimes.sh, scripts/lib/release-common.sh, any remaining scripts/lib/channel-common.sh, replaced generator and npm scripts, release/Boundary.lean, its command registration, the command-spelling corpus, policy-shell hygiene scans, rc_tool_gate tests, and documentation that contracts the lexer plus PATH-shim pair as permanent architecture.

The tracked shell allowlist becomes exactly install.sh and scripts/verify-release-artifacts.sh. Formula/tl.rb remains Ruby and the npm launcher is JavaScript. A new shell file fails the inventory test by default.

The dependency budget is enforced by typed external-tool declarations for tlrelease commands, comprehensive public-command tests, the tracked-shell allowlist, and the hermetic GitHub-only run. Do not replace the deleted lexer with another parser or generated shell policy. Update ADR-0006, ADR-0026, AGENTS.md, docs/codebase-map.md, and remove the stale known-shell-defects backlog entry in this change.
title: Delete obsolete release shell and lexer-shim enforcement

description:
External channel setup after the complete tlrelease npm port is available.

Use tlrelease npm bootstrap to build and publish the immutable 0.0.0 placeholders for @taskloop/tl and all four platform packages under the bootstrap tag. Confirm the launcher is published last, latest does not resolve to the placeholder, and the registry copies match the locally planned packages.

Configure the release workflow and release environment as the npm trusted publisher for each package, with no long-lived token. Run tlrelease prereqs and retain operational errors as unchecked rather than missing configuration.

This task performs irreversible external publication and configuration. It does not enable npm in release/plan.json; the final channel-enablement task does that only after rehearsal.
title: Bootstrap the npm packages and configure trusted publishing

description:
External channel setup after the complete tlrelease Homebrew port is available.

Create or validate DmitryKorolev/homebrew-tap with the expected Formula path and repository protections. Configure the repository credential used only by the stable Homebrew publication job, and verify tlrelease prereqs distinguishes missing, unchecked, and established state.

Exercise tlrelease homebrew publish against a disposable repository first, then confirm an identical formula is an idempotent no-op and a changed formula produces the intended commit without affecting prereleases.

This task changes external repository and credential state. It does not enable Homebrew in release/plan.json; the final channel-enablement task does that only after rehearsal.
title: Create the Homebrew tap and configure publication access

description:
Final repository change after both external channels are configured and the simplified workflow rehearsal is green.

Change release/plan.json from deferred to enabled for npm and Homebrew in one deliberate edit. Remove obsolete plannedFor values, run tlrelease prereqs against live external state, and require zero missing or unchecked blockers for the enabled channels.

Verify the release workflow derives both publication jobs from the plan, stable and prerelease policies remain distinct, the GitHub Release stays the source of signed artifacts, npm publication is resumable and launcher-last, and Homebrew publication is idempotent and stable-only. Re-run real npm pack/install and real Homebrew load, style, audit, install, and test gates.

Do not close until the implementing commit lands on local main. This task enables irreversible publication paths; it does not perform a release.
title: Enable npm and Homebrew in the release plan

description: Write ADR-0028 as the authoritative architecture for release machinery after the simplification campaign. Define the ownership boundary between tlrelease, GitHub workflows, the signed manifest, channel-native tools, and the three retained shell adapters: install.sh, scripts/verify-release-artifacts.sh, and npm/tl/bin/tl. Cover npm and Homebrew as complete downstream projections, explain why the npm launcher remains POSIX shell with exec and no lifecycle hook, define typed external-tool and hermetic enforcement, identify migration-only lexer and PATH-shim infrastructure for deletion, and reference rather than duplicate ADR-0006, ADR-0014, and ADR-0026. Update the ADR index and any direct architectural map references needed for discoverability.
title: Record the simplified release architecture in ADR-0028

description:
Replace release/Consistency.lean guardedCopies while scripts/lib/release-common.sh still exists as a comparison oracle. Platform classification must be checked against release/targets.json and the typed target model; the standalone signing pin must be rendered from release/identity.json; and shared digest, normalization, and classification behavior retained by install.sh, scripts/verify-release-artifacts.sh, or npm/tl/bin/tl must be exercised through their public adapters over one planted corpus. A block that is genuinely safer to generate may instead be rendered from a typed definition and compared byte-for-byte.

Mutation-check every replacement: perturb each old embedded source or typed authority and show that the new guard refuses before deleting the old library. Cover unreadable source, empty corpus, missing adapter, disagreement, and success through the public command. The completion change may remove guardedCopies only after each of its six current comparisons has a named successor.

This task deliberately precedes the policy cutover and shell deletion. It does not delete release-common.sh; it creates the evidence that makes that later deletion safe.
title: Replace retained adapter copy guards with typed authorities

description:
Perform the first real release only after the capability-free cutover rehearsal is green. This is the task that discharges the carried assumption that release.yml has never run past the artifact boundary; the rehearsal itself does not perform a release.

Before acting, obtain explicit owner authorization for the irreversible tag push. Confirm local main and protected origin name the intended reviewed commit, v0.1.0 is unused, the GitHub-only plan state is deliberate, the live prerequisite audit has zero missing or unchecked blockers for enabled channels, and every required local and GitHub gate is green. npm and Homebrew may remain deferred; do not enable either as part of this task.

Create and push the v0.1.0 tag through the documented protected path. Observe every build, handoff, signing, publication, and verification job to completion. Independently download the resulting GitHub Release, run scripts/verify-release-artifacts.sh with required signatures, compare the signed manifest and payload digests, and smoke-test install.sh from the published release on each Supported platform available to the release process. Refuse and preserve evidence on any partial or ambiguous outcome; never repair published immutable state by overwriting it.

After the release is verified, update docs/overview.md to replace the never-run carried assumption with the exact observed run and any residual, land that documentation on local main, and only then close this task.
title: Tag and verify the v0.1.0 GitHub-only release

description: Replace the release decision layer's following preflight plus predictable temporary write with a release-scoped native atomic replacement primitive. Create <destination>.tmp in the destination directory with O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW, write and sync the complete bytes, rename within the held directory, and remove the temporary path only after this invocation created it. ReleaseCore must not import Tl.*; expose a separate release/Sys.lean binding to the audited native object instead. Preserve typed teaching refusals. Public-command fixtures must cover an occupied regular staging file, a dangling staging symlink, refusal without following or deleting it, failed-rename cleanup, and an unwritable destination. Update docs/overview.md to distinguish the closed pre-existing-object class from the remaining operator-controlled-directory assumption.
title: Harden release evidence atomic writes

description: The new release atomic writer has a real phase boundary that its IO Unit / Except String Unit API erases. Repair ffi/tlsys.c and release/Sys.lean so pre-commit failure is distinct from replacement-committed-but-directory-durability-unknown. On Darwin, retry F_FULLFSYNC on EINTR, fall back to fsync only for explicitly unsupported errors, and propagate EIO/ENOSPC/other operational failures; factor the helper so tl_sys_sync receives the same correction. Add an injectable syscall seam and public-command rows for short/zero/EINTR writes, write failure, file sync, close, rename, directory sync after rename, and cleanup ownership. Pin destination and temporary bytes/status for each phase. Map stable error classes to teaching remedies, including invalid leaf, missing parent, permissions, full disk, and post-commit uncertainty. Correct docs/overview.md's nonexistent-parent fixture claim and retain only the genuine operator-controlled-directory residual.
title: Model and fault-test release atomic write phases

description: Replace Tests/ReleaseDriftTests.lean releaseToolHandoffShape's global substring counts with a bounded structural check over .github/workflows/release.yml. Bind the gates job, named stage/digest producer step, releaseToolDigest or releaseToolFileSetHash job-output mapping, pinned upload-artifact action, artifact name, upload source, and every privileged consumer. The current raw transition and ADR-0028 file-set-hash cutover must each have one canonical modeled shape. Mutation fixtures must cover canonical strings only in comments, an unrelated or reordered step, a decoy artifact with the canonical path, the real release-tool artifact using another source, changed output mapping, hidden/multi-file paths, and one omitted consumer. Keep the live non-hidden staging fix; this task makes its drift evidence non-vacuous.
title: Make the release-tool handoff guard structural

description: ADR-0028 currently forbids continue-on-error on authentication/policy/publication steps but does not explicitly forbid jobs.<job_id>.continue-on-error. A privileged job-level override can turn a failed authentication or publication job into a successful workflow result. Amend the authority grammar to refuse job-level continue-on-error on every privileged job and authority-output producer, while preserving the legitimate unprivileged best-effort build use. Add planted privileged/unprivileged fixtures and equivalent-expression mutations to the typed workflow guard and align the tl-yp5g task text.
title: Forbid job-level error overrides in privileged workflows

description: ADR-0028 calls the shell invocation registry closed but still leaves its membership circular: directly supported shells, supported env options, and command/exec option forms are unnamed. Replace that prose with a table enumerating every accepted frontend identity and path form, accepted prefix/interpreter options, literal script-operand position, and refusal behavior. Include direct sh/bash identities, exact path normalization, env forms, command/exec prefixes, and busybox/toybox multi-call forms only where explicitly accepted; every unknown option, -c form, missing/dynamic operand, or unknown frontend refuses. The tl-kpps implementation and mutation corpus derive from this table rather than choosing policy during coding.
title: Specify the closed shell frontend registry exactly

description:
Construct the ReleaseCore policy registry before either workflow cuts over. Gate membership, profile membership, distribution-surface effects, external-tool requirements, strict missing-tool behavior, invocation, completion, and reporting are typed data. GitHub Release, npm, and Homebrew carry publication effects; the installer carries only presence, documentation, and bootstrap-suite effects.

During coexistence, run a temporary parity oracle that requires the typed ci and release gate/profile lists to equal the existing shell policy lists for the same plan. Exercise both directions and mutation-check removal, addition, reassignment, profile drift, and vacuous empty registries. Keep the old shell policy authoritative until parity is green; delete this oracle only in the atomic shell cutover after the typed registry becomes authoritative.

Every pure total acceptance or effect decision whose silent false negative could make a gate, evidence set, or publication decision appear valid gets its characterization theorem and same-change entry in pinnedReleaseVerdictTheorems. Public process fixtures cover tool present or absent, strict or non-strict, pass or fail, multiple requirements, timeout, non-zero completion, malformed invocation, and enabled versus deferred surfaces. This task builds the registry only; its dependent task owns workflow authority grammar and cutover.
title: Build and parity-check the typed release policy registry

description:
Resolve the ADR-0015 and ADR-0019 product-storage question independently of ADR-0028 release writes. ffi/tlsys.c tl_sys_sync currently falls back from F_FULLFSYNC to ordinary fsync after every failure, so EINTR, documented unsupported results, and operational failures such as EIO or ENOSPC are conflated. Tl/Store/Sys.lean and ADR-0019 describe a stronger product durability contract.

Choose and state the product policy explicitly. The recommended policy retries EINTR, accepts fallback only for named platform unsupported errors if ADR-0015 permits the weaker guarantee, and otherwise propagates operational failures; if successful product mutation acknowledgment requires a full platform barrier, an unsupported full barrier is itself a refusal. A shared low-level mechanism may return SyncStrength, but release and product callers apply different policies over it.

Add injected native fault tests for full-barrier success, EINTR retry, each supported fallback errno, ordinary fsync success/failure, EIO, ENOSPC, and error rendering through the public Store path. Amend ADR-0015, ADR-0019, Tl/Store/Sys.lean, and docs/overview.md together so code, contract, and carried residual agree. Do not bundle this product guarantee into the release writer migration.
title: Specify and harden product sync durability semantics

description:
The ci profile of scripts/check-release-policy.sh runs scripts/check-channel-policy.sh, whose npm gate invokes ./.lake/build/bin/tlrelease npm-selftest --root . (since the npm packaging port). ci.yml's release-policy job installs actionlint and nothing else — it has no Lean toolchain by design — so that invocation is a 'No such file or directory' and the gate fails, taking a required job with it.

Reproduced locally against a checkout of HEAD with no .lake: 'scripts/check-channel-policy.sh: line 131: ./.lake/build/bin/tlrelease: No such file or directory', then '::error::release-policy gate failed: npm packaging over the real client'. It has not been observed in CI because main is unpushed since the port landed.

Same shape as the gates that already moved (tlrelease stamp, dependency-boundary, task-id-lint): a gate that is a Lean binary cannot run in a toolchain-free job. Options: move the npm gate to the job that builds the tool, give the release-policy job the binary, or have the channel policy treat an absent tool as a skip — the last only if a skip is honest there, which under --strict it is not.

Distinct from tl-yp5g, which owns the future workflow cutover: this is a live break on main.
title: ci.yml's release-policy job runs a gate that needs the built tlrelease

description:
release/Process.lean states that it deliberately does not scrub the environment because 'the programs here read none' of the repository routing. Three modules now falsify that: release/TaskId.lean (git ls-files), release/Stamp.lean (git, for the build stamp) and release/Homebrew.lean (git, in the tap checkout).

Reproduced: with GIT_INDEX_FILE pointing at an alternate index holding one file, 'tlrelease task-id-lint --root .' reports 'clean - no tracker id in 1 tracked file' and passes over the other 186 tracked entries. Fail-open, in a gate whose other refusals are all fail-closed (an empty scope, an unreadable file and an empty registry each refuse rather than report clean). The deleted scripts/check-task-ids.sh behaved identically, so this is not a regression from the port - it survived it.

Not a CI break: a GitHub job sets none of these. The realistic trigger is a git hook, which exports GIT_INDEX_FILE and GIT_DIR, and any wrapper that runs a release command inside one.

Shape of the fix: a git-specific spawn in release/Process.lean that unsets the routing variables, modelled on Tl/Sync/Ref.lean's scrubbedGitVars (ADR-0012), used by all three callers; hostile-environment command rows for GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE and GIT_INDEX_FILE; and the paragraph in Process.lean's header amended, since it is the sentence that made this look decided.
title: tlrelease spawns git with the caller's repository routing inherited

description:
release/Homebrew.lean pins the author identity of the commit it makes into a tap explicitly (-c user.name, -c user.email) so configuration cannot decide it, and then leaves signing to the operator's global config. A developer with commit.gpgsign=true and gpg.format=ssh gets a signed tap commit; one whose key needs a passphrase gets a prompt in the middle of a publish, and one whose key is absent gets a failed publish.

Reproduced with GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL pointing at a config that signs with a key that does not exist: the production-shaped commit fails with 'Couldn't load public key'. CI is unaffected - a GitHub runner configures neither - so this is about the manual tap-publish boundary an operator runs locally.

The test suite no longer depends on it: fixture repositories carry commit.gpgsign=false locally, so the command's commits into them are unsigned whatever the host says. That was a test-reproducibility fix and deliberately not an answer to this.

The question is whether the command should pin signing the way it pins identity. Arguments both ways: a tap commit is not a release artifact and the release already signs artifacts with cosign, which favours -c commit.gpgsign=false; against, an operator who signs everything may want this signed too, and silently unsigning it is a decision made for them. Whichever way it goes it should be stated in ADR-0006 rather than left to ambient config.
title: tlrelease homebrew-publish signs its tap commit according to the operator's git config

description:
Two guards in Tests/ReleaseDriftTests.lean read CI configuration as flat text where the thing being identified is a position in a structure. Both were shown to report clean on workflows and scripts where nothing runs.

The release-tool artifact handoff guard (stepsOf/jobsOf, Step.runs, Step.mentions) trims each line before deciding, so it loses the indentation that separates a step from a nested list, and latches inSteps on any trimmed 'steps:'. Its matching is substring over step lines. Demonstrated: every release-tool download changed into a checkout action, with the download-action text moved under with.uses, and releaseToolHandoffShape still returned ok.

A guard for the npm channel gate was written on this same pattern and removed rather than shipped. Six readings of it each called the gate present when nothing ran it: a commented-out step, the command named in another field, a key of the same name under env:, the same under with:, a '- run:' line inside a heredoc body, and a nested sequence item. The shell half was worse - the arm was looked up across the whole file rather than within 'case $only', the flag's own spelling was never checked, a deleted flag left nothing to check, and a function with an empty body or one written 'npm_packaging || :' passed on its name.

What to build, in the order it was proposed:

1. One workflow model both guards use: Workflow -> Job -> Step -> direct fields, run body, source line. Take the step-item indentation from the first item and accept a later '- ' item only at that exact column. Only keys at the direct-key column are name/run/uses; nested env, with, sequences and block-scalar bodies are data.

2. Collapse the shell's two-stage selector so the option maps to the function once - '--npm-only) only=npm_packaging ;;' and then "$only" - rather than a flag setting a token and a second case turning the token back into a function. Then there is no correspondence for a guard to reconstruct, and the misrouting, wrong-case and missing-arm classes stop existing instead of becoming detectable.

3. A planted-checkout black-box test per single-gate mode against a stub release tool: the stub was called exactly once with the expected arguments, the poisoned npm environment reached it, success propagates, a distinctive failure status stays a failure, and an unknown or misrouted flag refuses. That is the only instrument that reaches a no-op body or a swallowed status.

The mutation matrix to hold it to: comments, quoted fields, nested env/with, block scalars, nested sequences, wrong job, wrong order, duplicates, option misrouting, wrong-case arms, no-op functions, swallowed failures.

Until this exists, ADR-0026 records that the npm channel gate has no owner: it is in no profile and not in release/Policy.lean, and one step of ci.yml is the only thing that runs it.
title: one workflow model for the release drift guards, and black-box tests for the single-gate modes

description: Adversarial review of the hermetic release harness identified two existing launcher file-existence paths not exercised by the current Alpine image: /lib/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1 as the only glibc loader, and neither a glibc nor a musl loader. The current suite covers platform selection, glibc-present and musl-present behavior but its dynamic shell/utilities require the real musl loader. Add declared, digest-pinned static shell/utility fixtures and an isolated library observation mount, exercising the exact post-pack npm/tl/bin/tl bytes without adding capabilities, changing launcher code, or weakening the read-only image/checkout boundary. Pin the additional input and mount in Tests/ReleaseDriftTests.lean, prove collaborator reachability, and update the explicit coverage residual in docs/overview.md and ADR-0028 when the cases run.
title: Cover the remaining npm launcher loader observations with static fixtures

description: Recent adapter migration iterations repeatedly paid roughly 10-11 minutes for the full supervised tltest suite. Tests/Main.lean currently executes I/O groups sequentially before Tests/Harness.lean prints any results, so early failures stay invisible until all work finishes. Measure per-group wall time and subprocess/fixture costs; add immediate group progress and a supported focused group selector while preserving the default complete run, explicit nonempty-group checks, and worker completion supervision. Test unknown/empty selection, group failures, early worker exits, and default full coverage. Use measurements to remove redundant setup or choose safe parallelism; timing-bearing performance tests need uncontended execution. Keep this local feedback task distinct from cold release-runner provisioning/build measurements.
title: Measure local validation groups and provide supervised focused test runs

description: Local hermetic validation on macOS currently needs ad hoc, untracked Ruby helpers to read the CI YAML run block, supply its environment, and substitute a separately built Linux static release binary. Linux build preparation has also used temporary generated Lake configuration. These are agent-created conveniences, not declared or reproducible project entry points. Replace them with a supported native entry point that prepares the required Linux binary and digest-pinned inputs, invokes Podman with the reviewed restrictions, and reports complete validation. Share the CI recipe or typed authority instead of introducing a second independently maintained recipe. Do not add a fourth tracked shell program or require Python/Ruby for this orchestration; channel-native npm packing and Homebrew validation retain their documented scopes. Cover host/platform handling, missing tools, input/hash failures, process failures, and final completion through tests. Relevant sources: release/Workflow.lean, release/WorkflowContracts.lean, release/Policy.lean, .github/workflows/ci.yml hermetic-release job, Tests/ReleaseDriftTests.lean, and ADR-0028.
title: Provide a native local runner for hermetic release validation

description:
Confirmed adversarial review at commit bf7281728e2daae46a8afc2c82f170e0906b6a88. Tl/Sync/Ref.lean fetchRemoteLog (lines 546-550) fetches into FETCH_HEAD, then resolves and reads that mutable name in separate Git subprocesses. A concurrent ordinary fetch in the same worktree can replace it. Unknown branch-tree entries then ride the preserve-unknown union and can be published into refs/tl/log.

Reproduction: create a local bare remote with a main branch containing ordinary-file and an independent task-log ref. In a clone with a new task to publish, arrange one real git fetch origin refs/heads/main immediately after the first real git fetch origin refs/tl/log, before fetchRemoteLog reads FETCH_HEAD. A PATH wrapper can force this ordering without forging Git output. The first push rejects; the retry succeeds but carries ordinary-file into the remote task-log tree. Observed sync JSON: ok=true, pulled=true, pushed=true. The ordinary branch commit also enters merge ancestry.
