Implement invocation-private fetch isolation and use one immutable OID for the returned parent and all tree reads. Resolving FETCH_HEAD once alone does not close the earlier race. Cover cleanup/error paths and compatibility with the supported Git floor. Add deterministic real-process regression tests for an ordinary concurrent fetch and overlapping sync invocations; assert neither branch entries nor unrelated ancestry enters refs/tl/log, while task union and retry behavior remain correct. See Tests/SyncTests.lean and ADR-0001/0016. Run repository gates. Close as done only after implementing commits land on local main.

Original local evidence (optional, ephemeral): /private/tmp/tl-adversarial-review/reproduce.py and review.md. The reproduction above is self-contained.
title: Isolate sync fetch snapshots from concurrent Git fetches

description:
Confirmed adversarial review at commit bf7281728e2daae46a8afc2c82f170e0906b6a88. Tl/Sync/Local.lean absorbForeign (lines 120-124) skips the own replica unconditionally. Segment union preserves both copies' operations in Git, but neither local copy absorbs its peer's same-replica operations; publication/refresh markers can report reconciliation despite persistent divergent views.

Reproduction: initialize A in a Git clone backed by a local bare remote; create shared baseline and sync. Copy the whole directory, including .git and .tl/local/replica, to B. Create only A in A and only B in B. Alternate successful syncs three times for each. A lists baseline and only A; B lists baseline and only B; the remote segment contains all three create records. No stamp collision or conflicting scalar write is required.

Unique replica ownership is an assumption, but docs/adr/ADR-0007-identity-hlc-ids.md explicitly promises convergence still holds for byte-copied working directories; docs/overview.md repeats that promise. Implement safe recovery for missing same-replica operations (e.g. locked reconciliation preserving local appends and the HLC floor, or duplicate-identity detection with safe remint/recovery). Never overwrite the authoritative own segment via lock-free foreign writeback. Update the assumptions/recovery documentation to match actual guarantees. Add end-to-end copied-replica tests and concurrent local-append/clock-recovery regression coverage for the chosen path; validate all touched shell branches. Run repository gates. Close as done only after implementing commits land on local main.

Original local evidence (optional, ephemeral): /private/tmp/tl-adversarial-review/reproduce.py and review.md. The reproduction above is self-contained.
title: Recover convergence when working copies share a replica ID

description:
Confirmed adversarial review at commit bf7281728e2daae46a8afc2c82f170e0906b6a88. Tl/Sync/Ref.lean runBounded (lines 158-162) stops polling the deadline once the direct child exits, then blocks on outTask.get and errTask.get. A grandchild inheriting either pipe can keep a supposedly bounded Git command blocked indefinitely. Background work from a Git hook/helper is sufficient.

Reproduction: invoke Tl.Sync.runBounded with cmd=/bin/sh, args=[-c, sleep 3 & exit 0], empty stdin and timeoutMs=50. Observed elapsed=3023ms and status=0. The matching Release.run call returns timedOut after approximately 94ms: release/Process.lean runWithEnv already bounds pipe draining. Tests/SyncTests.lean syncTimeoutTests currently covers a still-running direct child, a fast child and zero-timeout opt-out, but misses inherited output pipes.

Apply the deadline to stream completion as well as direct-child exit; preserve the product's explicit timeoutMs=0 opt-out. Reuse the release runner's tested approach where appropriate, with explicit process/reader cleanup semantics. Add product regressions for inherited stdout and stderr, successful early child exit, normal complete output, timeout reporting and the unbounded opt-out. Bound fixtures so test failures cannot hang the suite. Run repository gates. Close as done only after implementing commits land on local main.

Original local evidence (optional, ephemeral): /private/tmp/tl-adversarial-review/Timeout.lean, runnable using lake env lean --run, and review.md. The reproduction above is self-contained.
title: Enforce product Git deadlines through stdout and stderr completion

description:
Reported in another agent session: piping descriptions into tl update --description - replaced eight descriptions with a literal dash. The affected records have not been inspected here. Source inspection confirms the behavior: Tl/Cli/Main.lean handles the explicit stdin sentinel only in create, while update passes the description flag unchanged to cmdUpdate in Tl/Cli/Commands.lean.

Implement explicit stdin support for tl update <id> --description -, consistently with create. This is a CLI consistency/data-loss footgun, not a kernel or CRDT defect.

Acceptance criteria:
- Read stdin only when --description - is explicitly requested. Literal description arguments and updates of other fields must not read stdin or hang on inherited open pipes.
- Read the complete body successfully before emitting any update operation. A read failure must return a stable error with a remedy and preserve every requested field, the prior description, and its timestamps; cover combined-field updates too.
- Pin and document empty/whitespace input and trailing-newline behavior for replacement. Do not blindly reuse create's absent-description normalization: an update must distinguish no replacement from intentionally clearing a description. Preserve multiline and Unicode content according to the documented rule; explain how to supply a literal dash.
- Add public CLI regression tests for stdin replacement, literal input, absent sentinel with a held-open pipe, read failure without writes, empty/whitespace input, trailing newlines, and JSON/human operation. Keep create and note stdin behavior covered; share the input-reading mechanism where appropriate without conflating their field semantics.
- Update Tl/Cli/Grammar.lean help, ADR-0017, relevant usage documentation, and .agents/skills/tl/SKILL.md in the same change. Audit the related text-input commands for the same mismatch.
- Follow repository validation requirements. No automatic repair of the reported eight records without identifying them and recovering their intended descriptions.

History: commit db180ac added the explicit sentinel specifically to fix create hanging on inherited, non-EOF stdin; ADR-0017 section 8 and create tests describe that command-specific contract. The reviewed history contains no rationale for update treating the same flag differently. A missed cross-command consistency check is an inference, not a recorded design decision. Related to the original create stdin fix and the pending editor-description work; this task is independently actionable.
title: Make update --description - read stdin without silently overwriting descriptions

description: Improve the human tl show relationship display: named sections with one row per parent, prerequisite, dependent and related issue, showing unambiguous short IDs, sanitized titles, effective status, priority and epic markers using existing display conventions. Keep completed prerequisites visible, retain cycle-safe children rendering, and show a clearly defined direct-child completion summary. Missing referenced tasks must be disclosed without inventing a status or priority. Preserve the JSON schema and existing canonical-parent semantics. Cover plain/Unicode/color modes, empty sections, hostile text, missing endpoints, closed/deferred/blocked states, child rollup and cyclic/shared child graphs with rendering and public CLI tests. Update ADR-0017. Use the existing indexed View so rendering does not rescan the whole state per row. The user supplied illustrative output from another project; do not copy its content into artifacts. This is separate from the pending stdin update fix in the working tree.
title: Show relationship titles, status and priorities in readable sections

description: Upgrade lean-toolchain from v4.33.1 to v4.34.0, pin a compatible immutable Mathlib and Batteries revision with matching transitive manifest, regenerate build metadata and license notices, and repair compiler or proof API incompatibilities without weakening verified claims. Validate a warning-free full build, trust verifier, complete compiled test suite, task-ID lint, and applicable release policy gates. Record upstream dependency availability or local platform limitations explicitly. Leave open until implementing commits land on local main.
title: Upgrade the Lean toolchain to v4.34.0

description:
Problem: tl why on a blocked child can show a substantial dependency tree, while why on its parent epic reports no open blockers and tells the user to check status/epic/defer. Users reasonably expect the epic query to explain what remains before completion. Current cmdWhy in Tl/Cli/Commands.lean traverses only explicit live blocking edges through State.whyFastH; parent edges are outside that relation.

Acceptance criteria:
- Explain an unfinished epic through its effectively unclosed children, recursively expanding nested epics and unresolved task dependencies. Expand unfinished children of an epic encountered as a blocker too.
- Distinguish unfinished-child relationships from explicit dependency relationships in both human and machine-readable explanations. Do not imply that dependencies control epic rollup: children determine effective completion, while blocking edges govern readiness. Preserve existing readiness, rollup and mutation semantics.
- Replace the generic empty-graph message with a concrete explanation for ready, in-progress, closed, deferred and epic states, including already-complete and cancelled epics. Define traversal stopping rules for effectively closed nodes.
- Remain total on parent, dependency and mixed cycles; handle shared descendants, multiple parents and missing endpoints according to existing merge semantics, with clear cycle/shared-reference rendering. Use indexed adjacency and memoized traversal rather than whole-state scans per node.
- Design an explicit compatible JSON extension under ADR-0008/ADR-0020. Preserve the existing blockedBy meaning; do not silently reclassify children as blocking edges. Record any necessary contract decision before changing schemas.
- Prove the new pure explanation traversal properties in the kernel, preserving the existing dependency-only why correctness claim or explicitly evolving the specification and landmarks. Relevant code: Tl/Kernel/Ready.lean, Reach.lean and ReadyFast.lean; human renderer and cmdWhy in Tl/Cli; ADR-0003, ADR-0004, ADR-0017 and ADR-0020.
- Ship shell and public CLI tests for a parent with no direct blockers whose child has a deep dependency chain, nested epics, epic blockers, shared work, cycles, closed/cancelled/deferred states, missing references, plain/Unicode/color rendering and JSON compatibility. Update user-facing help and documentation. Run repository validation gates before completion.
title: Explain unfinished epic work and its dependencies in tl why

description: The unblocks command still renders legacy issueLine rows while why uses styled task rows. Reuse the shared glyph, status, priority, short-ID and color conventions for human unblocks output, respecting plain/color/glyph controls and sanitization. Preserve the existing ready-difference query, JSON data contract and empty-result meaning. Cover populated and empty output and terminal modes in CLI tests; document the human presentation in ADR-0017.
title: Match unblocks human output to the shared task-row style

description:
Owner action, after the tap-commit signing code lands and alongside the tap setup.

- Decide the release committer identity. GitHub shows an SSH-signed commit as Verified only when the signing key is registered on the account that owns the committer email, so the pinned tl-release@users.noreply.github.com (no account) would read Unverified. Options: a dedicated machine account (its noreply email, key registered there) or accept Unverified and rely on the tool's own pre-push check.
- Generate a dedicated unencrypted ed25519 signing key for that identity (never a personal key). Commit its public half and the committer name/email to release/tap-signer.json.
- Store the private key as HOMEBREW_TAP_SIGNING_KEY in the protected release environment. Keep an offline copy only if manual publishing is intended.
- Inspect the tap's branch rules and record what is actually enabled. A "require signed commits" rule accepts any GitHub-verified signature and is not an allowlist of this signer; state that in ADR-0006 and do not describe it as enforcement of the signer.
- Run tlrelease prereqs and a homebrew-publish --dry-run, then one publish against a disposable tap with the real key, confirming the tap commit verifies against release/tap-signer.json.
Enabling the channel (release/plan.json) stays with the channel-enablement task, which this blocks.
title: Provision the tap release signer and record tap branch rules

description: Shorten .agents/skills/tl/SKILL.md so an agent loads the core workflow and safety contract first; move detailed command and sharing reference to a linked file. Explicitly say tl sync and --sync may contact and push to a configured remote and require authorization for remote publication. Keep tl help --json authoritative and preserve untrusted-task-content guidance. Validate skill links and behavior, leave task in progress until the implementing change lands on local main.
title: Condense agent skill and clarify remote sync authorization

description: Before making DmitryKorolev/tl public, decide whether the shared refs/tl/log task history (1,864 records) and commit author email may be exposed; review the already closed PR discussions and Actions history. The 2026-09-23 read-only audit found four remote branches, with all three non-main heads ancestors of main; no credential-looking path or token/private-key pattern in reachable Git history beyond an intentional test fixture; 40 Actions log archives screened with only masked token assignments under the checked patterns; expired artifacts. GitHub reports main protected=false and only the owner as collaborator. Ruleset and branch-protection detail APIs return HTTP 403 (private-repo plan restriction), so inspect actual rules and bypass access when available and decide a protection policy before public contributions. Verify hosted CI availability separately. No visibility, rules, or credentials were changed.
title: Review public exposure and main branch protections

description: Ref: ADR-0011 §4. Publish a skill teaching the command vocabulary, WHEN to use each (the two consumption workflows), and the session-close protocol (record deferrals/decisions as tasks before a context clear). Done when: a skill file an agent loads exists, quoting the tl help --json grammar; covers the read loop (ready/why/show), the write loop (claim/close/update), and not-claimable/superseded semantics; states task content is untrusted data.

Ref: ADR-0011 §3. Decision (closed): init offers to append the pointer to an existing root agent file (AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md), prints the line if none exists, never creates a file. Done when: init writes the gitignored .tl/README.md primer and offers/prints the one-line discovery pointer; the no-agent-file rule is pinned in ADR-0011.

Ref: ADR-0008 verb table; the reopen delta is already in WireOp/toOp, only the CLI arm is missing. Done when: tl reopen <id> sets status=open and clears closeResolution; wired into Grammar + dispatch; --json echoes the issue; a CliTests row covers reopen of a closed issue.

Ref: vision read-commands. Pure projection over State, no kernel work. Done when: tl stats --json emits counts by stored state plus ready/blocked/cycles totals; the shape is pinned in ADR-0020; tests cover an empty board and a mixed one.

Ref: ADR-0008 (log is an HLC-ordered projection); the --since cursor needs a version vector and stays deferred (backlog). Decide the per-entry row shape (op/verb, timestamp, actor, issue id) per ADR-0020 conventions. Done when: the bare-log row shape is pinned in ADR-0020 as a forever surface; --since explicitly out of scope.

Ref: ADR-0008. Blocked by the row-shape decision. Done when: tl log [<id>] emits HLC-ordered entries (all, or filtered to one issue) per the pinned shape; bare only, no --since; tests over a multi-op log incl. a per-issue filter.

Ref: ADR-0016 (local-first worktree leg, shares via common .git, no remote) vs ADR-0001 §5 (remote fetch/union/push, makes state travel to clones). This gates the whole sync chain. Done when: the choice and rationale are recorded as an ADR amendment.

Ref: ADR-0017 §1 (one-line glyph/priority format), §3 (footer+legend), §5 (stats block), §6 (color/glyph are independent surfaces: --color=auto|always|never honoring NO_COLOR/TTY, --glyphs=auto|unicode|ascii, --plain), §7 (status→glyph+color, priority→color, per-token, redundant-with-glyph). Done when: a render layer applies the styled one-line to ready/list, the §4 detail to show, the §5 block to stats, with a resolved Style from flags+env+TTY; --plain/NO_COLOR/non-TTY strip ANSI; tests cover the glyph/color mapping and the strip.

Switch effectiveStatus from fuel-bounded descent (effStatusAux with present-issue-count fuel) to the memoized shape: visiting — the current recursion path — detects a parent cycle at the exact node (a global visited set would mistake shared DAG children for cycles), and memo caches completed statuses so each node is evaluated once per query; the fuel form can re-evaluate shared descendants combinatorially on diamond-shaped parent DAGs. Semantics unchanged: manual Cancelled precedence, cycle-trapped epics fall back conservatively (never Done), dangling children inert. Proof obligations (ADR-0003 §3 amendment): totality by well-founded recursion on the unvisited measure; re-prove acyclic exactness (effectiveStatus_epic) and the never-Done cycle guarantee over the new shape — directly, or via a characterization (recurrence) lemma that quarantines the memo-coherence invariant in one proof; an equivalence bridge to a reference is admissible scaffolding, not a requirement, and no unmemoized version ships. Recommended additional theorem: once-per-query — an id present in memo is never recomputed. Wall-clock stays tested, never proved.

title: Ergonomics improvements

description: Build dep path A B (show a dependency path — the cycle-breaking tool) and dep critical (rank open issues by transitive dependent-count; the weight function is the Stage-0 kernel one). Decided 2026-06-11: no separate dep tree verb — the up/down dependency trees render on the question-shaped verbs instead: why <id> renders its transitive unclosed blockers as the upward tree, and unblocks <id> (planned with the read facets) renders the downward dependents tree; both reuse the generic treeLines renderer and must stay total on cyclic/dangling graphs. ADR-0017 §2 and vision.md record the fold.
title: Dep utilities: dep path + dep critical; tree renders on why/unblocks

description: The refs/tl/log transport epic. Landed children: git-plumbing ref read/write + CAS, the complete-line union merge, the local worktree leg, read-time ref-OID refresh, the remote fetch/union/push leg with rejection retry. Open children carry the remaining freshness/disclosure surface: auto-sync, claim --verify/--sync, doctor sync posture, the ready staleness advisory, degraded-read disclosure, the write-path freshness decision, ref-name validation on absorb, and second-local-leg reporting. ADR-0001/0016/0021 govern.

Human/agent CLI ergonomics on top of the pinned JSON contract (ADR-0020 shapes never change here): tree-by-default list, short display ids, defer/undefer, close --cascade, the read facets (list --stale/--deferred, unblocks), label/stats/claim output polish. Children carry the specifics; ADR-0017 governs human output.

Wire ADR-0021: after a successful transact, a post-transaction hook reads git config tl.autosync and, when true, runs syncLocal best-effort (publish own segment + absorb siblings). A hook failure must never fail the write — surface it as a non-fatal note, stderr and a --json field, per ADR-0021 §4. The remote leg stays explicit tl sync. Ships with tests: autosync unset/false (default off), true (sibling sees the write after no explicit sync), hook-failure disclosure, and the no-git degrade.

Pin tl defer input parsing before implementing (ADR-0010): timezone semantics for bare dates (local vs UTC), what a bare date means (start vs end of day), the --for duration base (from now), accepted units/formats, and the JSON echo of the resolved deferUntil instant. Outcome: an ADR-0010 amendment the implement task builds against.

Build tl defer <id> --until <when> / --for <dur> and tl undefer <id>, setting/clearing deferUntil (ADR-0010). The read side already exists: ready excludes deferred issues, show/stats render them. Blocked on the parsing decide task. Ships with tests: set/clear round-trip, ready exclusion until expiry, bad-input usage errors, the JSON echo.

Switch effectiveStatus from fuel-bounded descent (effStatusAux with present-issue-count fuel) to the memoized shape: visiting — the current recursion path — detects a parent cycle at the exact node (a global visited set would mistake shared DAG children for cycles), and memo caches completed statuses so each node is evaluated once per query; the fuel form re-evaluates shared descendants combinatorially on diamond-shaped parent DAGs. Profile evidence makes this the dominant read fix: at N=400, effectiveStatus is 8165/8183 samples of tl list (via the effClosed filter), because every call recomputes presentIssues (O(N^2)) for the fuel and presentChildren per node — list is Theta(N^3) today. The switch must therefore also hoist presentIssues/presentEdges out of the per-node recursion, or ship as a batched effStatusAll : State -> AMap IssueId Status with one pointwise agreement lemma against effectiveStatus, so a list does one rollup pass total. Semantics unchanged: manual Cancelled precedence, cycle-trapped epics fall back conservatively (never Done), dangling children inert. Reproduced on the built binary: 'tl create "title"' with stdin a pipe/fd that is OPEN but never EOFs blocks INDEFINITELY in readToEnd (fread), emitting nothing.

CORRECTION after reading the code: there IS already an isTty guard (Tl/Cli/Main.lean:149-150) — an interactive terminal correctly yields no body (pure none). The gap is specifically a NON-tty stdin that never reaches EOF: an agent that spawns tl with an inherited/held-open pipe (not /dev/null, not closed) hits the else-branch (Main.lean:152 readToEnd) and hangs. This is ADR-0017 §8 behavior by design ('a non-TTY stdin is read to EOF as the body').

So this is a CONTRACT change, not a surgical guard, and needs a decision: (a) require an explicit '-' / '--description -' sentinel to opt into the stdin body (safest; amends ADR-0017 §8); or (b) document loudly that callers must pass </dev/null or close stdin, and accept the footgun as standard Unix (like cat). A non-blocking peek is NOT reliable (a slow pipe writer looks idle). Recommend (a). Ship with a test: create with an open non-EOF stdin must not block; piped body with EOF still works; tty yields no body. Whoever takes this: amend ADR-0017 §8 in the same change.

NATIVE PROFILING REFRAME (2026-06-13, compiled exe Prof.lean, 4000 issues — supersedes the interpreted /tmp/prof3 numbers, which were ~7x inflated):

- effStatusAll native = 1590ms (cyclic synthetic, the COMMON case) / 927ms (deep 4000-chain). So it is the #1 view-build cost (~1.5s) and quadratic on the ORDINARY case, not only deep nesting. It is the largest single contributor to the ~2.23s warm-read floor (the other ~1.0s half is cache decode, now filed as tl-hkc3crt114b3z4ab).
- effStatusAll has THREE co-equal quadratic sources, all inside rollupVisit/rollupKids (RollupFast.lean), all must be fixed for it to go near-linear:
  1. kidsOfEdges pe i = (pe.filter (p.1==i)).map(.2) — an O(E) scan PER NODE ⇒ O(N*E). Fix: bucket once with bucketBy pe (getD_bucketBy bridge EXISTS in HashMapView).
  2. memo : AMap IssueId Status — find/insert O(N) per node ⇒ O(N^2). Fix: Std.HashMap memo.
  3. path.contains c — O(depth) per kid ⇒ O(N^2) on a deep chain. Fix: a companion Std.HashSet for path membership.
- Item "parentEdges" (the old item 2): native s.parentEdges (spec, hasIssue-per-edge) = 173ms, NOT 1183ms. loadView ALREADY routes through parentEdgesFast (=1ms, committed). The remaining 173ms is effStatusAll's INTERNAL `let pe := s.parentEdges` — fold that into the same fix (pass the fast/bucketed pe in).

PROOF GATE: the bridge effStatusAll_find / effStatusWith_eq must survive. The recursion's termination (path-filtered present-set measure) and soundness (rollupVisit_sound/rollupKids_sound, Coherent) are AMap-shaped; swapping the memo to HashMap + bucketed kids + path-set means re-deriving those proofs (AMap.find_insert -> Std.HashMap.getElem?_insert; carry bucket=bucketBy pe and path-set=path invariants) OR proving effStatusAllH = effStatusAll via a memo-simulation invariant. Substantial; do as a focused verified change.

notes:
SHA SPIKE MEASURED (2026-06-13, compiled ShaBench.lean, 2.4MB input, byte-exact verified vs spec on 8 inputs incl. the 2.4MB):
- current Sha256.digest = 155 ms/call
- fast unboxed sliding-window SHA-256 (8 hash words as let-mut locals, one reused 16-word window, no per-block zip/toList/64-entry schedule) = 77 ms/call = ONLY ~2x
- FNV-1a64 non-crypto checksum = 3 ms/call = ~50x

VERDICT: do NOT optimize SHA. Pure-Lean tops out ~2x (Array bounds-checks + inherent round work dominate, not boxing), and it would still owe a multi-day representation-shift fast=spec proof (ADR-0018). Instead use a fast NON-CRYPTO checksum for the cache: ADR-0014 already trusts .tl (the cache is the discardable, rot-detection artifact, not a security surface), so collision-resistance is not required. ~50x on the hash; the cache's two passes (~0.5s) drop to ~0.01-0.02s. Proof cost ~= none (new function + a round-trip/rot test; no FIPS spec to match).

STILL NEEDS the ADR-0014/0018 trust-wording note + sign-off before implementing (this is the Q1 decision). The correct fast SHA and the FNV reference impl are preserved at /tmp/ShaBench.lean.

DECISION (2026-06-13, signed off): replace the cache's SHA-256 with Lean CORE's non-crypto hash -- ByteArray.hash (@[extern lean_byte_array_hash], opaque/C, UInt64) -- for BOTH the decodeCache payload-integrity check and the cacheValid prefix check. Verified in core: Init/Data/ByteArray/Basic.lean defines ByteArray.hash : @& ByteArray -> UInt64 (extern) + a Hashable ByteArray instance; String.hash (extern) also exists. ByteArray.hash takes RAW bytes, so the non-UTF-8 log-prefix check is safe (never route segment bytes through String -- it panics).

WHY: the cache is rot-detection, not security -- ADR-0014 already trusts everything in .tl (the cache is the discardable artifact; tampering is the segments' domain), so crypto collision-resistance is not required. Measured (compiled, 2.4MB): SHA = 155ms; cache does TWO passes (~0.5s/read). A non-crypto hash = ~3ms (~50x); core ByteArray.hash (C) is at least as fast. The SHA half of the decode floor (~0.5s) drops to ~0.01-0.02s.

NOT a fast=spec bridge (there is no SHA spec to match): the cache integrity primitive becomes a TRUSTED core extern -- same posture as String.hash, already trusted throughout -- covered by a round-trip/rot test, not a proof. (The hand-rolled FNV-1a64 alternative is at /tmp/ShaBench.lean for reference; core ByteArray.hash is preferred: faster, zero code, from core.)

DELIVERABLES (shell tier):
1. Tl/Store/Cache.lean: replace shaHexOf (Sha256) with ByteArray.hash on the payload bytes and on (sd.bytes.extract 0 m.byteLen). CacheSegMeta.shaHex (hex String) becomes a UInt64 (store as decimal/hex string in JSON); update encSegMeta/decSegMeta + encodeCache/decodeCache. The 'equal byteLen => equal hash' fast-fresh shortcut still holds.
2. BUMP cacheVersion (format + integrity-primitive change).
3. ADR amendment: ADR-0022 (cache integrity is now ByteArray.hash, not SHA) + ADR-0014 trust wording (cache uses a 64-bit non-crypto rot-check; accidental collision ~2^-64; adversarial out-of-scope, segments are the trust domain) + docs/overview.md Trusted (the cache-integrity carried assumption moves from 256-bit SHA to a 64-bit non-crypto extern hash).
4. Tests/CacheTests.lean: codec round-trip + every validity branch re-checked with the new hash; corruption-detection (a flipped byte => rebuild) still passes.

PREVENT (tl-99mnzwt0): an end-to-end latency assertion so a silent revert to SHA (50x slower warm read) is caught.

description:
Read/write paths shell out to git (refresh, auto-sync-local) and sync shells out over the network (fetch/push/ls-remote) with NO timeout, so a hung git — a stale index/ref lock, a credential helper waiting on input, an unreachable remote — hangs the tl command silently and unboundedly. For a tracker driving an agent's ready->claim->close loop, a silent indefinite hang is a bad failure mode.

Fix: bound every git invocation with a wall-clock timeout, killing the child (SIGTERM) on expiry. All git calls route through two primitives in Tl/Sync/Ref.lean — git (text, IO.Process.output) and gitBytes (bytes, spawn). Replace both with a single bounded spawn helper (runBounded): spawn piped, drain stdout+stderr on tasks (no pipe deadlock), wait via a short tryWait poll (no added thread; <=~10ms fast-path latency), and on expiry kill + return the conventional timeout exit 124 with a teaching stderr. Modeling timeout as a non-zero exit means EVERY existing caller already handles it: best-effort calls (refresh/auto-sync) fall to the existing 'degraded' note path (refreshFromRef already catches Tl.Error and IO.Error), explicit calls throw internal with the timeout reason.

Per-call timeout, not global: the text git primitive serves both local plumbing AND the network legs. Short local bound (~5s; local plumbing on a tiny ref is sub-second) threaded as the default; longer remote bound (~30s) passed at exactly the network sites (ls-remote/fetch in fetchRemoteLog, push in pushRefLog). Constants for now; a git-config knob (tl.gitTimeoutMs / tl.gitRemoteTimeoutMs) is a possible follow-up.

Safe semantics: best-effort calls -> degraded (eventual consistency, ADR-0016). The explicit remote legs are atomic at the ref level server-side, so a killed client mid-push/fetch leaves either 'ref moved' or 'didn't' — never corruption. Tested-shell tier: a deterministic test exercises the kill path via runBounded over  (timeout -> 124) and a fast process ( -> 0), no hung git needed.

Note: the progress-signal/spinner half of the original task was split out (it was largely moot once the perf epic dropped reads under ~1s) into a separate low-priority task.

REOPENED — the forward-BFS attempt (branch perf/blockspath-bfs, commit b1e518b) is NOT a real fix and must NOT merge; /code-review caught it. MEASURED on a 300-node blocks chain: dep path = 62s (new bfsPath) vs 71s (old wbPath on main) vs why = 0.18s and tl list = 0.14s. So BOTH old and new dep path are catastrophically slow and roughly equal; my doc/commit 'now costs the same as why / single sweep' was FALSE. ROOT CAUSE: why does ONE reachClosure sweep via the SATURATING reachFix (ReadyFast.lean); dep path does ~N sweeps — old re-derives reachClosure per walk-back level, new's path map is a CLOSURE TOWER (pathState's .2 is a function; each lookup re-descends and re-forces pathState per level, the let-binding does NOT help). The proofs are correct (blocksPath_valid/isSome_iff unchanged, axiom-clean) — the defect is purely cost. REAL FIX: MATERIALIZE the path map (a concrete AMap/assoc-list threaded by the fold, or a parent map reconstructed once) so the build is one sweep and lookup is a flat read — that takes dep path to ~why's 0.2s (~300x). Re-prove the pathState invariant over the materialized map (the public theorems stay). Optionally also adopt reachFix's early-saturation exit. This is the genuine tl-dh6t deliverable.

EPIC. The entire reach cone is superlinear (O(N^2)-O(N^3) worst-case), NOT O(V+E). ROOT CAUSE: reachStep (Tl/Kernel/Ready.lean:41) = dedup (acc ++ acc.flatMap succ), and dedup (:28) is a foldr with an O(M) membership test per element ⇒ O(M^2) per round; reachClosure iterates it N times RE-SCANNING the whole accumulator ⇒ O(N^3) on a chain. Everything built on it inherits this: why (whyFast→reachFix), weight/dep critical (weightFast→reachFix), dep cycles (onCycle/reachClosure), and dep path (blocksPath). reachFix's early-exit only helps shallow graphs (a chain saturates at depth N → no early exit). They are fast in absolute terms only because the native list constant is tiny (why=0.18s@300). GOAL: a frontier-based reach engine — process each node's successors EXACTLY ONCE (worklist/frontier, not whole-accumulator re-scan) with a Std.HashSet visited (O(1) membership) ⇒ O(V+E). This is the deferred tl-whp0xy1 generalized to the whole cone. Children to file: (1) frontier reachStep + HashSet dedup with a reachClosure-equivalence bridge (the keystone); (2) rewire why/weight/cycles onto it via the existing _eq bridges; (3) dep path O(V+E) via a frontier BFS + parent map (subsumes tl-dh6t's true-O(V+E) goal — record parent at discovery, no predecessor search, reconstruct once). Substantial Mathlib-zone proof work (HashSet/HashMap reasoning via HashMapView; the memory flags the reachStep piece 'substantial+risky'). Filed 2026-06-19 per owner decision.

PROPOSED design (2026-07-01 survey, adversarially verified; pending ratification). Platform: GitHub Actions. Jobs: lint (fast greps, advisory except the Mathlib-scope allowlist) -> build-and-test (matrix ubuntu-latest + macos-latest; lake build --wfail, then lake exe tltest from the repo root) -> git-floor. Warning gate = lake build --wfail: EMPIRICALLY VERIFIED on v4.30.0 (exits 1 on warnings incl. cache-replayed ones; the repo passes it today, 1344 jobs). A log-grep gate was DISPROVEN -- the real warning format has no ./ prefix, the proposed grep matches nothing. git 2.17: build 2.17.1 from a hash-pinned tarball on the modern runner (NO_CURL/NO_PERL minimal build, ~1-2 min, cached), assert git --version = 2.17.1, PATH override scoped to the test steps only (lake's own git stays modern). ubuntu:18.04 container REJECTED: node20-based actions need glibc>=2.28 vs 18.04's 2.27 (node16 fallback sunset), EOL apt, and it forces a second toolchain install. Caches: ~/.elan (keyed on lean-toolchain), ~/.cache/mathlib (manifest+toolchain key, OS-agnostic ok), .lake/packages SOURCES (manifest key), and a tl-only .lake/build (sha-suffixed + restore-keys). NEVER glob .lake/packages/*/.lake/build -- that re-ships the ~5 GB of mathlib oleans per commit and thrashes the 10 GB budget. Verified: all 8 dep revs in lake-manifest.json byte-match mathlib's own manifest, so lake exe cache get is a full hit; add 'cache get reports full hits' to the ADR-0009 pin-bump checklist. Evaluate leanprover/lean-action@v1 before hand-rolling. concurrency cancel-in-progress only on non-main refs (main runs populate the caches PRs restore). sorry/axiom greps are advisory fast-fail only -- verified holes: same-line attribute forms, native_decide/ofReduceBool (no token, no warning), axioms in out-of-Tl/ dirs; the closure is the checked-in print-axioms probe (own related task). Task-ID lint ships advisory until its regex decision (own related task) lands. Branch protection on the four checks once green; no merge queue (single contributor). Expected ~15-25 min warm PR latency. Floor smoke: tl init + tl doctor --json in a scratch repo asserting the gitVersion row is ok at a real 2.17.

PROPOSED defaults + semantics (2026-07-01 survey, adversarially verified; pending ratification). DEFAULT: fail-closed force-required (existing code, exit 6, no new error code), COLLECT-ALL violations in one pass; the message names the first few + total count and teaches the fix; Error.context carries the machine-readable violation list. --allow-large: proceed VERBATIM + one disclosure per violation; NEVER truncate (the native write path is cap-free -- cmdCreate/cmdUpdate/label/meta have no storage caps -- and Sanitize.lean:12-14 pins 1KiB/64KiB as render-only bounds; a truncating import would be lossier than tl update on the same content). --max stays total-bytes-only, giving the raise-total-keep-granular-armed middle setting for free; NO per-bound override flags -- record the exclusion in ADR-0005. DEFAULTS (UTF-8 bytes; justified against the render bounds + measured own-log usage, title max 133 B / desc max 5.8 KB): title and every single-line field 1024; description 65536; notes 65536; label bytes 1024; meta key 1024 (check the DERIVED import:<key> name too); meta value 4096; labels-count 64; meta-count 64 (pre-dedup, incl. up to 3 derived keys: ext:<tag>, import:source, duplicate-of); edges-count 128 (raw pre-skip list lengths); parent-depth 64 via a MEMOIZED single pass over the parent DAG (a naive per-record walk is O(n^2) -- ADR-0023 violation). CRITIQUE CORRECTIONS to fold in: (1) parent CYCLES are a disclosure only, never a bounds violation -- the native path deliberately permits longer cycles (Commands.lean:1495-1496, matching dep add) and the kernel is provably total on them; (2) ADD the ADR-MANDATED SEED-SIZE bound -- ADR-0005:129 pins total input/seed size and the input-only reading drops it; buildSeed amplifies ~40x worst case via label fan-out; suggest 4x maxBytes, checked after buildSeed and before writeForeignSegment; (3) checkBounds must run BEFORE initTarget (Commands.lean:2178) or a bounds-refused import leaves a freshly created .tl/; (4) amend ADR-0005:131 '(or a raised --max) proceeds' to scope --max to the byte bounds, and fix ADR-0014 T6's --force/--max conflation plus its stale dotted-id wording; (5) record the JSON-nesting pre-parse exposure (deep [ / { recursion before any granular check) as a carried limitation, or add a raw-line-length bound (~1 MB/line) on the same gate. Hook: a pure checkBounds in Tl/Import/Bulk.lean between the parse loop and buildSeed (finally consuming opts.allowLarge, dead weight there today). Tests per bound: exactly-at-bound passes / over-bound fails naming bound+record / over-bound + --allow-large proceeds verbatim with the disclosure and the stored field surviving (differential show); plus collect-all, cycle-disclosure, max-raised-but-granular-armed, and byte-stable re-import rows (pattern: CliTests.lean:3183-3270).

Keep Rekor inclusion required; publish per-asset Sigstore bundles (offline-capable modulo the cosign TUF root). Pin homes: install.sh (operative; a loud TL_INSTALL_SKIP_SIG=1 escape that still enforces SHA-256 digests, failure text includes cosign install one-liners), VERIFYING.md with an identity-history table (old artifacts stay verifiable forever), the Homebrew formula, and ADR-0006 -- plus a drift-guard test keeping all pin copies identical. Rotation: identity change = schema-bump-class event (update pin + history table + release-notes headline; old pinned installers fail closed, correctly). (2) NETWORK FS: detect-and-warn; never refuse, never per-lock-acquisition. New shim fstatfs probe opening its OWN no-follow fd (Paths.lean validate closes its fds -- nothing to reuse) + a pure unit-testable classifier over (flags, fstype): darwin MNT_LOCAL plus a FUSE-ambiguous tier (macFUSE volumes lack MNT_LOCAL -- same softened wording as linux); linux magics with vboxsf added as definite-remote, FUSE/9p ambiguous (WSL /mnt/c is 9p -- never hard-error). Record in ADR-0015; teaching warn text points at a local clone or --dir/TL_DIR. (3) DISCOVERY: scrub the GIT_DIR family (GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_COMMON_DIR, GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY, GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES, GIT_INDEX_FILE, GIT_NAMESPACE) from EVERY shelled git via ONE shared spawn baseline -- including readTimeoutNat (Ref.lean:96-97), not just git/gitBytes; keep auth/config vars and GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES. Keep the discovery walk git-free; close the ascend-past-bare read hazard with the cheap fs-only bare-gitdir heuristic (HEAD + objects/ + refs/ present => boundary) rather than accepting it as a residual; doctor gains a split-brain check (walk classification vs inGitRepo disagreement). PROPOSED pinned design (2026-07-01 survey; the first draft's placement was OVERTURNED by adversarial review -- this is the corrected form; pending ratification). DELIVERABLE = the pinned ADR decision, not the implementation (ADR-0008:397-399 records GC is not needed at expected scale; destructive Stage B stays deferred until a real size trigger). Pin: (1) TRANSPORT PRESERVE-UNKNOWN -- sync today silently drops any non-replica-named tree entry from refs/tl/log on every sync (readRefAt name filter Ref.lean:183-187 + buildCommit :206-217; verified live). Carry unknown tree entries through verbatim (the transport-level analogue of the record-level preserve-unknown rule, ADR-0008:242-243). Freeze-sensitive, build pre-release -- spun out as its own blocked-by-this task. (2) PLACEMENT: the snapshot is a reserved NON-replica-named tree entry in refs/tl/log, line-unioned like any segment (concurrent compactors' records both survive), never enumerated as an on-disk segment (Segment.lean:44-49 junk filter unchanged). REJECTED: a synthetic-replica snapshot segment (a permanent violation of the replica-id-uniqueness Trusted assumption, overview.md:249-252, plus forged owner stamps poisoning provenance); a non-replica name without (1) (old binaries silently drop it); a separate ref (breaks single-commit atomicity); a frontier-dropping union (silently loses never-observed ops -- the ADR-0008:452-455 class). (3) Trimmed segments carry v:2 compacted marker records via an owner-check CARVE-OUT in Materialize (not forged owner stamps); note markers sort into byte order after any union -- never claim first-line position. (4) HONEST mixed-version text in the ADR: an old binary post-compaction reads ok:true with an under-folded board (foreign-segment refusals do not fail commands, ADR-0008:299-307) and its syncs REGROW the trimmed lines from its on-disk foreign caches (reconcile unions pre-absorb local segments, Local.lean:163-167; the union never re-shrinks). Physical removal converges only after full v2 adoption + repeated compacts. Pin ONE of: regrowth-until-recompact as the accepted disclosed cost (RECOMMENDED -- the overlap-tolerance theorem makes resurrection state-harmless and no workload needs hard size bounds yet), or a v2 sync-side trim-at-marker with its residual never-observed-op hazard disclosed as part of the destructive confirmation. (5) CRASH ORDER pinned: ref CAS (snapshot + trimmed blobs) -> absorb -> own-segment trim LAST (atomic rename under the mutation lock); any crash then degrades to harmless regrowth, never loss. (6) THEOREMS: Thm1 fold-preservation = the reserved wording, discharged by filter-partition + fold_perm/fold_append (Theorems.lean:127/139); Thm2 OVERLAP TOLERANCE -- fold equal for ANY retained superset of above-F (via fold_eq_of_mem_iff, Theorems.lean:113) -- the theorem that makes keep-everything unions provably safe; worth recording in the ADR regardless of placement; Thm3 frontier-join (belowF of the pointwise-max frontier = union of belowF sets). Causal stability of F stays an explicit tier-3 carried assumption (compact requires a successful preflight fetch + an explicit destructive confirmation). Compact preconditions: abort on any refused segment; the frontier excludes skew-deferred lines; a re-trim always recomputes a fresh snapshot from currently visible lines, never re-cuts at the old F. Also in the pin: snapshot/compacted records exempt from skew deferral, reseed floor from max(frontier), cacheVersion bump, additive compacted-gap error code + resync cursor for log --since below the horizon (ADR-0025:123-131), tl log earlier-ops-compacted disclosure, and feed/stats/provenance hygiene excluding both record kinds. STAGE A (the ADR-0022 §4 shared non-destructive snapshot for cold clones/CI) is buildable independently: no v bump, no union change, no theorem debt.

title: Release and repository safety gates

description: Problem: tl selects its state directory and repository from filesystem discovery, then invokes Git with git -C <repo>. Git still honors inherited routing variables such as GIT_DIR and GIT_WORK_TREE, so filesystem operations can target repository A while ref, object, configuration, and remote operations target repository B. An inherited environment from a shell, IDE, hook, or automation process can therefore make sync publish A task data into B, absorb B task data into A, or report misleading health. Required invariant: once tl selects repository A, no ambient Git routing or configuration-injection state may redirect any Git subprocess to another repository, worktree, object database, index, namespace, or remote configuration. Implementation: route every shelled Git command, including timeout-configuration reads, through one environment-scrubbing baseline. Remove GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_COMMON_DIR, GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY, GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES, GIT_INDEX_FILE, and GIT_NAMESPACE; audit and pin the treatment of GIT_CONFIG_COUNT, GIT_CONFIG_KEY_*, GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_*, GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS, GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM, and GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL rather than broadly promising to retain configuration variables. Preserve only credential, transport, and intentional discovery variables that cannot violate the invariant, including a deliberate policy for GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES. Refuse init in a bare repository with a teaching usage error, retain bare repositories as remotes, stop filesystem discovery at a bare-gitdir boundary, and add a doctor split-brain check comparing filesystem discovery with Git classification. Tests must cover every Git spawn path, each routing/config-injection class, shell/IDE-style inherited environments, explicit --dir/TL_DIR behavior, linked worktrees, bare local refusal versus bare remote support, discovery boundaries, doctor reporting, and every new error path. ADR-0012 owns the normative discovery and sanitized-environment policy; ADR-0014 records the cross-repository disclosure/corruption threat and mitigation; ADR-0016 receives only a cross-reference for its common-git worktree assumption.

This task pins the design in an ADR (new ADR, or fold into ADR-0002/ADR-0008 in present tense) BEFORE implementation — the implementation is its own follow-on task blocked on this one. Design points the ADR must resolve:

History to carry into the ADR (recovered from vision.md + git, since no ADR ever recorded it): the field split was intentional from the start — vision.md's field table defines description as "task *input*" and notes as "task *output* / human notes", both "(whole-field, not threaded)"; threaded comments were consciously excluded (imported comments are routed to the opaque meta map, vision.md field table / ADR-0005). --notes arrived only as one of minimal update's generic scalar flags (Stage 1; update is the scalar verb, ADR-0003/ADR-0008 wire table); --append-notes was added later as loop ergonomics because "the documented primary agent use is incremental progress notes, but --notes replaces wholesale" (commit ff81a25), with the LWW race known and accepted for serial loops. The ADR should state the description=input/document vs notes=output/journal roles explicitly; that distinction currently lives only in the vision.md field table.

Decision (RATIFIED 2026-07-14, third and final same-day revision — supersedes both the keep-LWW ratification and the observed-reset design): notes become an append-only journal of immutable entries; description remains the single mutable LWW document (the issue's current specification/context). There is NO replace or reset on notes — corrections are new notes; cleanup is per-entry retraction. The constraint that motivated the observed-reset hybrid (preserving update --notes replacement vocabulary) is void: tl is pre-public, and the first release ships the sound design. Both scalar interfaces are retired: update --notes and update --append-notes are removed, with usage errors directing to tl note add.

Surface:
- tl note add <id> <text> — creates an immutable entry with a stable note id (exact positional/--message shape to pin here).
- tl note list <id> — entries in deterministic order; --all additionally shows retracted placeholders (provenance visible, text hidden by default).
- tl note retract <id> <note-id> — adds the note id to a grow-only retraction set. Visible = entry exists AND its id is not retracted.

Contract to pin (each clause maps to a theorem or an explicit non-guarantee):
- Concurrent note adds are all retained. Entries are immutable in v1 — no note edit (record the exclusion; corrections are new notes).
- Duplicate delivery of the same op yields one entry; equal text from separate ops yields separate entries (identity = note id, minted from the op stamp).
- Ordering is deterministic by the complete stamp with an unconditional fallback tie-break — mirror the canonical-parent ratification: no traversal-order dependence, no distinct-stamps hypothesis.
- Retraction is remove-wins: a retraction that arrives before its entry hides the entry when it arrives (the visible predicate is a pure function of both sets; dangling retraction ids are total-safe). Retracted ids are never reused; a retracted note never becomes visible again (monotone).
- Retraction is element-scoped BY CONSTRUCTION (keyed by note id) — it cannot affect another note; no observed-set minting exists anywhere in the design.
- Actor and time on an entry are provenance, not authenticated facts; any repository writer may retract (actor is not authorization) — the ADR-0013/0014 trust posture.
- Frame-safety: notes drive nothing — readiness, rollup, cycle detection, and graph behavior never read them (like labels, ADR-0002); state it in the ADR and overview.
- Honesty disclosure (CLI output + ADR): retraction removes an entry from materialized views only; the log is append-only and replicated, so historical bytes and already-synced clones may still contain the text. No secure-deletion claim — true erasure would require destructive history rewriting and cannot reach synced replicas.

CRDT shape: entries = grow-only map noteId -> (stamp, actor, text); retracted = grow-only noteId set; both merge by union — a 2P-set over never-reused ids. Record WHY remove-wins is correct here (entries are immutable and unique; re-add does not exist) while the edge/label OR-Set is add-wins (elements are re-addable) — the two coexist deliberately.

Theorem set the implementation must prove: union convergence (comm/assoc/idem, both legs); delivery-order and duplication independence; concurrent adds all retained; retract-exactness (only the named id is affected); no-resurrection; rendering/ordering deterministic under permutation, duplication, and replica merge.

Decision points to close in the ADR: note-id form and display (op stamp's canonical string vs a short Crockford hash like issue ids; unambiguous-prefix reference rules); fate of create --notes and the importer's "notes" field (retire vs lower to one synthetic noteAdd — align ADR-0005); show's journal rendering (inline last-N + pointer to note list, or full); JSON schema of entries (id, time, actor, text; human/json parity).

Migration rule to pin: an issue's winning legacy scalar notes value projects to ONE synthetic immutable entry, stamped with the winning write's stamp (provenance preserved); historically overwritten values do NOT each become entries. The log-format change ships under ADR-0008 versioning; this repository's own tracker log is migrated once (separate task, blocked on the implementation).

History to carry into the ADR (recovered from vision.md + git; no ADR ever recorded it): the field split was intentional from the start — vision.md's field table defines description as "task *input*" and notes as "task *output* / human notes", both "(whole-field, not threaded)"; threaded comments were consciously excluded (imported comments go to the opaque meta map, ADR-0005). --notes arrived only as one of minimal update's generic scalar flags (Stage 1; update is the scalar verb, ADR-0003/0008); --append-notes was later loop ergonomics ("the documented primary agent use is incremental progress notes, but --notes replaces wholesale" — commit ff81a25), its LWW race known and accepted for serial loops. The journal completes the original task-output intent and keeps the not-threaded exclusion: entries are an evidence/decision journal, not a conversation — no replies, edits, or notifications. That is also why the name stays notes, not comments.

Rejected alternatives to record: keep-LWW-and-document (silently loses concurrent appends in exactly tl's multi-agent scenario); observed-reset append log (convergent and provable, but its replace verb surfaces observed-tombstone semantics to users and its base register keeps notes half-document — description already fills that role); HLC-cutoff schemes (total stamp order is not causality; a concurrent append could vanish for sorting below a replacement); "comments" naming (implies a conversation surface — threads, replies, editing, notifications — that tl deliberately excludes).
