`lake exe tlverify` spends most of its run re-submitting constants to the kernel that it has already checked in another scope. Each of the six scopes replays its dependency cone into a fresh `mkEmptyEnvironment` (Verify/Environment.lean:499), so every shared constant is checked once per scope.

Measured by replicating Verify/Main.lean's exact scope selection (including the `without` subtraction at Main.lean:50 that reduces the test scope to test-only modules):

  scope            selected   cone     replayable
  production           4227   15,048       14,996
  tests                 507   14,922       14,914
  verifier              782   10,277       10,269
  supervisor             41    5,017        5,017
  test-supervisor        41    5,017        5,017
  tooling                29    5,196        5,196

55,477 cone memberships over 19,108 distinct names, a factor of 2.90. The production cone is not a subset of the test cone; the test scope excludes production modules by construction and its cone is smaller.

Runtime: the compiled gate warm measures 66.1s user / 10.4s sys, with 89.5s and 136.3s real across two runs and 3.17-3.64 GB maximum resident set size. Wall clock swings with machine load, so user time is the measure to track. An interpreted `lake env lean --run` probe overstates CPU cost and should not be used for absolute timings.

Do not implement the naive form
-------------------------------
A union keyed on `Name`, or a cumulative environment threaded across scopes, is unsound here, and a probe measuring the union looked green while silently checking less. Six roots deliberately define the same top-level constant `main` (Main.lean, Tests/Main.lean, Verify/Main.lean, Verify/Launcher.lean, Verify/TestLauncher.lean, scripts/GenLicenses.lean). Measured: exactly 5 cross-scope name collisions with differing stored content, all on `main`, of which 4 are safe and total and therefore kernel-checked today (production, supervisor, test-supervisor, tooling; the tests and verifier `main` are unsafe and already skipped by `Lean.Environment.replay`). A `HashMap Name ConstantInfo` union keeps one and drops three. Threading a cumulative environment fails the same way from the other side: the second `main` is either filtered out as already-present and never checked, or reaches `addDecl` and is rejected as a duplicate.

The scopes therefore do not load the same content under the same names. They share dependencies and differ at exactly the executable roots the six-scope split exists to separate.

Sound design: shared base plus per-scope delta
----------------------------------------------
1. Compute each scope's cone independently, as today.
2. Determine the conflict set: names present in two or more cones whose stored constants differ. Compare structurally (name, levelParams, type, value?, isUnsafe, isPartial). Do not key a trust decision on a non-cryptographic hash.
3. Base = union of the cones minus the conflict set, and verify the base is dependency-closed rather than assuming it. Today it is: `main` has zero dependents in every cone (measured), so removing it closes.
4. Replay the base once from an empty environment. `Environment` is persistent, so fork the returned environment and replay each scope's delta (its own constants absent from the base) from that fork. Never thread one cumulative environment through the scopes in sequence.

Projected submissions: about 19,111 versus 55,477 today, so the soundness fix costs almost none of the win.

Proof obligation
----------------
A planner that silently drops a declaration produces a false-green trust gate, which is the same argument that already put `propagatedAxioms` in the proved tier. Two properties belong in Verify/Proofs.lean, not in sampled tests:
- coverage: every safe, total constant of every scope occurs in the base or in that scope's delta;
- separation: no name whose stored content differs across scopes occurs in the base.
Cone collection and the replay itself stay outside the TCB and comprehensively tested.

A third property is worth proving in the same change, because deduplication weakens a check that is currently free: replaying a union can mask a cone that is accidentally short, since a dependency omitted from scope A may be supplied by scope B, where today's per-scope empty replay would fail. Proving `replayClosure` closed under `replayDependencies` removes the concern at its source.

Also in scope
-------------
- Per-scope attribution of a replay failure. `Observation.evidence.replayError?` is per scope today; Lean's error names the declaration ("while replaying declaration 'X'"), so map it back or change the reporting deliberately.
- Wording that currently states the stronger property: the "complete stored dependency cone ... from an empty environment" claims in CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md and ADR-0026, docs/codebase-map.md, and the docstrings on `replayConstantsError?` / `replayedConstantCount`.
- Surface the count. `replayedConstantCount` is computed per scope (Verify/Environment.lean:514) and never printed; the success line reports inspected declarations and says "safe total dependency cones independently replay-validated" with no number.
- Regression guard as an op-count assertion (submissions equal base plus deltas, and equal the distinct-plus-conflicts count), not a wall-clock ceiling. A 30ms wall-clock floor masking a 16x quadratic is what the perf prevention net epic was created to fix.

Alternative, lower risk, not exclusive
--------------------------------------
Run the six existing independent replays with bounded concurrency. This preserves empty-environment validation, collision behaviour, and per-scope diagnostics, and needs no planner or proof. It does not reduce total work: it is bounded by the largest scope and by available cores, and CI runs on GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest and macos-latest (4 and 3 cores). Peak RSS measured 3.17-3.64 GB for one sequential run; the arm64 macOS runner has 7 GB, so benchmark memory before raising concurrency past two. Reasonable as a first step, with the planner as the larger and slower win.

Measurement note
----------------
Earlier per-phase numbers in this task's history charged pure work to the wrong phase: a `let`-bound pure result can be floated past the timestamp that was meant to bracket it, which made closure and axiom propagation look free. Forced, they are not: closure 7.7s and propagation 5.3s across the six scopes under the interpreter. Force every pure phase before stamping the clock.
title: tlverify: replay each constant once across the six scopes (shared base + per-scope delta)

description:
`lake exe tlverify` currently replays each of its six stored dependency cones
from a fresh `mkEmptyEnvironment` (`Verify/Environment.lean`). Shared
declarations are therefore submitted to Lean's kernel once per scope in which
they occur.

Current measurements
--------------------
The counts below reproduce `Verify/Main.lean`'s exact scope selection,
including the `without` subtraction that restricts the test scope to test-only
modules:

  scope              selected   cone     replayable
  production             4227   15,048       14,996
  tests                    507   14,922       14,914
  verifier                 782   10,277       10,269
  supervisor                41    5,017        5,017
  test-supervisor           41    5,017        5,017
  tooling                    29    5,196        5,196

That is 55,477 cone memberships over 19,108 distinct names, a 2.90x name
redundancy factor. A warm compiled run measured 66.1s user / 10.4s sys and
89.5s real, with 3.17 GB maximum resident set size. User time and kernel
submission counts are the useful regression measures; wall clock varies with
machine load. Interpreted `lake env lean --run` probes overstate absolute CPU
cost and must not be used as compiled-gate timings.

The optimization is worthwhile but not currently urgent. Implement it only as
a trust-preserving replay planner, not as a name-keyed union.

Why a naive union is unsound
----------------------------
The six loaded environments do not necessarily contain the same declaration
under a shared name. Their executable roots all define `main`. Today there are
five additional cross-scope instances of that name with differing stored
content; four of the six `main` declarations are safe and total and are
kernel-checked by the current gate. A `HashMap Name ConstantInfo` union would
silently retain one instance and drop the others. Threading one cumulative
environment through the scopes is equally wrong: later declarations are either
filtered as already present or rejected as duplicates.

Required design: shared base plus per-scope deltas
-------------------------------------------------
1. Compute each scope's roots and dependency cone independently, using exactly
   the selection in `Verify/Main.lean`.
2. Before combining scopes, fail closed unless every selected root is present
   in its cone and the cone contains every dependency named by
   `replayDependencies`. A cone that is accidentally short must never be
   repaired by a declaration supplied by another scope.
3. Define exact structural equivalence for `ConstantInfo`. It must cover every
   constructor and every field relevant to stored declaration identity and
   replay, including declaration kind, reducibility and mutual-block metadata,
   and inductive/constructor/recursor metadata. The common projection
   `(name, levelParams, type, value?, isUnsafe, isPartial)` is insufficient.
   Do not use a non-cryptographic hash as a trust decision.
4. A declaration may enter the shared base only when all occurrences with that
   name have equivalent stored content and its required replay context is also
   in the base. Remove conflicts and their reverse dependency closure from the
   base, placing the exact scope-specific instances in the corresponding
   deltas. The base must be dependency-closed. If the planner cannot establish
   these conditions, fall back to the existing independent per-scope replay;
   an optimization precondition must not reject an otherwise valid gate.
5. Replay the base once from an empty environment. Fork the returned persistent
   environment and replay each scope's delta from that fork. Never thread a
   cumulative environment through the scopes.

With the current cones, all differing declarations are named `main` and have
no dependents, so almost all redundancy can be removed. The earlier estimate
of about 19,111 kernel submissions means safe, total declarations after
partitioning; it is not the number of distinct names and must be re-measured by
the final implementation.

Required proved properties
--------------------------
The pure planner and its fail-closed closure predicate are part of the trust
decision and belong in `Verify/Proofs.lean`:

- Exact coverage: every safe, total `(Name, ConstantInfo)` instance in every
  scope is replayed either in the base under a compatible dependency context or
  in that scope's delta.
- Separation: the base contains no name with inequivalent stored content across
  scopes.
- Base closure: every replay dependency of a base declaration is also in the
  base.
- Scope closure acceptance: accepting a collected cone implies that all
  selected roots and all replay dependencies are present in that cone.

Coverage by name alone is insufficient. The theorem must preserve the exact
scope-specific stored content. The filesystem/environment collection and Lean's
actual replay remain comprehensively tested; only the pure predicates and
planner decisions above move into the proved tier. If `replayClosure` itself is
refactored into a total provable function, update the documented proved/tested
boundary accordingly.

Diagnostics, counts, and regression coverage
---------------------------------------------
- A base replay failure must name the declaration and attribute it to every
  scope containing that exact stored declaration. Delta failures remain
  scope-specific. Preserve the existing fail-closed `replayError?` evidence or
  deliberately replace it with an equally explicit structure.
- Surface both logical scope coverage and physical kernel submissions. Define
  physical submissions exactly as `replayedConstantCount base` plus the sum of
  `replayedConstantCount` over the deltas.
- Add an exact op-count assertion derived from the completed plan. It must
  account for unsafe/partial filtering and for declarations that must be
  replayed in more than one scope-specific dependency context. Do not equate it
  vaguely with "distinct names" and do not use a wall-clock ceiling as the
  primary regression guard.
- Test every planner branch and error path: identical declarations, differing
  declarations with the same name, transitive dependents of a conflict,
  missing roots, non-closed cones, fallback to independent replay, base replay
  failure attribution, and per-scope delta failure attribution.
- Forced stage timings are useful observability. Force each pure result before
  taking the timestamp; lazy pure work can otherwise be charged to the wrong
  phase.

Documentation in scope
----------------------
Update the claims that currently say each complete dependency cone is replayed
independently from an empty environment: `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, ADR-0026,
`docs/codebase-map.md`, and the docstrings for `replayConstantsError?` and
`replayedConstantCount`. Pin any new verifier-internal theorems in
`pinnedVerdictLogicTheorems`; do not add product landmarks or an overview
proved-claims row for gate internals.

Lower-risk alternative
----------------------
Bounded concurrency over the six existing independent replays preserves their
current trust argument and diagnostics, but it does not reduce CPU work and may
multiply peak memory. One sequential run already measured 3.17-3.64 GB RSS,
while the GitHub-hosted arm64 macOS runner has 7 GB. Benchmark before allowing
more than two concurrent replays. Parallel environment loading can still
compose with base-plus-delta replay; after deduplication there is simply little
replay work left for concurrency to accelerate.
title: tlverify: replay identical stored constants once via shared base and per-scope deltas

description:
Three review rounds produced 63 + 8 + 15 findings and the recurring defect is one shape: POSIX shell discarding a non-zero status so a check that cannot run reports success. Fixed twice and reintroduced four times while fixing other things, which makes it a language problem rather than an author problem. Move the DECISION layer into a separately built tlrelease executable following the tlverify precedent.
HARD CONSTRAINTS. Release/ imports nothing from Tl/ — that keeps release administration out of the shipped product AND keeps the toolchain-free CI gate fast, since the gate must not wait on the product build. Batteries only, no Mathlib. tlrelease is NOT part of the product TCB.
PROOF BOUNDARY. Most of tlrelease is tested I/O-shell code that happens to be written in Lean; being in Lean does not make it verified. Theorems go only to small pure verdict functions whose failure mode is a silent false negative, exactly as Verify/Proofs.lean does for the trust gate. Three are intended, named in their tasks; everything else is tested. The first version makes no new proved claim in docs/overview.md and adds no landmark theorem.
NATIVE BOUNDARIES, unmoved: install.sh (piped from curl), Formula/tl.rb (Homebrew requires Ruby), verify-release-artifacts.sh (a precompiled verifier must not become the only way to authenticate the release containing it). npm still performs npm operations; Lean plans and classifies them.
SCOPE SPLIT. Required before v0.1.0: model, manifest+metadata, prerequisites, SBOM, the identity pin, the rehearsal. NOT release-blocking: npm planning and Homebrew rendering — porting deferred channels adds risk without enabling the first release. The policy runner is a measurement, not a commitment.
Sibling of tl-afsa rather than its child: tl's rollup would otherwise hold the hardening epic open until deferred channel ports finish. Supersession is recorded per task.

title: Measure whether the policy runner should move to Lean at all

description:
NOT a commitment to port. check-release-policy.sh aggregates gates with an explicit `gate <name> <cmd>` loop that observes each status directly; it is not where the status-loss defects were, so porting it buys little and costs something real. The release-policy CI job is deliberately toolchain-free so a lint failure surfaces in seconds rather than after the build matrix (ADR-0026), and a Lean runner makes it wait on a build.
DECISION CRITERION, to be measured and recorded in ADR-0026: time `lake build tlrelease` from a cold cache and from a warm one on the CI image. Port only if the warm build is under about a minute AND the port removes a class of defect the shell runner can still exhibit. Otherwise keep the shell runner, which then becomes the last remaining non-trivial shell in the release path and should be documented as a deliberate exception rather than an oversight.
PROOF BOUNDARY: none. This is orchestration.
DELETES: nothing unless the measurement says otherwise.

title: Inert two-line identity pin, so the shell verifier needs no parser

description:
verify-release-artifacts.sh needs python3 solely to read the certificate pin out of identity.json without mangling its regex escapes, and it must stay shell.
NOT a generated identity.sh that gets sourced: generating shell code and executing it adds a code-generation and quoting surface for no gain, and would itself need adversarial quoting tests. NOT constants embedded in the verifier either — its selftest substitutes a malformed identity.json to prove the anchor and empty-pin refusals still fire, and embedding would make those cases unreachable.
Instead: release/identity.pin, two inert lines — issuer, then expression — read with `IFS= read -r`. No parser, no generated code, no quoting hazard, and the selftest can still substitute the file. Generated by tlrelease from identity.json and drift-guarded by Tests/ReleaseTests.lean, which already guards the copies in VERIFYING.md, the ADRs, install.sh and Formula/tl.rb.
PROOF BOUNDARY: none.
DELETES: the python3 dependency from verify-release-artifacts.sh — the last user-facing path that has one.

Release/Model.lean and Release/Json.lean. Make the problematic states unrepresentable rather than validated after the fact: a malformed digest cannot inhabit Sha256, a published target carries its build metadata by construction rather than an Option that a check can forget to consult, and an audit outcome is an inductive — verified | missing remedy | unchecked assumption | operationalError detail — so an API outage cannot become an empty string that reads as absence, which is how two confirmed findings arose.
Batteries only, no Mathlib, no imports from Tl/.
PROOF BOUNDARY: none yet — these are definitions. The theorems land in the tasks that consume them.
DELETES: nothing directly; it is what makes the deletions below possible.

Release/Manifest.lean + Release/Metadata.lean.
ABSORBS (round 3): rc_targets failure swallowed by an assignment prefix, which empties the target list and skips every build-metadata check while exiting 0; and runId compared only leg-to-leg, never against the ambient GITHUB_RUN_ID, so a self-consistent artifact set from another run passes.
PROOF BOUNDARY: two theorems, both verdict logic with silent-false-negative risk, in the Verify/Proofs.lean spirit. (1) the --verify predicate accepts a directory iff every described asset is present with a matching digest AND no undescribed asset is present — an iff, since a one-way bound is satisfied by a verifier that accepts nothing. (2) the build-metadata predicate accepts a published target iff a complete record exists agreeing on digest, commit, target, tier, toolchain, manifest digest and run. Everything else here — reading files, walking directories — is tested.
DELETES on completion: scripts/gen-release-manifest.sh entirely. The workflow calls tlrelease directly; no wrapper.
Keeps the shell implementation as a differential oracle until the golden-output comparison is green in CI, then removes both it and the comparison.

Release/Prerequisites.lean. Lean classifies; gh is still invoked through IO.Process with explicit exit classification.
ABSORBS (round 3): a gh failure collapsing into an empty policy and being reported as MISSING, aborting a legitimate release inside the sign job with a remedy telling the operator to fix something already correct; and the tag-ruleset check accepting any refs/tags/v prefix. That second row has been a proxy for the property in ALL THREE rounds — first a count of rulesets, then a prefix match — so the typed version must express 'the include set covers every v* tag', not 'an include looks v-ish'.
PROOF BOUNDARY: one theorem. The run-wide verdict is `missing` iff at least one row is missing, and an `unchecked` row never masks a `missing` one nor counts toward a pass — the aggregation is where a silent false negative would hide, and it is a pure fold over the row list.
DELETES on completion: scripts/check-release-prereqs.sh entirely.

Release/Sbom.lean + Release/Homebrew.lean. NOT release-blocking for v0.1.0 in the Homebrew half; the SBOM half is, because ADR-0006 requires it in every binary release.
The formula stays Ruby and keeps being validated by brew load/style/audit in CI; only the rendering moves. The fallback-digest hole and the prerelease version line are already fixed in shell (818f192), so this is consolidation rather than repair.
PROOF BOUNDARY: none. Rendering and document assembly are tested — byte-identical output for identical inputs is a test, not a theorem.
DELETES on completion: scripts/gen-sbom.sh entirely; scripts/gen-homebrew-formula.sh entirely.

Release/Npm.lean. NOT release-blocking for v0.1.0 — npm is deferred to v0.2.0, so this is follow-up and must not gate the first release.
ABSORBS (round 3): content comparison that ignores symlinks and file modes (compare type, mode and symlink target, not regular-file digests alone); nothing establishing that dist-tags.latest is not the 0.0.0 bootstrap placeholder — that check belongs in the prerequisite audit; and a vacuous [^\n] bracket class that makes the never-publish-to-latest guard unfireable.
PROOF BOUNDARY: none intended. The publish decision — absent | matches | conflict — is a candidate if it grows, but a three-way match on registry state is not where a silent false negative hides; the risk is in the comparison inputs, which are I/O.
DELETES on completion: the planning half of scripts/npm-publish.sh and all of scripts/npm-bootstrap.sh. npm-publish.sh survives only if it is reduced to invoking npm.

title: Decide and document the v0.1.0 channel scope, before the port starts

description:
The epic said v0.1.0 is GitHub Release + installer and then listed npm and Homebrew port tasks with nothing marking them non-blocking — a contradiction that would have pulled deferred channels into the critical path.
REQUIRED for v0.1.0: signed GitHub Release with SHA256SUMS, per-asset bundles, the compliance assets, the manifest, and install.sh.
DEFERRED to v0.2.0: npm and Homebrew. npm needs a manual bootstrap that has not happened; Homebrew needs a tap that does not exist; neither works while the repository is private.
Record the deferral in ADR-0006 rather than leaving it promising channels the release does not deliver, and say in VERIFYING.md what a v0.1.0 user can and cannot install. Do this BEFORE the port, so the port knows what is on the critical path.

Release/Sbom.lean. REQUIRED for v0.1.0 because ADR-0006 requires an SBOM in every binary release. This task deliberately contains no Homebrew work: it blocks the rehearsal, while Homebrew is a separate deferred channel task and must not do so.

Lean reads lake-manifest.json and the typed release model, renders deterministic SPDX JSON, and refuses malformed or incomplete dependency evidence. The GitHub release workflow invokes tlrelease directly. No Python, Ruby, Node, npm, brew, or channel-specific runtime is permitted on this path.

PROOF BOUNDARY: none. Rendering and document assembly are tested, including malformed JSON, unreadable inputs, missing fields, deterministic output, and disagreement with the compiled dependency inventory.

DELETES on completion: scripts/gen-sbom.sh entirely and every inline Python snippet used to construct or validate the v0.1 SBOM.
title: Port SBOM generation for the v0.1 GitHub release

description:
Release/Npm.lean. DEFERRED CHANNEL WORK for v0.2.0: npm is not release-blocking for v0.1.0 and must not gate its policy, dependency-boundary check, or rehearsal.

At this channel boundary, npm operations necessarily use node/npm. Lean owns bootstrap planning, registry-state classification, package-content comparison, dist-tag policy and resumability decisions. No Python or Ruby is permitted. npm-publish.sh survives only if reduced to a thin invocation wrapper around npm with no parsing or policy logic.

ABSORBS (round 3): content comparison that ignores symlinks and file modes (compare type, mode and symlink target, not regular-file digests alone); nothing establishing that dist-tags.latest is not the 0.0.0 bootstrap placeholder; and a vacuous [^\n] bracket class that makes the never-publish-to-latest guard unfireable.

PROOF BOUNDARY: none intended. The publish decision — absent | matches | conflict — is a candidate if it grows, but the principal risk is in the I/O comparison inputs, which receive complete branch and error-path tests.

The five-package manual bootstrap and trusted-publisher configuration happen only when npm becomes an enabled channel. Until then, node and npm are not reachable from the v0.1 release.

DELETES on completion: the planning half of scripts/npm-publish.sh and all of scripts/npm-bootstrap.sh, including every Python invocation in the npm channel.

Three review rounds produced 63 + 8 + 15 findings and the recurring defect is one shape: POSIX shell discarding a non-zero status so a check that cannot run reports success. Fixed twice and reintroduced four times while fixing other things, which makes it a language problem rather than an author problem. Move the DECISION layer into a separately built tlrelease executable following the tlverify precedent.

HARD CONSTRAINTS. Release/ imports nothing from Tl/: release administration stays out of the shipped product and Batteries only keeps it independent of Mathlib. tlrelease is NOT part of the product TCB. The release-policy runner is measured rather than automatically ported.

V0.1 DEPENDENCY BOUNDARY. No path reachable from the GitHub-only release workflow, install.sh, verify-release-artifacts.sh, or strict v0.1 policy may invoke Python, Ruby, Homebrew, Node, or npm. Lean owns JSON and decision logic; POSIX shell is thin orchestration. This is enforced by a release-blocking inventory plus hostile PATH shims, not left as documentation.

CHANNEL-NATIVE EXCEPTIONS, deferred. Homebrew formulas are necessarily Ruby and are tested by real brew using Homebrew-managed Ruby; formula rendering remains Lean. npm operations necessarily use node/npm; planning and classification remain Lean. Neither channel is reachable in v0.1, and neither introduces Python.

PROOF BOUNDARY. Most of tlrelease is tested I/O-shell code that happens to be written in Lean; being in Lean does not make it verified. Theorems go only to small pure verdict functions whose failure mode is a silent false negative, in the Verify/Proofs.lean style. The first version makes no new proved claim in docs/overview.md and adds no landmark theorem.

NATIVE BOUNDARIES, unmoved: install.sh (piped from curl), Formula/tl.rb (Homebrew requires Ruby), verify-release-artifacts.sh (a precompiled verifier must not become the only way to authenticate the release containing it), and thin npm invocation when that channel is enabled.

SCOPE SPLIT. Required before v0.1.0: channel decision, verifier scope, model, manifest+metadata, channel-aware prerequisites, SBOM, identity pin, dependency-boundary gate, and workflow rehearsal. NOT release-blocking: npm planning, Homebrew rendering, and the policy-runner experiment. SBOM and Homebrew are separate tasks so their different criticality is represented by the graph rather than prose.

Sibling of tl-afsa rather than its child because tl rollup is done iff all children are closed. Supersession and remaining known defects are recorded per task.

Resolve the channel-scope contradiction before any port code lands.

REQUIRED for v0.1.0: a signed GitHub Release with SHA256SUMS, per-asset bundles, compliance assets, the manifest, SBOM, build metadata, install.sh, and the standalone artifact verifier. DEFERRED to v0.2.0: npm and Homebrew. npm needs a five-package manual bootstrap and trusted publishing; Homebrew needs a tap and credential; neither channel gates the first release.

DEPENDENCY BUDGET for v0.1.0: no reachable GitHub-release, installer, verifier, or strict-policy path invokes python, python3, ruby, brew, node, or npm. Record this in ADR-0006 and ADR-0026, and distinguish project dependencies from channel-native runtimes: Homebrew owns Ruby when enabled; npm owns node/npm when enabled. VERIFYING.md states exactly which v0.1 installation and verification paths exist.

The release plan must be machine-readable enough that prerequisites and workflow jobs are derived from enabled channels. Disabled npm and Homebrew checks are absent, not reported as missing or unchecked. The strict v0.1 policy omits their generation and audit gates.

Correct docs/design-backlog.md at the same time: the manifest and prerequisite defects are active blockers for a GitHub-only release; only the three npm defects are inert until npm is enabled. Do this before the port so every later task knows the critical path and dependency boundary.

verify-release-artifacts.sh currently needs python3 solely to read the certificate pin from identity.json without mangling regex escapes, but v0.1 user-facing paths may not require Python.

Use release/identity.pin: exactly two inert lines, issuer then identity expression, read from one opened descriptor with IFS= read -r. It is data, never sourced or evaluated. Reject a missing line, empty value, extra third line, carriage return, malformed/unanchored expression, unreadable file, and trailing data. Preserve the selftest ability to substitute malformed pins and prove every refusal fires.

The pin is generated by tlrelease from identity.json only after the Release/ verifier scope exists, and a Lean test drift-guards every embedded copy in VERIFYING.md, the ADRs, install.sh, and Formula/tl.rb. The v0.1 verifier and installer selftests run with failing python, python3, ruby, brew, node and npm shims.

PROOF BOUNDARY: none.

DELETES: the Python dependency from verify-release-artifacts.sh, the last user-facing path carrying it. No generated shell file, source, eval, Ruby, or second JSON parser is introduced.

Release/Prerequisites.lean. Lean classifies; gh remains the GitHub API boundary through IO.Process with explicit exit and timeout classification. No Python, Ruby, Node, npm, or brew is invoked for the v0.1 audit.

Prerequisites are derived from the typed enabled-channel plan. For GitHub-only v0.1, repository visibility, release environment, reviewers, deployment-tag policy, tag ruleset and signing identity are applicable. npm packages, npm trusted publishing, the tap and its token produce no rows at all; a disabled channel is neither missing nor unchecked.

ABSORBS (round 3): a gh failure collapsing into an empty policy and being reported as MISSING; and the tag-ruleset check accepting any refs/tags/v prefix. The typed predicate must express that the include set covers every v* tag, not that one pattern looks v-ish.

PROOF BOUNDARY: characterize the pure aggregation and release decision. Missing is reported iff an applicable row is missing. Operational errors remain distinct from missing and never permit release. Explicitly carried unchecked assumptions follow their declared policy but never count as verified. The release may proceed iff every applicable blocking row is verified or is an explicitly permitted carried assumption. State the precedence/reporting behavior rather than leaving mixed missing-plus-operational-error cases implicit.

Test all I/O collection branches: missing gh, non-zero exit, timeout, malformed JSON, unreadable response file, 404 versus other API errors, pagination, narrowed tag patterns, disabled channels, and every outcome mixture.

DELETES on completion: scripts/check-release-prereqs.sh entirely and its Python JSON parsing.

Release/Manifest.lean + Release/Metadata.lean. This is v0.1-critical and replaces every Python and shell decision on the manifest/build-metadata path, including inline release-workflow JSON construction.

ABSORBS (round 3): target-list failure swallowed by an assignment prefix, yielding an empty target list and skipped checks; and runId compared only leg-to-leg rather than against ambient GITHUB_RUN_ID.

PROOF BOUNDARY: two pure verdict theorems. (1) Given an explicit collected-evidence value, manifest verification accepts iff every described asset is present with the matching digest and no undescribed asset is present. Do not phrase this as proving a directory property: walking, file typing, reading and hashing are I/O and receive comprehensive tests. (2) Build-metadata verification accepts a published target iff a complete record agrees on digest, commit, target, tier, toolchain, manifest digest and ambient run. Both are iff statements so a verifier that accepts nothing cannot satisfy them.

Test collection and parsing separately: missing command, non-zero exit, malformed JSON, timeout, unreadable file, absent or duplicate asset, symlink/non-regular entry, digest-tool absence, stale run, empty target inventory, and extra asset.

DELETES on completion: scripts/gen-release-manifest.sh entirely and all inline Python used by the v0.1 workflow to create or validate release metadata. The workflow calls tlrelease directly with no wrapper. Keep the shell implementation only as a differential oracle until golden comparison is green, then remove both it and the comparison.

Release-blocking, and its own task because none of the four build legs has ever executed.

MUST OBSERVE: all four legs run; Supported versus Best-effort behavior on a deliberately failed leg; glibc-floor assertion; link audit and build metadata per leg; manifest assembly and verification over artifacts that crossed the artifact store rather than a local fixture; and no signing or publication capability. A workflow_dispatch rehearsal must be incapable of publishing, not merely told not to.

DEPENDENCY BOUNDARY: run the GitHub-only path after the dedicated boundary gate. Install failing PATH-precedence shims for python, python3, ruby, brew, node and npm; prove each shim can fire, then demonstrate the entire rehearsal and every v0.1 selftest succeed without invoking them. No Homebrew or npm job may be present in the enabled plan, and absent tap/packages must not appear as failed or unchecked prerequisites.

FAULT INJECTION: missing command, non-zero exit, malformed JSON, timeout and unreadable file. Each produces a refusal naming the cause, not a pass or bare status. Include an operational GitHub API error distinct from a genuinely missing prerequisite.

The cross-job artifact handoff is the part local selftests cannot reach and where the build-to-sign evidence check lives. The dry sign-stage assembly verifies ambient run id and complete evidence but holds no id-token or publication credentials.

PROOF BOUNDARY: none. This is end-to-end I/O-tier evidence.

NOT a commitment to port. check-release-policy.sh is straightforward orchestration; porting it buys little unless measurement or a remaining defect class justifies the cost. Whether it stays shell or moves, the strict v0.1 runner may invoke tlrelease and ordinary POSIX tools but must not invoke Python, Ruby, Homebrew, Node or npm.

DECISION CRITERION, recorded in ADR-0026: measure complete wall-clock time of the actual release-policy CI job from a clean runner, including Lean toolchain provisioning and a cold tlrelease build, against the current toolchain-free shell baseline. CI does not cache .lake/build, so a warm-build-only threshold is not representative. Port only if the end-to-end cold feedback remains within the explicitly accepted budget and the port removes a defect class the shell runner can still exhibit. Otherwise keep the shell runner as a documented thin exception calling tlrelease subcommands.

The v0.1 policy is channel-aware: Homebrew and npm generation/audit gates are absent when those channels are disabled, rather than skipped as successful. Channel-specific CI may still validate deferred artifacts separately, but it does not gate the v0.1 release path or introduce its runtimes there.

PROOF BOUNDARY: none. This is orchestration.

DELETES: nothing unless measurement says otherwise. Regardless of that decision, remove Python/Ruby/Node channel logic from the v0.1 runner.

Release/Model.lean and Release/Json.lean, Batteries only with no imports from Tl/ and no Mathlib.

Make problematic states unrepresentable: malformed text cannot inhabit Sha256; a published target carries complete build metadata by construction rather than an Option; audit outcomes distinguish verified, missing remedy, explicitly carried unchecked assumption, and operationalError detail; and a typed ReleasePlan names enabled channels so disabled-channel jobs and prerequisites cannot leak into v0.1.

The v0.1 plan enables GitHub Release plus installer/verifier and disables Homebrew and npm. JSON parsing and validation are Lean-owned so v0.1 paths do not need Python, Ruby, Node, npm or brew.

PROOF BOUNDARY: none yet; these are definitions. Pure verdict theorems land with the consumers. Parsed external data enters through Except and only validated values reach decision functions.

DELETES: nothing directly; this model enables the manifest, prerequisite, SBOM, identity and dependency-boundary tasks to delete their parallel parsers and channel assumptions.

title: Full CI rehearsal — BLOCKED: requires the workflow to reach GitHub

description:
The branch stays local, so the CI matrix cannot run — but most of a build leg is not GitHub-specific. Eight of its fourteen steps are ordinary commands and can be executed directly on the development machine, which de-risks the largest untested surface without pushing anything and without adding any tooling.
RUNNABLE NATIVELY on the macOS host, covering the whole darwin-arm64 Supported leg: stamp the checkout with gen-build-provenance.sh --stamp; lake build tl; stage the artifact; ad-hoc codesign and verify; record the macOS minimum version; the full smoke test including the git task round-trip; the link audit via otool -L and nm; and the build-metadata record. Then feed the result to the manifest generator and to verify-release-artifacts.sh, so the local half of the artifact contract runs end to end against a real binary.
NOT RUNNABLE LOCALLY, and to be stated as untested rather than implied working: both Linux legs, which build inside the pinned glibc-floor container on the runner; actions/checkout; upload/download-artifact and therefore the cross-job handoff where the build-to-sign evidence check lives; the cache actions; OIDC; cosign signing; and gh release create.
Do not introduce local containerisation to close that gap. The container is a CI-side mechanism for meeting the ADR-0006 glibc floor and is not a dependency of this project for anyone — no contributor, user or script needs it. Rehearsing the Linux legs locally would mean adding a tool nobody otherwise requires, to test a path that CI will exercise the moment anything reaches it.
Prefer driving the workflow's real step bodies over reimplementing them: a rehearsal script that drifts from the workflow rehearses the script.

scripts/check-release-identity.sh is a strict-policy gate on a v0.1-reachable path and invokes python3, so the v0.1 dependency budget cannot hold while it stands.

DECISION. Keep the regular expression only at the Cosign boundary and keep release/identity.pin as the same parser-free two-line file. Do not implement a second regular-expression parser or matcher. Instead, make repository, releaseWorkflow and certificateOidcIssuer the authoritative structured inputs. Release/Identity.lean renders the one canonical, fully anchored Go-regexp identity expression from exact escaped literals plus the fixed tag grammar owned by Version.parseTag. certificateIdentityRegexp is removed from configuration or retained only as a generated mirror that must equal the canonical rendering.

WHY. A configurable regular expression admits an anchored but permissive policy. A custom matcher merely creates a second semantics whose agreement with Go RE2 remains an assumption. Canonical generation makes the permissive configuration state unrepresentable while preserving the existing installer, standalone-verifier, Homebrew and VERIFYING.md interface.

POLICY MODEL. Define the intended pure predicate structurally: an accepted identity has exactly the configured repository, exactly the configured workflow path, refs/tags/, and a tag accepted by Version.parseTag. Prove the silent-false-negative verdict as an iff over that structured value. Do not claim that Lean implements or verifies RE2.

TESTS. Pin the canonical rendered bytes with a golden fixture. Mutations must catch a changed repository or workflow, dropped or changed escapes, missing anchors, changed tag grammar, malformed configuration, and drift in release/identity.pin. Keep the existing adversarial accept/reject table against the structured predicate. Exercise unreadable files, malformed JSON and every command error path. The v0.1 release candidate is the integration check against actual Cosign. Record explicitly in docs/overview.md the residual assumption that Cosign interprets the fixed emitted Go-regexp fragment according to its documented syntax.

DELETES on completion: scripts/check-release-identity.sh, both inline Python identity checks in release.yml, and arbitrary regular-expression decision logic outside Release/Identity.lean. The workflow calls tlrelease directly.
title: Generate and enforce one canonical signing identity policy in Lean

description:

Use scripts/gen-sbom.sh as a differential oracle while porting and make any intentional output change explicit in tests and documentation.

FAIL CLOSED. Refuse malformed, unreadable or incomplete inputs rather than emitting an empty or partial SBOM. Tests cover the successful committed inputs, representative missing/wrong-type/malformed fields, empty or invalid package inventories, deterministic regeneration, changed-version output, inventory/revision agreement, output-write failure, and command usage errors. AGENTS.md supplies the general requirement that every touched I/O branch and exit status has a discrete test.

Reuse release/Json.lean, release/Model.lean and the existing tlrelease command framework. Do not add a JSON library, interpreter, scanner or channel-specific runtime, and do not turn this into a general SPDX framework. The existing license-classification gates remain authoritative; this task does not reimplement them. Do not change the signing-identity mechanism.

The normal repository gates in AGENTS.md pass, the tlrelease command produces and validates the committed-input SBOM directly, and the completion note records the deleted paths, intentional compatibility differences if any, verification performed and residual assumptions. Finish and verify the release workflow wiring after the manifest/metadata and signing-identity ports land. This is an integration task; it must not reimplement either decision layer.

OWNERSHIP. The manifest port owns build-metadata creation and deletes its inline Python. The signing-identity port owns both workflow identity checks and deletes their inline Python. This task is blocked by both and starts from their resulting interfaces.

Replace only residual orchestration with direct tlrelease invocations, or remove it when an upstream command already performs the check. Keep YAML and POSIX shell thin: pass explicit workflow context and paths into typed commands; do not parse or render JSON, evaluate identity policy, or calculate release decisions in YAML/shell.

INTEGRATION CHECKS. Confirm the build legs still emit complete metadata for the artifact they built, and the pre-build/pre-sign identity refusals still occur before privileged work. GOAL: full Homebrew support with no first-party shell generator or publication program.

This is the canonical task for the first authoritative downstream manifest consumer. In the same change, widen ManifestDescription to a complete typed parse of targets, embedded build records, npm, and Homebrew sections; malformed or absent sections must fail manifest verification before any channel consumes them.

title: Port the complete Homebrew channel to tlrelease

description:
GOAL: full npm support with no first-party shell staging, bootstrap, planning, comparison, or publication program.

After the full typed manifest reader lands, add tlrelease npm commands that stage all five packages around signed release assets, validate the staged host binary and release identity, construct package manifests and optionalDependencies from manifest targets, plan and perform the 0.0.0 bootstrap, classify registry state as absent, identical, or conflict, select latest versus next, and publish missing packages in resumable order with the launcher last.

Lean owns file-type, mode, and symlink comparison; registry JSON parsing; dist-tag policy; immutable-version conflict refusal; package selection; publication order; and all messages. It invokes pinned npm as the channel-native external tool. No Python is introduced.

Replace npm/tl/bin/tl with a small JavaScript launcher because Node is native to npm. Preserve argument, exit-status, and signal behavior and the explicit native-Windows refusal.

DELETE on completion: scripts/npm-bootstrap.sh, scripts/npm-pack.sh, scripts/npm-publish.sh, scripts/lib/channel-common.sh, and the shell npm launcher. Remove npm decision logic from policy scripts and workflow run blocks. Tests use public tlrelease commands with planted packages and stub npm clients, plus real npm pack/install smoke tests.
title: Port the complete npm channel to tlrelease

description:
ARCHITECTURAL END STATE: the only tracked shell programs are install.sh and scripts/verify-release-artifacts.sh, the two bootstrap boundaries that cannot rely on the release binary they install or authenticate. Formula/tl.rb remains Ruby by Homebrew definition. The npm launcher becomes JavaScript.

This issue is the parent for three bounded changes: port build stamping and task-ID lint; add a typed tlrelease policy runner and cut both workflows over after the npm and Homebrew commands exist; then delete the old policy, runtime-shim, shared-library, generator, channel, and lexical shell-enforcement infrastructure.

The policy runner owns profile membership, required external tools, strict missing-tool behavior, command execution, and reporting as typed data. Both ci.yml and release.yml invoke it identically after building tlrelease. Cold-runner timing is measured and optimized after this architecture is in place; timing does not decide whether thousands of lines of shell remain.

Tests for the two bootstrap scripts move to Lean-driven black-box fixtures where practical. No general shell lexer is part of the end state.
title: Eliminate non-bootstrap shell from the release pipeline

description:
The architecture is decided: repository policy and release orchestration move to tlrelease, leaving only the installer and standalone artifact verifier as shell bootstrap boundaries.

Measure the complete cold-runner cost after the typed policy runner and workflow cutover land: Lean provisioning, dependency restoration, lake build tlrelease, and the policy command itself. Compare it with the former shell baseline to identify feedback regressions, then improve job ordering, cache reuse, or parallelism without restoring a second shell policy implementation.

This task is performance evidence, not permission to keep shell. It deletes nothing and must not block the port. Record the accepted cold-runner budget and measurements in ADR-0026.
title: Measure and optimize cold tlrelease policy execution

description:
After the non-bootstrap shell cutover, run the complete first-party release policy and both bootstrap-script black-box suites in a pinned minimal container that does not contain python, python3, ruby, brew, node, or npm.

This hermetic run is the dependency-budget authority for the GitHub-only path: absolute names, PATH names, variables, strings, and subprocesses all fail because the forbidden runtime does not exist. Prove the container really lacks each runtime before trusting the clean run.

Instead, one dedicated unprivileged consumer instantiates the same canonical handoff prefix as every real consumer: download, canonical single-file set-hash comparison, /usr/bin/false mismatch guard, /bin/chmod, and the first tlrelease invocation. The structural guard requires all consumers to use that prefix and permits divergence only after first tool use. This rehearses hosted artifact transport and domination; the separate v0.1.0 task exercises signing and irreversible publication.

Observe all four build legs, Supported versus Best-effort behavior on a deliberately failed leg, glibc-floor and link audits, build metadata, authentication before typed manifest parsing, manifest assembly and verification, and the exact typed policy command both workflows use. Exercise Homebrew rendering with real brew, npm staging and real pack/install, the runtime-stripped launcher suite, safe-fixture idempotence decisions, and every distribution-surface effect possible without authority.

Mutation fixtures cover inherited permissions, secret-only jobs, authority-bearing outputs, expression and script-bearing action inputs, continue-on-error, status-function overrides, file-set producer and mapping drift, prefix truncation, insertion, reorder, bypass, and rehearsal drift. Fault injection covers missing command, non-zero, malformed JSON, timeout, unreadable file, corruption, API error, and absent prerequisite. Completion unblocks the separate v0.1.0 release task and does not create or push a tag.

The CI profile validates deferred channels; the release profile derives enabled effects from release/plan.json. npm and Homebrew commands run directly after their ports land. The atomic shell-deletion task removes the now-obsolete parity oracle and shell runner later.

Move complex workflow decisions into typed commands. The drift guard follows authority through effective workflow and job permissions, id-token, secrets, protected environments, and transitive needs outputs. Every authority-bearing output except the pre-execution file-set hash comes from one named tlrelease invocation with its producer, mapping, consumers, and predicate pinned together. Privileged run scalars are one declared argv with closed env, action-input, runner, shell, and working-directory schemas. Refuse continue-on-error and status-function bypasses as ADR-0028 specifies. Every OIDC-bearing channel job uses the protected release environment and minimum permissions.

Every pure total workflow-policy or distribution-effect decision whose silent false negative could admit publication receives a characterization theorem and same-change pinnedReleaseVerdictTheorems entry. The policy registry construction task owns list parity; this task owns authority-flow and invocation grammar, workflow wiring, and cutover.

Use the canonical release-tool handoff prefix from ADR-0028: download, canonical one-file set-hash comparison, /usr/bin/false mismatch guard, /bin/chmod, and the first tlrelease invocation. Every real consumer and the capability-free rehearsal consumer instantiate it. Keep releaseToolDigest raw until its atomic removal; never compare releaseToolFileSetHash with a raw digest. Mutation fixtures cover inherited permissions, secret-only and authority-output jobs, direct expressions, script-bearing actions, environment drift, status bypass, producer/mapping drift, prefix truncation, insertion, reorder, and consumer omission.

GOAL: full Homebrew support with no first-party shell generator or publication program.

This is the canonical task for the first authoritative downstream manifest consumer. In the same change, widen ManifestDescription to a complete typed parse of targets, embedded build records, npm, and Homebrew sections; malformed or absent sections must fail manifest verification before any channel consumes them.

Add typed tlrelease commands for Homebrew formula rendering, validation inputs, and idempotent tap publication. Render Formula/tl.rb from the authenticated signed manifest rather than SHA256SUMS or workflow-derived target lists. Stable releases update the tap; prereleases generate and validate an artifact but do not replace the stable tap formula. Refuse to render any formula that lacks a URL for a Supported target on its running platform; dropping an unavailable target is allowed only for Best-effort. Publication may invoke git and real Homebrew as external tools, but parsing, channel policy, target selection, credential refusal, change classification, and messages belong to Lean.

Keep Formula/tl.rb because Homebrew requires its Ruby DSL. Validate generated formulae with real brew on macOS, including full, missing Best-effort, missing Supported, stable, and prerelease cases. Homebrew idempotence compares rendered formula text, not archive bytes.

DELETE on completion: scripts/gen-homebrew-formula.sh and every Homebrew decision embedded in policy scripts or workflow shell. Workflow steps become direct tlrelease invocations plus pinned actions. This task absorbs the former manifest-authority task.

For every new pure total Homebrew acceptance or publication decision whose silent false negative could admit an incomplete or wrong formula or update, add a characterization theorem about the function the command calls and pin it in pinnedReleaseVerdictTheorems in the same change.

GOAL: full npm support with no first-party shell staging, package bootstrap, planning, comparison, or publication program. npm/tl/bin/tl remains as the single npm runtime adapter.

After the full typed manifest reader lands, add tlrelease npm commands that stage all five packages around signed release assets, validate the staged host binary and release identity, construct package manifests and optionalDependencies from manifest targets, plan and perform the 0.0.0 bootstrap, classify registry state as absent, identical, or conflict, select latest versus next, and publish missing packages in resumable order with the launcher package last.

Lean owns file-type and executable-mode comparison; registry JSON parsing; dist-tag policy; immutable-version conflict refusal; package selection; publication order; and all messages. A staged symbolic link is refused: npm's served tree excludes or normalizes symlinks, so no symlink equality is accepted unless a future npm-native oracle first proves one published representation that can be compared unambiguously. Invoke pinned npm only as the channel-native external tool. No Python is introduced.

Keep npm/tl/bin/tl as a narrowly scoped POSIX-shell dispatcher. npm exposes this fixed bin path while platform-specific native packages arrive as exact-version optional dependencies, so the launcher selects the installed target, diagnoses unsupported or damaged installations, and execs the compiled Lean binary. For every new pure total npm acceptance, equality, ordering, dist-tag, or publication decision whose silent false negative could admit a conflicting or incomplete package state, add a characterization theorem about the function the command calls and pin it in pinnedReleaseVerdictTheorems in the same change.

Formula/tl.rb remains Ruby because Homebrew requires its DSL.

ReleaseCore imports nothing from Tl and remains outside the product TCB and Mathlib boundary. Pure, total acceptance or verdict functions whose silent false negative could make a gate, evidence set, or publication decision read as valid receive characterization theorems. The compile-time release theorem-pin registry names every non-private release contract theorem; private proof helpers are intentionally refactorable because the pinned public statement exposes the relied-on property. Other parsers, renderers, and transformations remain comprehensively tested unless a relied-on invariant becomes a formal claim.

The authenticated signed release manifest is the authoritative downstream channel description. The four plan surfaces have typed effects: GitHub Release, npm, and Homebrew are publication channels; the installer is a repository-served adapter with presence, documentation, and suite obligations but no publish job. Homebrew establishes the first full typed reader; npm consumes the same representation. Both channels are complete, fail-closed projections of the signed GitHub Release. npm equality includes regular bytes and executable modes and refuses staged symlinks that npm cannot represent comparably.

Workflow enforcement follows authority through effective permissions, secrets, environments, and transitive needs outputs. Privileged-job run steps launch one declared argv with no direct expression interpolation; authority-output producers are named typed steps, while raw build bytes are governed by authenticated evidence and the manifest. Pinned actions have closed input schemas, and runner/container identity, shell, working directory, and process-control environment are pinned. The repository-built release tool is handed off with the distinctly named releaseToolFileSetHash, produced by an unprivileged runner step and compared between pinned producer and consumer patterns that each match exactly one file before executable mode and every execution. It proves same-run transport equality, not a raw digest or provenance; releaseToolDigest keeps its SHA-256 meaning until atomic removal. Privileged job conditions and later steps cannot override prior failure with status functions.

The GitHub-only dependency budget is enforced by typed external-tool declarations, comprehensive public-command tests, an exact three-program shell allowlist, and a pinned inner Linux environment without Python, Ruby, Homebrew, Node, or npm. All three retained adapter suites run there; the exact post-pack npm launcher uses a planted installed tree, injected platform/libc observations, and an exec stub. The actual-Darwin residual is therefore narrowed by reachability to unobserved macOS-only install.sh behavior: verifier digest-tool fallback and npm platform selection are both executed under Linux injection. It stays explicit. Per-adapter fixture PATH isolation remains test machinery, while the repository-wide shell lexer and runtime-shim campaign are deleted.

Cold-runner measurement optimizes the chosen design; it does not decide whether shell policy remains.

Define the Lean-side model and fault-injection seam required by ADR-0028 before the native writer is accepted. This task owns the sealed non-empty representation of validated relative path components and the boundary checks that reject absolute, empty, dot, dot-dot, and embedded-NUL components. It also owns the typed mechanism observations: WriteOutcome is either committed SyncStrength DirectorySync or failedBeforeCommit primaryError CleanupDisposition; SyncStrength distinguishes fullBarrier from ordinaryFsync, DirectorySync distinguishes synced from unsynced with a structured error, and cleanup distinguishes not-created, removed, and retained with cleanup error. Release policy accepts ordinary fsync because it requires atomic visibility inside the live run, not power-loss survival after the run dies. Product tl_sys_sync policy remains separate.

Provide the fault-injection seam and phase matrix for empty and invalid components, intermediate symlink and regular file, base ownership, permissions, occupied regular and symlink staging paths, ordinary nested output, short and zero writes, EINTR, file sync, close, rename, post-rename directory sync, and cleanup. Pin destination and staging bytes and the typed outcome for every phase. Operation and errno are structured; add a permanent drift row refusing formatted errno classification under release/.

This task does not implement the C writer, add --output-dir to commands, change workflow invocations, or build the extern, linker-input, and native-recipe registries. Those integration responsibilities belong to the capability-based writer implementation after this model lands.

It creates the predictable sibling with O_CREAT, O_EXCL, and O_NOFOLLOW in the held final directory; writes and syncs all bytes; renames within that directory; and cleans up only a sibling this invocation created.

title: Complete the release-tool artifact handoff and hosted rehearsal

description:
Before deleting the lexical and repository-wide PATH-shim migration gates, run the complete first-party GitHub-only release policy and public suites for all three retained adapters inside a pinned minimal inner Linux container launched from one ordinary outer workflow run step.

The drift guard pins the complete outer podman run argv: immutable image identity, read-only checkout mount, separate writable scratch mount, no container-engine socket, no credentials or publication capability, disabled network, and a numeric --user matching ownership of the scratch mount. These flags are authority-bearing configuration. The checkout cannot be chowned and is never used as an output capability. The inner run proves both PATH lookup failure and filesystem absence for python, python3, ruby, brew, node, and npm before trusting the clean run. Outer JavaScript actions remain outside this boundary.

Define and check the positive input set too: POSIX shell and declared file utilities, git, sha256sum, shellcheck, actionlint, and either the pinned Lean/Lake toolchain plus dependency cache or digest-verified handoff binaries for every compiled gate. The verifier suite uses a declared cosign stub and proves it was reached; any real-cosign row receives a pinned binary and offline trust root. A declared shasum stub executes the digest fallback and proves reachability. Nothing downloads a missing tool or refreshes trust state.

Run the exact post-pack npm launcher bytes against a planted installed tree and native exec stub, injecting uname and libc observations for every supported and refused branch. The hermetic run is evidence against accidental forbidden-runtime growth on exercised Linux paths under ADR-0028 protected-source threat model, not a sandbox against malicious admitted adapter code and not proof of unexecuted Darwin branches. Keep the narrower Darwin-host residual explicit in docs/overview.md and cover branch bodies with injected-platform public tests.

Do not preserve the custom shell lexer or repository-wide PATH-shim runner after this task is green. Per-adapter isolated-PATH fixtures remain required branch tests. Channel-native npm, Node, Ruby, and Homebrew remain in their own enabled-channel jobs.

Problem: tl why on a blocked child can show a substantial dependency tree, while why on its parent epic reports no open blockers and tells the user to check status/epic/defer. Users reasonably expect the epic query to explain what remains before completion. Current cmdWhy in Tl/Cli/Commands.lean traverses only explicit live blocking edges through State.whyFastH; parent edges are outside that relation.

Acceptance criteria:
- Explain an unfinished epic through its effectively unclosed children, recursively expanding nested epics and unresolved task dependencies. Expand unfinished children of an epic encountered as a blocker too.
- Keep typed unfinished-child and dependency relationships in the machine-readable explanation. Human output shows one task row per parent, merging duplicate targets across relationship kinds, without repetitive relationship labels; retain shared-node markers across different parents. Do not imply that dependencies control epic rollup: children determine effective completion, while blocking edges govern readiness. Preserve existing readiness, rollup and mutation semantics.
- Replace the generic empty-graph message with a concrete explanation for ready, in-progress, closed, deferred and epic states, including already-complete and cancelled epics. Define traversal stopping rules for effectively closed nodes.
- Remain total on parent, dependency and mixed cycles; handle shared descendants, multiple parents and missing endpoints according to existing merge semantics, with clear cycle/shared-reference rendering. Use indexed adjacency and memoized traversal rather than whole-state scans per node.
- Design an explicit compatible JSON extension under ADR-0008/ADR-0020. Preserve the existing blockedBy meaning; do not silently reclassify children as blocking edges. Record any necessary contract decision before changing schemas.
- Prove the new pure explanation traversal properties in the kernel, preserving the existing dependency-only why correctness claim or explicitly evolving the specification and landmarks. Relevant code: Tl/Kernel/Ready.lean, Reach.lean and ReadyFast.lean; human renderer and cmdWhy in Tl/Cli; ADR-0003, ADR-0004, ADR-0017 and ADR-0020.
- Ship shell and public CLI tests for a parent with no direct blockers whose child has a deep dependency chain, nested epics, epic blockers, shared work, cycles, closed/cancelled/deferred states, missing references, plain/Unicode/color rendering and JSON compatibility. Update user-facing help and documentation. Run repository validation gates before completion.

text:
DESIGN (in progress on perf/fold-cache). Bridge strategy: foldFast ops = joinAll (ops.map delta) [then = fold via existing fold_eq_joinAll]. Each State component is a foldl of AMap.merge / FinSet.union over the deltas; build it batched (mergeSort entries by key + adjacent group-combine, O(N log N)) and prove equal to the iterated merge via AMap.ext (find-pointwise). Combiners (IssueData.merge, FinSet.union) are comm/assoc/idem semilattices, so combine order is free — mergeSort_perm suffices, NO stability needed.

DONE (committed e201bcf, Tl/Crdt/MapFold.lean, green): find_foldl_merge (find of iterated merge = running optCombine of per-map find k); foldl_optCombine_perm (per-key combine is perm-invariant for comm/assoc f, via core Perm.foldl_eq').

REMAINING (~250 lines): (1) ofEntries f entries := canonical build = collapse(mergeSort entries keyLe) where collapse groups adjacent equal keys combining with f; prove Sorted (uses core pairwise_mergeSort with TotalOrd.le_trans/le_total in Bool form) + find char: (ofEntries f es).find k = foldl optCombine none over (es.filter key=k).map(some snd), tied to find_foldl_merge via foldl_optCombine_perm + mergeSort_perm. (2) AMap.ext bridge: joinFast f ms = ms.foldl (merge f) empty, where ms entries flatMap'd. (3) Lift to OrSet (adds: AMap K (FinSet Stamp) comb FinSet.union; removed: FinSet comb (fun _ _=>())) and State (3 comps) via State.ext. (4) Kernel/FoldFast.lean: foldFast + foldFast_eq_fold; swap Cache.lean refold to foldFast; add a cold-fold near-linear ratio assertion to Tests/PerfTests.lean (currently cold fold is setup-only/excluded).

DONE (perf/per-issue-find, 5 commits, build green + tltest 886 + axiom-clean throughout):
- 2d31fd2 amapOfHashMap + find=getElem? bridge (HashMapView)
- 82378c0 rollup memo AMap -> Std.HashMap (kills the O(N)-per-op memo)
- 615fa1a kids via bucketBy (kills the O(E)-per-node kidsOfEdges filter)
- 34fb52f amapOfHashMap O(N^2) -> O(N log N) (mergeSort + proved strict sort)
- 836b480 internal parentEdges via hash-set presence-filter (kills the O(N*E) spec call)

effStatusAll @4000 (native, in-session machine ~1.6x faster so normalize via SHA=160ms baseline): cyclic 1590 -> 215ms; deep chain 927 -> 269ms. The titled scope (hash the memo + presence-filter parentEdges) is complete, plus the two supporting fixes (bucketed kids, O(N log N) materialize). The COMMON/cyclic case now has NO remaining O(N^2)/O(N*E) -- it is the near-linear walk + O(N log N) materialize + O(E) bucketBy. effStatusWith_eq / effStatusAll_find / readyFast_eq / isReadyFast_eq / cycle diagnostics all transferred BYTE-IDENTICAL (zero downstream re-proof).

RESIDUAL spun out (NOT a regression; pathological-only): deep-chain path.contains is O(depth)/kid -> tl-gws0rs9nc7n49kmb (HashSet path mirror + PathMirror invariant). Real trackers nest shallowly so it never bites; correctness-safe (ADR-0004/0023 tested-not-proved perf on a pathological input).

DONE (commit e7f66b8, perf/per-issue-find, build green + tltest 886): swapped the cache integrity hash from the pure-Lean SHA-256 to core ByteArray.hash (non-crypto, fast extern over raw bytes) for BOTH the decodeCache file-integrity check and the cacheValid prefix check. ckOf b := toString (ByteArray.hash b). CacheSegMeta.shaHex -> ck; JSON key "sha" -> "ck"; cacheVersion 1 -> 2. The cache carries NO crypto assumption now (was a tier-3 SHA-collision-freeness carried assumption) -- justified because the cache is a discardable rot-check and tampering is the segments' trust domain (ADR-0014). ADR-0022 amended (+ overview.md Trusted); CacheTests sign/version literals + all validity/corruption/round-trip branches re-checked.

Measured @4000: warm-read decodeCache 447->286ms; the cacheValid prefix SHA (~148ms) -> ~0. ~0.3-0.5s off the warm-read floor. SHA-256 (ADR-0018) untouched as the id-mint/import primitive. The decState half (~0.44s JSON parse) remains in tl-hkc3crt (deferred per Q2). The PREVENT guard (tl-99mnzwt0) should catch a revert to SHA via the e2e latency row.

DONE (commits 4758115 + 42c8b13, branch perf/per-issue-find; build green, 894 tltest, output byte-identical). Added ViewIndex (Tl/Cli/Project.lean): once-per-command hash/bucket copies of data/rollup/present/blocks-by-target/blocks-by-source/kids-by-parent/parents-by-child/prov, built by ViewIndex.of from the lists loadView/postView/cmdDoctor already hold (one new View.idx field + ~15 View.* row helpers). Routed every per-issue read on list/ready/stats/doctor/show + label-list through the helpers; each = its spec accessor pointwise via the PROVED kernel bridges (issueDataH_eq / isReadyFastH_eq / blockerDischargedH_eq / blocksByTarget_eq / blocksBySource_eq / getD_bucketBy / getElem?_hashAssoc_amap / contains_hashSetOf_present), so rendered output is byte-identical. Decisive in-process probe: hashed effStatus skips the effectiveStatus fallback (12s/4000 if hit) on a map hit (Option.getD @[inline] guards the default); per-row body 1516->2ms. Warm binary @4000: list 2.69->2.04 (now == show one issue, per-row gap gone), stats 3.17->2.24, doctor 2.89->2.11. Shell-tier pin: existing CliTests output unchanged + new rowAccessorAgreementTests (every helper == spec over epic/done/blocked/deferred/multi-parent/duplicate, non-empty prov). RE-MEASURE reframed the floor: warm~=cold (cache barely beats refold), the ~2.0s read floor is now decodeSegment parse 500ms + provenanceMap 506ms + decode 473ms + effStatusAll 364ms.

DONE (commits 3b6ca38 + 8b32a6d, branch perf/per-issue-find; build green, 894 tltest, output byte-identical). Two parts: (1) treeLines/treeForest emitted+path membership List.contains -> Std.HashSet (was O(N) per node => O(N^2) over the forest; O(depth) on a deep chain). Membership-only, so the cycle/diamond/shown-above markers are byte-identical (diamond/cycle/shared-root fixtures pin it). (2) canonicalParentE: cmdList tree isRoot ran it per visible issue and its maxTagOf did an O(E) tagsOf find => Theta(N*E) on the default tl list. Added ViewIndex.edgeTags (hash copy of state.edges.adds; EdgeKind now derives Hashable so Edge is Hashable), edgeTags[e]?.getD empty = tagsOf e at O(1); View.maxTag folds it identically; canonicalParentE reads candidates via the pbc bucket (O(deg)) + max tag via View.maxTag, so isRoot is O(N*deg). Output identical (unique max add-tag; canonicalParentTieTests + rowAccessorAgreementTests pin canonicalParentE == canonicalParent). Children-bucketing was already done by the tl-z2nj35hk per-row routing (v.kids reads pbk). Wall-clock at 4000 is masked (deg~1, the N*E term is ~10-20pct under the ~1.3s loadView floor), but the superlinear path is structurally eliminated; the op-count/ratio pin belongs to the perf-suite keystone tl-mbjw5qe.

DONE (commits 7a583ef + 5feeded, branch perf/per-issue-find; 898 tltest green). Two additions to Tests/PerfTests.lean: (1) perfBinaryTests -- the ADR-0023 §2 end-to-end row: warm `tl list` over a scaled repo (500 vs 2000 ops) spawned via IO.Process, ×4-op ratio (small ~131ms, big ~419ms ⇒ ~3.2×). Synthetic segment is past-dated (foreign-past folds, no skew defer); a guard row asserts ≥2000 rendered lines so a setup bug cannot pass as a fast empty read. synthOps gained a timestamp-base param. (2) Two in-process CLI per-row ratio rows (cli per-row projections; cli tree canonical-parent) that were the MISSING coverage for tl-z2nj35hk + tl-p8kqkfh -- a revert to a raw AMap.find/edge-filter turns them quadratic and the ×4-op ratio jumps. De-floor-masked warm-materialize/provenance/sync (sized reps to clear the 30ms floor). Two rows stay floor-backstopped, documented: batched rollup (effStatusAll is loop-invariant + small ⇒ the compiler hoists it out of bench, 0ms at any rep; pinned instead by the RollupFast theorems + the e2e binary row) and fast ready queue (still superlinear ~10.6×/×4ops -- coupled to tl-whp0xy1, cannot honestly un-mask until that lands). The lint child tl-pcwk6awx is separate.

RE-SCOPED after a measured attempt (2026-06-13). I built the blocks-by-source adjacency (blocksSuccAdj/blocksSuccA + a proved blocksSuccA_eq mirroring succOfAdj_kindAdj_eq, threaded through weightFast/keyOf/readyFast, readyFast_eq re-proved axiom-clean) -- exactly this task as titled. It made NO measurable difference: the perf ready row stayed ~10.6× for ×4 ops, per-call time unchanged. REVERTED (complexity without demonstrable benefit). ROOT CAUSE is elsewhere: reachStep (Ready.lean:41) = `dedup (acc ++ acc.flatMap succ)`, and dedup (Ready.lean:28) = `foldr (if x ∈ acc ...)` is O(M²) (List membership per element). So the weight closure is dominated by the dedup, not the succ edge-filter. reachFix/reachStep/dedup are SHARED spec infra (weightFast, whyFast, and the diagnostics reachFix all use them), so the real fix is a near-linear closure -- accumulate the reach set in a Std.HashSet (O(1) membership) while preserving the result so reachFix the fixpoint `next == acc` check and reachFix_eq/iterateN_of_fixed still hold (the == is order-sensitive, so either keep insertion order or change the fixpoint check + its proof). Everything built on it inherits this: why (whyFast→reachFix), weight/dep critical (weightFast→reachFix), dep cycles (onCycle/reachClosure), and dep path (blocksPath). reachFix's early-exit only helps shallow graphs (a chain saturates at depth N → no early exit). GOAL: a frontier-based reach engine — process each node's successors EXACTLY ONCE (worklist/frontier, not whole-accumulator re-scan) with a Std.HashSet visited (O(1) membership) ⇒ O(V+E). This is the deferred tl-whp0xy1 generalized to the whole cone. Children to file: (1) frontier reachStep + HashSet dedup with a reachClosure-equivalence bridge (the keystone); (2) rewire why/weight/cycles onto it via the existing _eq bridges; (3) dep path O(V+E) via a frontier BFS + parent map (subsumes tl-dh6t's true-O(V+E) goal — record parent at discovery, no predecessor search, reconstruct once). Scoping found the decisive fact the task text missed: propagatedAxioms' 'while h : cursor < pending.size' loop elaborates through Lean.Loop.forIn to an opaque whileM.impl carrying a one-step unfolding lemma and NO induction principle — nothing about the result could be proved as written, so a total reformulation is step one and is not optional. Also corrected: Tl/Kernel/Reach.lean is NOT usable precedent (wrong type, and its completeness half rests on Mathlib Finset cardinality, which Verify/ cannot import without widening ADR-0009). Design taken instead: reformulate the worklist as a fuel-structural drain returning Option — none = bound hit, refused; some = the loop actually drained. That makes the drained exit OBSERVABLE, so completeness follows by induction on an inductive Reaches derivation with no cardinality/pigeonhole argument, and Verify/ stays batteries-only. Fuel exhaustion is therefore not a carried assumption: it makes the gate FAIL, never silently pass.
