Second review proposed a different order: bounded-parallel scope replays first, deduplication second, module path-resolution caching third, and stage timings plus a wall-clock ceiling before any algorithm change. Recorded here with the reasons the task keeps deduplication first.

Parallelism and deduplication do not compose on the replay phase — after dedup there is one replay left. Parallelism's ceiling is the largest scope (tests, 24.8s), close to dedup's measured 30.4s, but it spends about three times the CPU to get there and needs the cores to exist: CI is GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest and macos-latest (4 and 3 cores), so the realistic CI factor is ~2.5x, and each in-flight Environment.replay builds a full result environment where today only one is ever live. They do compose on the load phase (31.8s, six independent olean loads), which is where bounded parallelism is a clean win and touches no trust argument.

Path-resolution caching is real but small: projectModulesIn + declarationNamesOf + replayClosure measured 144-387ms per scope, 1.5s across all six, so eliminating it entirely is under 1% of the run.

On the regression pin: prefer an op-count assertion (constants submitted to the kernel equals distinct constants across the six cones) over a wall-clock ceiling. That is exact and machine-independent, and it is what the perf prevention net epic concluded after a 30ms wall-clock floor masked a 16x quadratic. Stage timings in the output are worth having either way.

One trust-surface item the parallel option carries and the review did not mention: it changes the gate from a deterministic sequential run to a concurrent one, and diagnostic emission order becomes nondeterministic. The verdict logic proved in Verify/Proofs.lean is order-insensitive on the evidence, but the reported line order is not.

Numbers cross-check: the second review's distinct-constant count (19,108) matches exactly. Its sum of closure memberships (55,477) is 3,982 below the per-scope cone sizes measured here (15,048 + 18,904 + 10,277 + 5,017 + 5,017 + 5,196 = 59,459), and its warm sequential replay total (~61s) is well below the 100.1s measured on this machine. Re-measure before choosing an order if the gap matters to the decision.

Correction to the timings in the description and the preceding note. The compiled gate, warm, is faster than either figure recorded above: `/usr/bin/time -l lake exe tlverify` measured 89.5s real, 66.1s user, 10.4s sys, 3.17 GB maximum resident set size. The 2:51 that started this investigation (130s user) was a cold or contended run, and the 100.1s replay total in the description came from an interpreted `lake env lean --run` probe, which overstates the compiled cost. On a warm compiled run, roughly two thirds of 66s user is about 60s of replay, which is consistent with the second review's ~61s. Treat their figure as the credible one for the compiled binary and mine as an upper bound from the interpreter.

What does not change: the redundancy factor is a count, not a time. 59,459 closure memberships over 19,108 distinct constants is measured by the same code either way, and the union-replay ratio (30.4s / 100.1s = 0.30 under the interpreter) should carry over. Expected payoff is therefore roughly 60s of replay down to ~20s, so a ~90s gate becomes ~50s rather than the 1:15-1:30 estimated in the description.

The 3.17 GB peak also sharpens the concurrency argument: that is one sequential run on a 16 GB machine, and GitHub's arm64 macos-latest runner has 7 GB. Stacking replays would plausibly exceed it.

DESIGN: do NOT reimplement SHA-256 in release/. Pure-Lean SHA-256 over a release binary is not viable — Tl.Hash.Sha256 interpreted takes 17s for 4MB and the real binary is 112MB — and release/ cannot import Tl/ anyway. Shell out to sha256sum/shasum through IO.Process, capturing the exit code as a VALUE (which is what fixes the recorded 'sha256sum f | cut' pipeline-status defect). The task's own test list already expects this: it names 'digest-tool absence' as a case. Needs a bounded-spawn helper in release/ modelled on Tl/Sync/Ref.lean runBounded (timeout, both pipes drained, status as data) — gh needs the same, so build it once.

One source adaptation, and it is the 4.33.0 transparency change: backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency.types now defaults to true, so metavariable types are compared at implicit rather than default transparency. 'def FinSet (a) [TotalOrd a] := AMap a Unit' is semireducible, so AMap.find_mapVal could no longer unify its 'm : AMap K V' against a FinSet argument and the two tombstone-projection proofs in Tl/Crdt/Journal.lean failed to rewrite. Fixed at the definition with @[implicit_reducible] — the annotation the release notes prescribe for a type synonym used in type position — rather than hand-coercing at each use site. FinSet is the only type synonym of that shape in the tree, and AMap declares no instance FinSet also declares, so there is no diamond.

PINNED BEHAVIOUR (agreed): VISUAL then EDITOR, with no surprise fallback to vi. Refuse --json and a non-interactive stdin, teaching the 'tl update --description' route instead. A non-zero editor exit means no write. An unchanged buffer is a no-op. An EMPTY buffer deliberately clears the description.

TWO EDGE CASES on top of those five. (1) EDITOR/VISUAL set but not executable must refuse with the same remedy class as 'not on PATH' — never no-op and exit zero. A command that reports success for a check it could not run is the exact defect class the release port exists to remove, and this would be a fresh instance of it in the product itself. (2) The non-zero-exit rule must be evaluated BEFORE the empty-buffer rule: an editor that crashed after truncating its temp file otherwise reads as 'the user deliberately cleared the description', which is a silent data loss dressed as an intentional edit.

`tlrelease npm-selftest` pinned npm's cache and config by appending arguments at

and one that omits it fails with ENOTDIR on every platform. Checked against the
defect rather than a hand-made one: putting `packedEntries` back on a stripped
client fails the gate, and restoring it passes.
